changesets.headline: `astryx add` refuses a named pipe or a device where it writes a file, never opening it.

The AI Chat Landing template's keywords name its greeting, its suggestion cards and its composer. `astryx search` now finds it for an idea about a greeting, and `astryx build` lists it as an alternative start for more ideas that name a greeting, suggestions or a composer.

The `ai-chat` page template now gives its dead buttons and menu items a behavior: the composer's send, mention and attach buttons, the document version menu, and the document's share action now show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), and Copy copies the document to the clipboard (desktop and narrow screens). No layout or styling changes.

AlertDialog: under a finger the alert appears and leaves the way an iOS alert does. It scales down into place from 1.2 while it and the dimming fade in, on the theme's entrance timing. When it closes it fades out with the dimming, on the theme's exit timing, and a close or a reopen midway turns back from where it is. While it appears a touch does nothing, and keys and assistive technology still act. While it leaves nothing reaches it, but a toast its action raised stays live and its words are read. With reduced motion it only cross-fades. On a phone (a compact window under a coarse pointer) the width with no `width` prop goes from 400 px to 320 px in every theme; a `width` you pass still wins. With a mouse nothing changes.

`astryx theme build` warns, at its line, a typography value Core builds into something no browser uses, as `astryx experimental theme` refuses it: a font stack with a space in one `family` (Core quotes it whole), a quoted family name with a space, a role weight with no type scale, and a `weights` entry that is no heading level. Both judge a family by what Core writes, so a quoted name without a space (`'"Lato"'`) and a list without one (`'Lato,serif'`), which build as written, are taken. On the font dial, a weight number in any form CSS reads (`Inter +500`, `Inter 1e3`) after a known family, or a weight or style word before it (`700 Inter`, `bold Inter`), is that weight or style, never saved as a family of that name.

`astryx theme build` warns a typography value wherever the theme writes it (a const, a role const, a spread, an import, a value computed at run time), at the line that writes it when one does; a role weight that is no font weight (`'semi-bold'`, `'1200'`), which the browser drops; and a heading weight under a number key that is no level (`{7: '800'}`). Both the build and `astryx experimental theme` read a heading level as Core does, so `'01'` and `'1.0'` are level 1. On the font dial, a weight or style word after a name that starts with a family the editor knows (`Inter Tight Bold`) is read as a number there is: a weight where a family goes.

`astryx theme build` and `astryx experimental theme` name a typography weight given as a number (`weight: 600`) as a type mismatch: the field takes the text `'600'`. The message says Core still writes a weight from 1 to 1000, and offers the text form.

`Badge` is as wide as its label. A badge alone in a `Grid` cell or a `VStack` no longer stretches into a bar across the cell or the stack; in a crowded `HStack` it still shrinks and ends its label with an ellipsis.

The Best Practices section of `astryx component <Name>`, `astryx hook <name>` and an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` puts a `Do:` or `Don't:` label line before each run of items with the same guidance, instead of repeating a bold badge on every item; a blank line separates runs, so each run stays its own Markdown list. Every item keeps its place and its guidance; `--json` is unchanged.

Six chat example blocks (the full-featured composer, the composer drawer with progress, the message bubble with custom content and with metadata, and the message metadata footer and showcase): Copy now copies the message and says so; Retry, the thumbs, Mention, Attach and the report card show a short demo note instead of doing nothing. Other chat examples are unchanged.
Layout header and footer, card and empty state example blocks: their action buttons show a short demo note instead of doing nothing. The general Layout example blocks are not part of this change.

The CommandPaletteGroup basic block, both CommandPaletteList blocks and the DropdownMenuGroup showcase: picking an item shows a short demo note instead of doing nothing. Other command palette and dropdown menu examples are unchanged.

Five nav example blocks (TopNav showcase, centered navigation, enterprise dashboard and mega menu; SideNav with a header menu): Search, Notifications and Profile show a short demo note, and Sign in, Get started, Upgrade and the header-menu side nav's items are links. Other top and side nav examples are unchanged.

Nine example blocks (Toolbar card header, sizes and three slots; Selector and MultiSelector ghost toolbars; Selector option descriptions; Table bulk actions; TabList tabs with actions; Popover hook usage): their action buttons show a short demo note instead of doing nothing, and the three-slot toolbar's Back arrow mirrors in right-to-left. The three-slot toolbar's Back still does nothing on press; the bulk-actions Delete and Archive, and controls in other blocks (such as the toolbar-with-tabs New item), are unchanged.
`astryx build`'s block picker counts every block its doc-side word weights were fitted with as known, so those blocks no longer get the head start the picker gives blocks it has never seen.

`astryx build` ranks blocks also by single words a block's docs use that its fitted word weights do not know (such as a newer Core block's own terms), so a request that uses those words can tie to that block.

`astryx build` calls page or app shell with a refit word table and new blend numbers. The weights file stores that table once: the pick model reads the call model's tables when it carries none of its own.
The `build()` API description says a whole-page idea that would start on the app shell starts from the closest page template.

`astryx build` starts from a family's frame template when the frame holds the page the idea names. "Notification settings in a modal" now starts from the settings dialog template instead of the plain settings page; a modal that holds only a part ("a toggle in a modal on the settings page") keeps the settings page.

`astryx build` treats a frame as evidence for a page template only when the frame holds that template's kind of page. "Saved drafts in a modal with resume and delete row actions" asks for a list of drafts in a modal, not a settings page, so it no longer starts from the settings dialog; it starts from the app shell, with the parts listed in the kit.

`astryx build` no longer starts a part, a change to an existing page, or a page it would put on the app shell from a template kept off the template gallery. The theme showcase, a page of sample product screens, was taken as the app shell; those requests now start from a real shell template.

`astryx build` reads a request that opens with "add" and says where the piece goes ("add a filter row above the table") as a change to a page the builder already has, so it starts from the app shell. "Add a dashboard to the app" and "add a new dashboard" still start from a page template.

`astryx build` keeps "a side panel with an owner, a status, and a history" as one part that starts from the app shell, and reads "a list of planning jobs" as a page. Component categories now declare the page-template family whose records their components hold.

`astryx build` picks which page template to start from with a second word model, once the existing model has called a page. The page-or-shell and page-or-block calls are unchanged; only the choice among page templates changes.

The `build` API doc and the build kit's comments say that for a whole page the page-pick model chooses the start from the ranker's list and its own word tables, so the start can differ from the ranker's first template.

`astryx build` names a page template that is not ready only when the idea names it, as a reason ("`incident-console` isn't ready yet, so build started from `shell-top-nav`."); otherwise no not-ready template appears in its output, including `pages` and the "Keyword search matched" line.

`astryx build` chooses its start from ready page templates only: a template that is not ready yet, however well its words match, is no longer search's direct match for build and no longer keeps an idea on the app shell.

`astryx build` reads search as if every page template that is not ready yet were absent: search leaves such templates out of what it ranks for build, so the start, the page list, the block suggestions, the components and `matchCount` are exactly what they would be without them. A not-ready template's name typed as the idea no longer empties the kit. When the idea names a not-ready template that search matches directly, the reason still says it is not ready yet. `astryx search` still lists every template.

`astryx build` reports `start.fit` on a page-template start: the page-pick model's probability for that template among the ready page templates, from 0 to 1. At 0.4 or more the choice is clear; below it, several templates fit about as well. It is absent for a template the word tables do not list. `--verbose` text shows it too.

`astryx build` names where its start and each alternative go in the project it runs in, so the scaffold command runs as printed: the path `astryx template` names for that template from the project's layout and the template's own id (not the Core id an integration replacement stands in for): in a Next app, its App Router folder (`app/<name>` or `src/app/<name>`) or, with only the Pages Router, the page file `pages/<name>.tsx` or `src/pages/<name>.tsx`; else `src/pages/<name>`. The path is quoted when a shell would read it otherwise. In a folder with no package.json, the command keeps the `<path>` placeholder.

`astryx build` settles an exact ranker tie by whether a template is its family's base, instead of by how many hyphen-separated parts its id has: a family's base keeps its place ahead of a tied variant. Templates still tied, in the same family or not, are ordered by how strongly each one's own descriptor answers the idea, then by how typical of its family it is, then by name. A template the idea names by its whole name wins a tie. The page-pick model settles an exact tie of its final score the same way, and its rank features give equal values equal ranks, so the order of the weights file never decides.

When page templates of one family tie exactly and the ranker's pick is one the word tables do not list (such as the collapsible and comparison tables, or an integration's template), `astryx build` starts from the tied template whose own description, keywords and page components best match the idea, then the one most typical of its family, instead of the alphabetically first.

When `astryx build`'s ranker picks a template the word tables don't list, it now weighs that template against the pick model's best listed page, the same model that chooses the page everywhere else, instead of against the call model's.

A page template that is not ready yet no longer takes one of the places in the search results `astryx build` reads, so it no longer pushes a page, a block suggestion or a component out of build's kit; `matchCount` still counts it. When the idea names a not-ready template, the reason still says so even if another not-ready template ranks above it.

`astryx build`: a page template named the way code writes it (`CheckoutWizard`, `kanbanBoard`) starts that template, as its plain words do, and so does a name with two neighbouring letters swapped in a word of six or more letters (`dashbaord`). Shorter words are read as written.

A required `CheckboxInput` is no longer announced as invalid before anyone touches it. Chromium reported an unchecked required checkbox as invalid from its first render, so a screen reader said "invalid" on every required checkbox of a fresh form. The invalid state now follows `status`, as on `Switch`, and native validation still blocks a form submitted with the box unchecked.
Internal: the technical documentation template's Copy prompt button uses Core's useClipboard instead of calling the clipboard API directly. Pages look and behave the same.
Internal: the editor template sizes its sidebar with LayoutPanel's width prop instead of an inline style. Pages look the same.
Internal: the shell-nav template registers its Cmd+K and Ctrl+K shortcuts with Core's useHotkeys instead of a hand-written key listener. Pages look and behave the same.
The neutral and y2k themes that `astryx theme eject` scaffolds show Skeleton placeholders on their light page: their `--color-skeleton` takes a darker neutral stop, as the theme packages do.
When Node already uses a compile cache (`NODE_COMPILE_CACHE`), the CLI leaves it as it is and no longer makes an empty `node-compile-cache-<uid>` folder in the temp folder.

`astryx docs --list` lists every docs topic: the same list that `astryx docs` prints with no topic, in text and as `docs.list` with `--json`. It used to fail with `unknown option '--list'`, while `component --list`, `template --list` and `hook --list` each list their catalog. Every other docs flag reads with `--list` as it reads with no topic; a topic or section beside `--list` is refused with `ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `docs()` takes the same `list` option.

`astryx docs <name>` points to the right command when the name is a component, hook or template rather than a docs topic. The read still fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_TOPIC`, and its first suggestion is now the command that reads that entry, such as `astryx component Button`, `astryx hook useHotkeys` or `astryx template ai-chat`. Only an exact name counts, in any case and with or without spaces and hyphens (`docs text-input` points to `astryx component TextInput`); a hook also answers to its name without `use`. The suggestion keeps the usual `{name, reason}` shape and takes the last suggestion's place, so the list does not grow. When no docs topic shares a word with the name, it is the only suggestion, instead of the whole topic list. The check reads file names first and loads no docs for other names, so a docs miss stays fast. Docs routes and docs typos get the same suggestions as before. `doctor`'s cache row names the docs not-found hint's name summaries.

The `theme` row of the bare `astryx docs` list says what the topic is in one sentence; the theme editor's how-to lines (make or change a theme, look after each change, a denser or roomier app, one kind of part, a starter app with no app yet) are now the first sections of the `theme` topic, each shown whole where `astryx docs theme` opens.

`astryx doctor` text used to print each check as a block of `id:`, `status:`, `label:`, `message:` and `fix:` lines, with the summary counts on four lines. It now prints each check as one record: its status (`[ok]`, `[warn]`, `[fail]`, `[info]`) in a column, then its id, label, message and `fix`. A legend under the heading names each field by its `--json` key, and the summary prints its counts on one line. Every field still prints, so the answer reads the same in less space: about 10% less on a small app checked with `--built`. The JSON output does not change.

CLI errors name a run to try. An option a command does not take now names the options the command takes, and the command as meant when the option points at one of them: `component Table --format json` names `component Table --json`, `--full` names `--detail full`, `--props-only` names `--props`, and `theme --list` names `theme list`. A word the CLI has no command for names the command the words point at: a whole command passed as one word, a command's plural, an option some commands take (`list` names `component --list`), a command deeper in the tree (`verify` names `integration verify`; `eject` names `theme eject --help`, since it needs a theme), or a name another command reads (`info Text` names `component Text`); with no such command, it names near command names by Commander's own rule (at most three edits, and more than 40% of the name the same), so `info Text` names `component Text` where it used to name `init`. `doctor` given a path names `doctor --built <path>`, and several paths in the project name the folder that holds them. `upgrade --from <version> --list` names `upgrade --list` and the migration from that version, `template` with `--skeleton` or `--list` and other words names each run alone, and an option given without its value prints the command's usage with that option in it. Every named run parses, and a call that does not itself name the `experimental` group gets no experimental command in its answer. A word that names no command followed by an unknown option (`astryx describe Table --format json`) now reports `ERR_UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, as the same call without the option does, instead of `ERR_INVALID_OPTION`; every other error code, and every exit code, is unchanged.

`astryx doctor integration validate` (and so `integration check`) lists each component example that is not `kind: 'setup'` but cannot run on its own, the way a docs page or catalog card runs it as a live preview: code that does not compile, such as a top-level `return` or code that stops partway (`example_does_not_compile`); code that renders nothing (`example_renders_nothing`); a name the example never defines or imports (`example_undefined_name`); an import of code that runs only on a server, an async server component it renders, or a read of `process.env` (`example_server_only`); and an import of a relative path or of a package the package does not declare (`example_import_unresolvable`). Each is a note with its fix that fails `integration check --strict --next` now and `--strict` from the next minor release, so no build that passed before fails. An example may use without importing the components its package documents, the components and hooks Core documents, React's exports, and browser globals. `previewableExample(example, scope)` from `@astryxdesign/cli/authoring` is the same rule for a tool that shows examples as live previews: it returns the module to bundle, or why the example cannot run. `integrationExampleScope(pkg)` from `@astryxdesign/cli/api` returns the scope Doctor reads a package's examples with, as JSON, so a catalog can store it and a preview tool read each example exactly as Doctor does. `showcase_not_standalone` now reads the same packages: a Node built-in name such as `events` that only `devDependencies` installs counts as server-only, because an app that installs the package does not get it.

`astryx component`, `astryx hook` and `astryx template` now point to the right command when a name they do not find is an entry another lookup command reads, as `astryx docs` already did. One rule serves all four commands. An entry's name is its full id: a component, hook or template id, or a docs route. A name matches the typed name at one of four tiers, best first: exact (the whole name, in any case); folded (the whole name without spaces and hyphens, and a hook with or without `use`); last segment (only the last segment of a path id or docs route, exact or folded); words (the name carries every typed word). When the typed name matches another command's entry at one of the first three tiers, that command joins the suggestions by the entry's full id, such as `astryx hook useHotkeys` for `component use-hotkeys`, `astryx component Button` for `template Button`, or `astryx docs typography/font-setup` for `hook font-setup`. A better tier wins; inside a tier, a component comes before a hook, a hook before a template, and a template before a docs route; among docs routes, the route with the fewest segments comes first, then the first in tree order. The hint goes right after the command's own suggestions that match at its tier or a better one, so it is first only when none does. The list never grows: the last suggestion drops, and a hint that would come last is left out; when a command had no suggestion, the hint is the only one. Every hint names an entry the hinted command reads: a template only when `astryx template` lists it, and any route of the docs tree, namespaces included. The error code and the `{name, reason}` shape stay. Docs keeps its rule that the hint stands alone when no topic shares a word with the name, and `component` keeps its example-block message, which already names `astryx template`. Names that resolve still resolve as before, and a miss stays fast: file names and doc text say first which components, hooks, templates and docs routes can match, so only those are read.
`CodeBlock`'s and `Timestamp`'s copy buttons no longer update after they unmount: a clipboard write that finishes once the control is gone sets no state, starts no timer and announces nothing.

Copy works inside a frame that does not allow the async Clipboard API, such as a sandboxed artifact viewer or an embed. There `useClipboard`, and so the copy buttons of `CodeBlock`, `Timestamp` and Markdown heading links, copy with the browser's copy command inside the reader's click or key press, also in an open modal dialog or a hover card, without moving focus. Before, those buttons copied nothing there (`CodeBlock` and `Timestamp` showed a failed copy), and the browser logged a permissions-policy violation for each press. Where the async Clipboard API is allowed, nothing changes.

CodeBlock's run-time highlight stylesheet now sits in the `astryx-base` cascade layer, like the rest of Core's CSS. A theme's syntax colours and an app's own `--color-syntax-*` or `::highlight()` rules now win over CodeBlock's defaults in any load order, also for a CodeBlock in a portal under a root Theme.

`CodeBlock` scrolls a long line, or code past `maxHeight`, before script runs and in a page that runs none, such as a file made with `astryx experimental render`. Until now the code was cut off at the edge of the block until script measured it, and in a static page it stayed cut off. The code viewport still becomes a Tab stop only while its code overflows.

`upgrade` skips a codemod for a file that holds a backslash when the file's escapes spell none of the codemod's words, as it already did for files with no backslash. Before, any backslash anywhere in a file (a `\n` in a string, a `\d` in a regular expression) sent the file through every codemod's parse, so a scan of a typical app parsed about a quarter of its files several more times than needed. An upgrade from 0.6.8 answered 24% to 55% sooner across the apps measured; ranges that run mostly older codemods gain less, because those codemods still run on every file. Output and written files are unchanged.

`upgrade` binds jscodeshift to each parser once per codemod instead of once per file, which built a new copy of jscodeshift's helpers for every file. An upgrade over a 240-file app runs about 150 ms faster. Output does not change.

The CLI orders names the same way on every machine. Build, search, discovery and the CLI's lists (such as `astryx component --list`) broke ties with the host's locale, so a machine set to another language could pick a different template or print lists in a different order. They now use one fixed text order, and a lint rule keeps locale-dependent comparisons out of the CLI.

`astryx component <name>` no longer opens a component through one of its keywords. A keyword is a word to find a component by, not another name for it. A name that is clearly one component's keyword now gives the usual not-found error, with that component as the first suggestion. Exact names, names in another case, and file names open as before. The component doc type and the single-component authoring guide now define keywords the same way, and the guide has a section on choosing them.

`astryx component <Name>` names a family's sub-components that have their own doc on one line, with the command that reads each, instead of a heading and a "see" line per sub-component. A sub-component with its own description or props keeps its section.

`astryx component <Name>` with a name that is not a component now suggests the components of your project's integrations, not only Core's. A typo of an integration component's name (`ZorbletCrd` for `ZorbletCard`), or its name without its package's prefix, gets that component as a suggestion, matched by the same rule as a Core component: name, keywords and description. Two adjacent letters swapped in a name (`Butotn`) now count as one slip, as a one-letter typo does, and so does one slip in a name typed as words (`hover crad` or `hover-crd` for `HoverCard`): that name comes before a component that only has the words as a keyword. A component whose name is part of the typed name now comes before a component that only has one of the typed words as a keyword, from any package (`MetricCard` suggests Card, not InfoTip). Among names that hold every typed word, the one with the fewest extra words comes first (`time` lists TimeInput before Timestamp). Only a Core component still resolves by a close match, and the suggestion count rules are unchanged. `astryx component tag-list` no longer opens OverflowList: the name is also one slip from TabList, so the lookup lists OverflowList first, then TabList.

The Astryx skill the CLI writes for agents on the computer, and the Claude Code and Codex plugin skill made from it, now say to start a page with `astryx build "<what the page is for>"`, and to start anything else with `astryx search`.

The `useContainerReveal` usage block says the actions stay visible under a coarse primary pointer (a phone or tablet), not on any touch device, matching the hook's behavior on a touchscreen laptop used with a mouse.

The order detail, work item detail and component documentation page templates read correctly when they are shared as a file that runs no script. Their first paint is the narrow layout at every width, instead of a desktop side rail that squeezed the page into a narrow column on a phone; once script runs, wide screens still get the side rail. On a narrow screen the order and work item details now follow the main column instead of opening in a full-screen dialog, and the component documentation's section links stay on top as links instead of a picker.

The documentation, technical documentation, design documentation, order detail, work item detail and library page templates now list keywords in the words their users use for those pages, so `astryx search` and `astryx build` find them for more ideas. The template authoring guide now asks authors to describe each page that way.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the part data now knows the context menu (and its dividers): each part is right-clicked when a press opens nothing and it holds a layer, as one drawn in its own place is, so `how` reads what a context menu draws instead of saying it is unknown.

A pointer `ContextMenu` (the default presentation, and every Table cell menu) no longer carries the touch sheet's action list: `ContextMenu` now shares `DropdownMenu`'s sheet module, which loads the sheet only for the sheet presentation. A page with a Table that has cell actions, or with a `ContextMenu`, loads about 57 KB less JavaScript before first paint (about 20 KB gzip). A menu with `presentation="bottom-sheet"`, or `adaptive` on a compact touch screen, still loads its sheet after mount and opens it as before.

`defineTheme` names a token map that holds itself ("tokens refers to itself: the value of self holds an object it sits in …") instead of recursing until the call stack overflows, when the theme extends one with adaptations. Themes whose tokens hold no such loop build as before.

`defineTheme({extends})` refuses a base written as a plain theme object (a name and tokens, not built by `defineTheme()`) with the named "`extends` must be a theme from defineTheme()" error. Before, it merged the object's raw values, so a light/dark pair was written as `#fff,#000`. A base from `defineTheme()` or a built theme module merges as before.
Adds two English catalog messages for the Lab media player's visible time readouts (elapsed and total, and remaining time), so a locale can translate them.

The active option of a select, multi-select and typeahead list (the one the keyboard or pointer is on, named by `aria-activedescendant`) carries a `highlighted` theme state on its row target, as Item and CommandPaletteItem rows do: `selector-option-row`, `multi-selector-option`, and the typeahead's option row, which gets its own target, `typeahead-option` (with `size` and `selected`). A theme can style the highlighted option without a structural selector.

The radio's circle (RadioList, the menu radio, and every host of the shared radio indicator), its dot and its pressed layer are drawn at a 50% radius instead of the `--radius-full` pill token, so a theme that squares its pills keeps round radios. A theme that wants square radios overrides the radio component.

`Theme`'s runtime style injection hint no longer names a package or an import made up from the theme's name (`@astryxdesign/theme-canvas-editor/built`, `canvas-editorTheme`). It gives the build step, `astryx theme build` on the file that defines the theme with `--detail full`, whose printed import lines bring in the built .js and .css; a theme from an Astryx theme package ships both built.

A theme value left `undefined` in a part's style block, a color-mode block (`@light`, `@dark`), a pseudo-class block, an `onDark`/`onLight` surface or an adaptation rule's parts is now not set, and so is a component, style key or color-mode block left `undefined`, or one whose every value is, as a page token left `undefined` already was: the stylesheet writes nothing for it. In a style key or a color-mode block, the value the theme inherits for that property stays. A restated pseudo-class block still replaces the inherited one whole, even when every value in it is `undefined`: it stays, empty, and its component counts as themed. Before, the stylesheet held the text `undefined` (`padding: undefined;`), which the browser drops, and the inherited value was lost too; in an adaptation rule, `defineTheme` refused the theme. A `null` value keeps its meaning: it replaces an inherited value and is written as it is, and an adaptation rule still refuses it.

`defineTheme` treats a local token left `undefined` (in the theme or in an adaptation rule's `localTokens`) as not set, as a token, or a value in a part, surface or adaptation rule, left `undefined` already is: the theme builds and the stylesheet writes nothing for it. Before, it was refused as no CSS string, so a conditional spread or an unset environment value failed the theme. An adaptation rule that writes a local token name no theme in the lineage declares still fails with its name. `localTokens: undefined` at the root is refused by name ("localTokens is undefined: omit the field or pass an object"), as `extends: undefined` is: a root `localTokens` or `extends` left undefined is almost always a failed import.

Toast: before the surface is measured (a server render, a static page), the Toast's text side comes from the theme's own resolved inverted surface color, by the same rule the measurement uses, instead of assuming the surface is dark in light mode. This applies when the inverted surface is an opaque hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `black` or `white` value and the on-dark and on-light colors are hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `black` or `white` values; any other value (such as a translucent surface, `oklch()`, `hsl()` or another named color) still starts from the color mode until the measurement runs. A theme whose inverted surface is a light hex or `rgb()` color in light mode no longer renders a Toast with white text on a white bar until the page runs its script.

The typography docs say what Core builds, in one rule: a heading with no `family` takes the body's whole font list; with its own `family`, only its own `fallbacks`; `fallbacks` with no `family` build nothing. `TypographyConfig`, its `heading` field, `defineTheme`'s `typography`, the `fonts-and-assets` doc page and the theme template say it; the `font-setup` page says a heading with no family uses the body's and points to `fonts-and-assets` for the rest.

Controls that did nothing in six dashboard page templates now respond with a demo message that says what would happen: Reload and both View more buttons on the analytics dashboard, Export on the comparison, scorecard and funnel dashboards, Export status on the program dashboard, and View more on the portfolio dashboard.

On Linux, in a project whose integration takes the CLI's debug record, every command finishes about 11 to 17 ms sooner. The record names the locale and time zone the process's Intl uses, and asking Intl for them first loads ICU's data at the end of the run. The answer is now kept beside the kept gathers while the environment values, the Node and ICU versions and the time zone files it comes from are unchanged. Elsewhere, and on other systems, it is asked as before. The record's values do not change.

`astryx component <name>` keeps a suggested component whose keywords or synonyms are the typed name ahead of another command's hint for a near spelling, and leaves the hint out when such components fill the list (`astryx component Combobox` lists Typeahead, Selector and Tokenizer, not `astryx hook useCombobox`).

`astryx discover` names an installed integration's docs the way `astryx docs` opens them: a doc that adds sections to a topic by that topic's name, and a guide by its route. It listed each doc by the name on its file, so a doc such as a theme package's guide, which adds its sections to `theme`, printed a name `astryx docs` did not know.

`astryx discover` names the sections an installed integration adds to a doc another package owns, so a reader can open its own section straight away: the list prints the read beside the doc, `docs: theme (read: astryx docs theme install-and-apply)`, the JSON entry gains `docSections` (each name's section keys, each opening with `astryx docs <name> <key>`), and the doc's item page gains `sections` and prints the same reads.

`astryx discover` shows an installed integration's package.json `description`, as it already did for a package a source lists: on the list's Installed side and on the package page (`discover <package>`). Text shows its first sentence; `--json` carries the whole description as the entry's `description`. Terminal escape codes and control characters are removed, and a blank description is left out. Search (`discover <words>`), which already matches package descriptions, now also finds an installed package by a word in its description.

`astryx discover` with no query asks the project's discover sources for their catalogs while it reads the installed packages, instead of after. With a large integration whose source asks a remote catalog, the list came back about 0.4 seconds sooner. Output does not change.

A section an integration adds to a topic, or to a guide by its route, now stays when another integration, configured later, replaces that topic or guide: whether it showed used to depend on configured order alone. A topic read also names, at its top, the sections other packages add to it, since an added section joins the end of a topic that can be long.
The technical documentation page template's "Next steps" items wrap on a narrow screen instead of cutting off after one line, so a phone reader sees each item in full. Wide screens are unchanged.

The technical documentation page template reads correctly when it is shared as a file that runs no script. Its first paint is one column with the section links on top at every width, instead of a desktop side rail that squeezed the article into a narrow column on a phone; once script runs, wide screens still get the side rail. Copy buttons appear only once the page runs, so a static copy shows no buttons that do nothing. On a phone the section links stay on top as links instead of a picker.

The `theme` topic has a section on publishing a theme so other teams can use it (ship it in a package; another team runs `theme add <name> --package <package>`), in English, dense and Chinese, and its summary no longer calls its steps "sections", so a search for a section or a scoped section theme finds Section and MediaTheme first again.

`astryx docs <topic>` opens a page typed in another spelling of its route: spaces, hyphens, slashes, dots and underscores all separate words, and word order does not count (`docs tokens.tokens-color` opens `tokens/tokens-color`). When the typed words only name a page and no other command's entry matches, the miss suggests the pages whose title or declared keywords carry them, closest first (`docs theming` suggests the Theming topic first), keeps a route the typed words name first, and never lists more than before; a namespace's children are ordered the same way.

`docs` keeps the CLI's own docs tree between runs, while every file it was read from is unchanged. In a project where an integration can load, `docs` and its topics start about 30 to 65 ms sooner. Where none can load, `docs` keeps nothing and nothing changes. `doctor` still checks the tree's files themselves. Output does not change, except that `doctor`'s row for the per-user cache now names the docs tree among the entries it holds.

`doctor --built <path>` now reads doctor's kept checks back as `doctor` does, once the per-user cache folder exists: the CLI took the path after `--built` for a subcommand, so those runs checked the docs again every time. In a project whose integrations add docs, a warm `doctor --built` is about 200 ms faster; in a Core-only project the difference is within noise. The build itself is still checked on every run. Check results do not change; the cache row counts the kept checks.

`doctor --built` reads source files faster: it parses each file without attaching comments to syntax nodes, blanks comments in one pass, and walks a file's syntax tree for `require()` and `import()` calls only when its text can hold one. On a 240-file app the source scan takes about a third less time. Output does not change.

`astryx doctor` reads its kept docs checks back after an edit to the app's source. They run before the scans that read the app's source (its theme wiring and, in a project that names an icon set, its placeholder icons), so what they keep no longer depends on the app's files. Right after an edit, `doctor` in a project with an app finished about 230 ms sooner. Output does not change.

`astryx doctor` no longer reports a theme as wired because a theme source or a generated theme file imports it: the theme editor's settings module, a theme build's output, or a theme source that imports a package theme only to extend it. Before, an editor theme built on an installed theme package (`--like <theme>`) turned the "no theme appears wired" warning into a pass while the app rendered no theme; now only the app's own imports of a theme, or a theme it passes to `Theme`, count.

`doctor`'s theme font check now counts a family as loaded when a `family` parameter of a font service URL in the theme's font stylesheet names it. The Google Fonts import in every Astryx theme's font stylesheet does this. Before, an app set up correctly with the neutral theme got a warning it could not act on: "External font imports prevent proof for neutral: Figtree." A family that no `family` parameter names still gets that warning, as does a font service URL that names its families another way.

With no update check recorded, `astryx doctor`'s `newest-release` check no longer says the check runs once a day after a command, which is true only for a copy installed for the computer. It now says that only that copy checks, that a project's own copy changes only when the project upgrades it, and that a tool that runs its own copy chooses its release.

`astryx doctor integration <check> <package>` run in the folder of that package now says the package is the one in this folder, not one the project installs, and names `astryx integration check` for checking the package you are making. Before, it said only that the package was not installed and to install it first.

With no update check recorded, `astryx doctor`'s `newest-release` row reads "Newest release unknown: no update check recorded here. Only a copy installed for the computer checks, daily in the background after a command; a project's copy changes only when the project upgrades it; a tool running its own copy picks its release." The `gather-cache` row keeps its list of what is kept, and states the CLI's build id, the lookup commands' not-found path and the size limit in short clauses. Check ids, statuses, fields, the JSON shape and exit codes do not change.

`astryx doctor` no longer fails its private theme variables check in a Yarn Plug'n'Play project. For a built-in theme that the app installs as a package, the check now reads that package's own theme source, which is the copy the app uses, instead of the CLI's copy, whose icon import Yarn refuses to resolve.

`doctor`'s private theme variables check now loads each theme input with the Core the project installed when the CLI is installed for the computer. Before, in an app with Core and a theme package but no CLI in the project, the check failed for every theme input that imports `@astryxdesign/core`, as every Astryx theme package does. That CLI has no Core of its own: "Added theme inputs set private --_* variables directly (…: input could not be inspected …)". When the project's Core isn't installed yet, as in a fresh clone, the check now says that it did not inspect the theme inputs. Before, it failed for each input that imports `@astryxdesign/core`.

A `DropdownMenu` whose layer opens after its trigger becomes a valid anchor now takes focus as it opens, and fires `onClick` once. A menu in a native `<dialog>` that the page displays closed opens one commit after the press. The menu read that open as refused, so focus stayed on the trigger and `onClick` never fired.

A DropdownMenu sub-menu whose `label` is not a string, such as emphasized text or a translated message component, is now named correctly: a drilled-in view is named by the label alone, not by the whole row with its description; a view nested in it names its Back row "Back to" that label; and in a bottom-sheet data menu the sheet takes that label's text as its name while its level shows. Sub-menus with string labels do not change.

A kept value from an exact codec is stored as the JSON text its exactness check already read, so storing it no longer writes, parses and compares the value a second time. A run that keeps template discovery stores it about 15 ms sooner. A value that does not read back exactly is still never kept. Output does not change.

A layer's exit copy, which a touch close plays on, keeps the padding, border and colors of the element it copies. Before, the browser's popover style padded, bordered and painted it, so a surface with no padding of its own drew its content inset during the close.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "the today date in the date picker" says why nothing is written in one line (the date picker's calendar is the plain Calendar, drawn in the layer it opens, so a change there reaches every calendar) and names the line that changes every calendar's today day instead. `set` with a CSS property and no `--on`, given a value labeled with a part (`'card: #eeeeee'`), offers that value on that part.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- An element named in, of or after a part ("the checked indicator in checkboxes", "the indicator in selects", "the knob of switches", "the tabs' indicator", "the hovered item in menus in cards", "today's date in the calendar", "the highlighted option in the selector") is the part that place draws it as: the place itself by its name, a part named after it, a lexicon phrase said owner first, a part drawn inside it, or the one whose own state the words name, never the place or every element in it. "The buttons' icons" are the icon tokens on the buttons.
- An element its place has no part of its own for ("the close button of toasts", "the hovered item in the context menu", "the today date in the date picker", whose calendar the part data draws closed) writes nothing, and the answer says why.
- A state read from the part and not said ("the dot in radios") is let go when the element has none.
- "The checked and disabled checkbox" is the box in both states at once, in the part's own order; `--state isPressed+hover` on a toggle button is taken (Core marks isPressed with aria-pressed); "highlighted" names the highlighted state.
- What a line inside a part draws is each part on its element (a dropdown menu's own divider draws its separators), and a part whose paint is a line takes the divider answers: "the menu separators red" is `--color-border` on the menu's own divider, those separators only. PART_DATA_VERSION 24.
- A token a variant never reads is refused with a line that keeps the state and the mode asked.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part kept to its container ("buttons inside cards", "headings in cards", "the card title", "the button groups' dividers") is answered only with a token the part reads, set on the container, which keeps it there ("headings in cards bigger" and "the card title bigger" set the heading sizes on the card); a part's own setting would reach every one, so then nothing is written, and the answer says why.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a value question ("how thick are dividers", "how round are the cards now?") reads a token set on the part itself (or its group) before the theme's own value, so it answers what the part shows.

`astryx experimental theme editor show` draws the parts it shows open as a desktop window of the pictures' own size lays them out: a width or height media query is answered for that window, so AlertDialog's buttons sit side by side in the open states picture instead of in its phone layout.

`astryx experimental theme preview` reads each preview page once per element when it checks whether the page was changed by hand: a page whose JSX nests deep took time that doubled with each level, so `preview add` and `preview remove` were slow on the generated pages.

`astryx experimental theme preview app --theme` judges an import written as a template literal with nothing put in it (``await import(`../shared.ts`)``) as the string it holds, so a theme file outside the theme folder, a Sass file or a name the new app cannot type is refused there as it is when quoted. A query or a hash on any module the theme imports (`./x.ts?raw`, `./d.json?raw`) is refused too, since the new app's type check reads it as part of the module's name.

`astryx experimental theme preview app --theme` refuses a theme that imports a stylesheet in a language other than CSS by the same list the theme build loads (Stylus, PostCSS and SugarSS beside Sass and Less), and with a query after it (`./brand.scss?inline`), before anything is written. Before, those starters were made and the new app's type check stopped at the import. A refusal that comes after the theme's stale build was made again puts that build back, so the refused command changes nothing, as it says.

`astryx experimental theme preview app --theme` refuses a theme that imports a file only a bundler loads by a name the new app's type check has no declaration for: a CSS file with a query or a hash (`./brand.css?inline`), an upper-case extension (`./brand.CSS`), or a font file (`./brand.woff2`). Before, the new app was made and its type check stopped at that import. The declarations it reads are the new app's own (`*.css`) and the pictures Next declares. A refused command that put back a build it made first now puts back each file's and folder's times too, so a dev server or watcher sees no change.

`astryx experimental theme editor`'s pictures and contrast checks take a toast's text side by Core's own rule for the fill the toast draws: the theme's text where it reads at 3:1, else the on-color that reads better; a see-through fill is composited onto the page first, and a gradient falls back from the inverted surface, as the app does. A problem there comes with a `color` line on the toast, which set takes. A transparent part on a lightbox's dark island is measured on that island. Parts drawn open keep the custom properties their inline styles set (a dialog's maximum size, a popover's gap to its trigger), and a plain element in a doc example (the Overlay's media) draws.

The response types reference describes the change result of `astryx experimental theme editor set` and `undo` as it is: `missed` counts the misses the change leaves and `missedParts` the parts they are on, and an undo of a setting listed more than once names the other entries it removed (`alsoRemoved`).
The response types reference says `astryx experimental theme editor show` leaves `look` out when no picture was taken, as the result does, instead of returning it as null.

`astryx experimental theme editor`'s contrast checks measure a part inside Core's media surface (a button on a lightbox's dark island) as that surface draws it, in its own scheme whatever the page's mode: an untouched base ships no problem there, and a light-only color on the page's part makes none. A problem there is listed once, and its fix is a color in the surface's scheme, which reaches it; when the part lets the surface's ground through and the same text on the page needs the other color, no line is offered, so following the fixes never cycles.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `show` and `set` count the missed list as misses on parts (a part can miss two ways, its border and its shadow), and `show`'s line under the six it lists counts the rest as misses, apart from the parts whose fill or text color is only still the base's. The JSON of a change adds `missedParts`.
- The sheet, the preview and the pictures draw an auto media surface inside a part with a fill of its own (a toast with a light background) on the side the app's measurement picks, so its text reads as it does in the app.
- Text drawn in a disabled color (an inactive segment) is held to no 4.5:1 contrast, and no fix whitens it.
- `set`'s note on a border width offers the frames `show`'s missed list has: only parts that draw a box, scoped to the variants that do, and none at a width of zero.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`'s sheet, preview and pictures draw a toast's text on the side the app's own measurement picks for the fill the toast draws, by the rule the contrast checks use: light text on a dark fill, dark text on a light one, in each mode and for each type a fill is set for (an error toast's own fill read apart), so the pictures match the app and the checks.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: `--check` of an editor theme also checks its app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` and fails with `ERR_THEME_STALE`, saying why, when the copy is kept back, missing a file, gone, or not the current build. Each theme's copy follows its own build, so a later theme failing no longer leaves an earlier one's copy behind. The copy's files are not theme sources: compiling its descriptor, a copy build file or `src/astryx-themes.ts` names the theme to compile, the copy's source from a subfolder names the app root, and an `--out` into the copy folder is refused. A copy left with only its build outputs is still the editor's, a copy file that is gone is written back by the next `set`, and a folder the copy could not be made in is named. The compile help says it writes and checks the app copy.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: a successful compile of an editor theme always writes its app copy from what it just built, a hand edit of `<theme>.theme.ts` included, with the copy's font stylesheet from the fonts the theme loads now (a font package installed or removed since; a `set` that changes nothing refreshes it too). `--check` reads the copy as a checkout writes it (CRLF line endings pass), compares it only once the theme's outputs are current (a hand-edited theme output is named by the outputs check), and a stale copy keeps the documented check result: `upToDate: false`, code `ERR_THEME_STALE` and `appCopyStale` saying why. The copy's source and folder are no compile targets, an `--out` at the copy folder (any case, with or without a slash) is refused and suggests the same compile without `--out`, and a refused compile writes no copy. The help says so.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the "thick borders on everything" answer and a whole-theme `--border-width` also reach a framed control (a segmented control), the parts that draw a box only when selected (nav items, segments), on that state, and the indicator lines (a tab's underline), at the border width.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a light-only or dark-only theme's build exports its one mode beside the theme (`export const colorModes = ["light"];`), and its app copy re-exports it, so `theme add` wires the theme in that mode. Older CLIs and Core ignore the extra export.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: the app copy guard reads paths as the build does, so an `--out` written with backslashes or through a link into an editor theme's copy is refused, and a copy file named with backslashes is answered with the theme to compile. A file of yours in the copy folder, without the editor's mark, compiles like any theme source. Refusals run from a subfolder suggest the compile from the app root. The note on fonts named but not loaded follows the font stylesheet this compile writes, and the copy's font file no longer says the system has a font no package loads. A check held up by a file of yours names it and never sends you to a command that does not move it.

`astryx experimental theme`: the editor reads which theme a source defines from the export a build of it loads, so a helper theme exported beside the real one is refused before anything is written, and a name given by a const or a `//` inside a string no longer counts as damage. Font notes, the previews and the app copy load fonts for the families the theme builds, from one list. `compile` refuses an `--out` in the theme's own folder (other than its default stylesheet) before writing anything; an `--out` elsewhere says that the theme's folder and its app copy were not written or checked (`appCopySkipped`). A pointer to compile from the app root leaves off an `--out` the root cannot reach, and a family refusal from a subfolder suggests a compile that runs. Suggested commands stay bare in JSON (`astryx …`), as the text output starts them the way the project runs the CLI. The compile doc says what compiles.

`astryx experimental theme`: the editor judges a theme's source by the theme a build of it loads, its name and the theme it extends after every spread and repeated key, so a spread or a second `extends` that replaces the settings is refused, a spread const or a namespace import of the settings is accepted, and a helper theme read first is named with how to make the build read the theme. `compile` takes an `--out` as the theme's default stylesheet only when it is that same file, refusing a name that differs only in case on a case-sensitive disk and a folder form of the stylesheet before anything is written; builds a source named through a folder link under its own path; says in JSON what the app copy write did (`appCopy`, `appCopyStale`); names the Fontsource package for an editor theme's fonts. Every suggested compile passes the same checks before it is shown. Fonts follow every family the build writes, a part's own font included. A module that imports a file beside the theme keeps the app copy as it was and says why. A change of mode on a theme the app lists names `theme add`.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: a compile or `--check` of an editor theme whose source no longer imports or extends its settings, or names another theme, is refused with the same message `set` gives, so it never writes another theme's files or drops every setting. The app copy's font stylesheet imports the installed `@fontsource` package of every family the built theme uses, the theme's own source included, and compile's note on fonts named but not loaded follows it. A theme build counts the families the theme's own font stylesheet beside its source loads (the app copy's), so a build of the copy's source no longer names them as unloaded. A blank or whitespace-only `--out` is refused.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the source, descriptor and font stylesheet of a theme's app copy (`src/themes/<theme>/`) name the exact command that writes them in their first comment, `astryx experimental theme editor show <theme>`, so a missing or stale copy is fixed with that command; the built `.css`, `.js` and `.d.ts` keep the build's header.

`astryx experimental theme`: a font family name is read as CSS reads it, so an escaped name (`Gill\ Sans`, `"\5FAE\8F6F\96C5\9ED1"`) is a family, never a font file. A family the theme holds in its own property and reads with `var()` counts as a family it builds: the app copy loads its installed package and compile names it until then. `compile` gives the note `show` gives when the theme's own type tokens do not show on phones, and that note's fix for a weight is a rule for the same screens, which keeps it. The full report of an editor theme wires its app copy (`theme add`), not its editor folder.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a settings entry whose mode is written in other words (`Dark`, `night`, `Light`, `day`) is read as dark or light, and one whose source is written in other letters (`Dial`) or missing is read from the thing (a dial, a `--` token, a part property). A note says how each was read, and the next change saves it that way, so no command is blocked. An entry whose mode or source means nothing is refused with the undo that removes only that entry first, and the step back, which loses the last change, second. When a theme name is typed as a path (`./t`, `themes/t`), the `set`, `undo` and `compile` with the theme's name is checked by that command before it is offered, with every repair in the one line; an `--out` outside the working folder is dropped, and the reason says why.

The agent block and the theme docs send a denser or roomier app to the theme (`astryx experimental theme editor set <name> spacing tight`, or `roomy`), as they send colors, instead of gap and padding changes page by page.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a weight word at the end of a font family's name is part of the name (`Arial Black`, `Archivo Black`, `Segoe UI Semibold` are taken as typed) unless the whole name is no family the editor knows and the name without the word is (`Inter ExtraBold` is Inter and a weight); a weight number (`Inter 600`) is never part of a name. The Segoe UI weights Windows ships as families of their own are on the system font list.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a radio's circle (a part with a checked state, a square box and corners at 50%) is no corner. The corners dial on its group leaves it, in the build as in `show`; the dial on the radio alone is refused (it changes nothing you see) with the line that does set its shape (`set <theme> border-radius 0 --on radio-indicator --only`); `how` offers that line for "make radios square" and answers "rounder checkboxes" with the checkbox alone.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a family whose last word the editor knows as itself (`Inter Tight`) is no weight typo and is kept; a misspelled style word (`Inter Bold Itallic`) is answered as the exact words are; any weight number after a known family (`Inter 650`, `Inter 6OO`) is read as a weight; and a value holding `NaN` or `undefined` is refused at set, naming the value, never left to fail the build.

`astryx experimental theme editor set … font`: a number after a family the editor knows is read as CSS reads it, a weight from 1 to 1000 (`Inter 450.5`, `Inter 50`) and any other number no family (`Inter 1500`), never saved as a family of that name; a word with another first letter is no typo of a weight word (`Inter Night`, `Inter Right` are kept); and a font role in other letters (`--on Body`) is answered as that role, never as the app shell.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> font`: a family no package loads is named with the install line of the Fontsource package its name maps to (such as `@fontsource/press-start-2p` for Press Start 2P); once installed, the previews and the app copy load it like any font package.

`astryx experimental theme editor set … font`: a weight or style word typed with a typo after a family the editor knows (`Georgia Blod`, `Inter semibld`, `Courier New Itallic`) is read as that word and refused with the family and weight lines and the name kept as typed, never saved as a family of that name. A typo of a font preset inside a list (`Robto, sans-serif`) is read as the preset, as it is alone.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the font dial reads every weight or style word after a family, each through the one typo limit (`Inter Bold Itallic`, `Inter Tihn`), and offers the family and headings lines for them as for the exact words. A `new` refused for its name keeps the repair of a font the font readers refuse (`--font roboto` for `--font Robto`). The note on a family near a system font with a weight word (`Arail Bold`) names lines set takes: the family, and the headings weight.

`astryx experimental theme`: a font family maps to its Fontsource package as Fontsource names it: a `<Name> Variable` family to `@fontsource-variable/<name>`, which loads it once installed, and other characters dropped (`Mrs. Sheppards` is `@fontsource/mrs-sheppards`). No package is suggested for a font a system ships on any platform (such as Microsoft YaHei or PingFang SC) or a name Fontsource cannot publish. An installed font package loads every weight the theme uses (a stylesheet per weight, as Fontsource ships them), in the app copy and the previews. The font dial takes a CSS-escaped family, as tokens do. `compile --check` names a missing output in its check result.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a color or timing function typed with commas and no spaces (`rgb(255,0,0);`, `hsl(210,50%,40%) !important`, `cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1);`) keeps its repair line: a comma is read as a number mark only outside parentheses. `font 'Inter ExtraBold'` offers `font Inter` and `headings heavy`, the rung nearest the weight in any form the weight table reads.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: settings typed where the theme goes, as a list or a pasted form (`show corners, accent`, `show corners:pill`, `'{"corners":"pill"}'`), get a look at each theme here, never a theme made of them nor "names more than one theme". `new` reads more settings typed after the name as their options, never as name words: a colon word apart from its value (`accent: red`), a dial typo (`cornres pill`), `base <theme>` as `--like`, a pasted value across words (`font=Inter, Arial`), a dial word after an option's value (`--accent red corners pill`), and a property new takes no option for (`padding 8px`), offered as a `set` after the theme is made; a setting with its value typed as the name (`new 'corners pill'`) is never the name offered. `undo` reads a value with commas typed unquoted when the theme is left out (`undo Inter, Arial`), a value then its setting (`undo t red accent`), and a scope in a spelling set reads (`--on Card`, `cards`, `--mode drak`): the line for that scope's setting leads. An option whose value names another subcommand (`editor --on show set t …`) keeps it. A mode typed with its letters in another order (`--mode kdar`) is that mode. `experimental theme compile` with no file names its usage and help.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `new` reads more of what is typed after the name as settings, never name words: the base in the key forms (`like=neutral`, `like: neutral`), a value before its dial (`red accent`), a quoted pair or list (`'accent red, corners pill'`), a dial word with no value, and a word typed after an option's value that no reading takes (`--accent red foo` keeps `--accent red`; `--corners pill padding 8px` keeps `--corners pill` and offers `set … padding 8px`). Settings typed where the name goes (`new 'accent: red'`) stay on the free name offered, and two bases in one `--like` (`neutral,stone`) give the first built-in one. `like`, the word `show` prints for the base, points to `set <theme> base` / `undo <theme> base`. The theme typed as an option (`set --theme t accent red`) gets `set t accent red`, and a line set does not read is never offered as working. A theme with a setting pasted on (`show t=accent`) and a list of values where the theme goes (`show 'Inter, Arial'`) get a look at the theme, never a new one. A whole command pasted as one word (`set 'set t accent red'`) is read as that command. An undo by a held value with a scope typed (`undo t 8px --on cards`) leads with the setting in that scope.

`astryx experimental theme editor new` reads a setting typed after the name in the pair form with its key in quotes (`'"like": "neutral"'`, `'"accent": "red"'`) or swapped (`red=accent`, `stone=like`), never as words of the name; the base word is never a value (`neutral=like` is `--like neutral`, never a gray tint). The name typed as an option (`--theme t2`, `--name t2`, `--theme=t2`) is that name, and the refusal says the option is none of new's.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: one reader takes every settings file and undo step. A null or other non-object entry gets the file refusal, never a crash, and the step back it names works. A damaged mode or base is read as meant by a change and recorded that way in the undo step, so undo works and the history is kept; `like: "none"` is no base. The folder names the theme: a missing or changed `name` in the file is the folder's. A headings value under the wrong half, an unknown half, or a half on another dial is refused with the undo that works, and a half listed twice offers `set <theme> headings <word>` lines that work. A dial listed twice by hand: set names every entry it replaces. A part in other letters or misspelt with `--only` gets the command on that part, `--only` kept. A did-you-mean follows the one typo rule (nothing for one to three letters). The theme-name rule, dashes included, is stated from one text in every refusal and in `new`'s help. `more` or `less` at a dial's last step is refused with the other way. A built-in theme that is not installed is offered with its install line first. A value saved in another form (corners in rem, a fractional text-size) leaves the build current for `compile --check`. `preview <word>` leads with a subcommand the word is a typo of, and offers a theme's pages only for a theme here.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: text of a part that sits in the app's top bar is checked over the header's background. A part with a see-through background of its own (a segmented control's track, a ghost button, a top nav item) shows the header through it, so a dark header now warns when those labels do not read on it, including the light/dark/system switch the in-app preview puts in its top bar, which looks the same in an app.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` checks every command it suggests against the question: the command must make the kind of change the words ask for (a color for a color ask, a radius for a corner ask, padding or a size for a size ask, a border width, a weight, an opacity or a shadow), move the way they say from the value there now, and reach none or 0 for a removal. A command that does not is left out, and the answer says plainly what it could not work out; a value you typed is always taken as given.

`astryx experimental theme editor how --help` lists the kinds of ask a question in plain words can be, each with examples it answers with commands (examples labeled "Asks how understands": a dial, a part's property by an amount or a value, a direction, a comparison, everything except some parts, a prohibition, one mode, a removal, several changes, a question about a value). A question it cannot answer points to that list, and `--help` is the first of its next commands.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a clause that only states a bound on a part, such as "never make buttons rounder than 12px", as a limit on the asks said with it, before or after them. The bound never becomes an ask of its own, and it never gives its part to those asks. Each answer that would build the part past the bound holds it there: it sets the part's own token after the answer's steps and says so. An answer that already keeps the part within the bound says that too.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "inline", "block", "horizontal" and "vertical" name a padding side only beside the padding they qualify ("inline padding", "padding-inline", "padding 8px vertical"), never as a word of a part's name, so "inline code padding 4px" and "block quote padding 8px" set every side of that part.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a color bound ("darker but never darker than #1e40af") holds every color an answer writes, a color dial's seed included, and a see-through tint is held by its own color with its transparency kept, never turned into the opaque bound color. A part named on, inside or in a container ("links on cards") has its token set on that container, so it changes there only; one that cannot be kept there says so instead of changing it everywhere. "Outline buttons red" gives the outline look with the main button in red, never a border on every filled button. "All text 50% transparent" and "the text half transparent" set the theme's text colors at that opacity. A part's padding is read on its own pieces only (a table's cells, never a command palette inside a dialog), for value questions and comparisons alike.

changesets.body:

`astryx experimental theme editor how` answers more consistently:

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a color word is the theme's own shade where the theme has a family for it.
