`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "2 steps more", "3 steps rounder" and "2 spacing units more" are that many steps (never a 2px or 3px value, never a "step" part); "avatars 24x24px" sets their width and height; a warmer or cooler accent moves only its hue (and says so when the accent is a gray), never the neutral grays; "headings 2-4" and "h2 to h4" change only those levels, each from its own size; variant words after except ("except transparent ones", "except success ones") keep that variant's own fill, never an overlay; a semi-transparent background is the part's own fill (never an overlay) mixed with transparent; "primary button text the same color as the secondary button text" takes that variant's own color; "bigger than 4px" goes past the bound from the value now, or says the part is already past it; and the answer check measures a part's color in the variant a command writes.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` judges a dial step by what it does, never by its own word: "more washed out colors" answers `vibrancy less` again. A typed value waives the way only for what it writes; every other value is still measured the way asked.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` checks that a write shows what the question names. A state, a mode, a typed color, a removal, an except, or the thing to change (a shadow, a border, corners, padding, an on-color) that is said in a clause but missing from every step means the clause was not read. Nothing is written, and the answer says what was read and what was not. For example, "card shadows at 30% opacity" no longer fades the whole card, and "on-accent text black" no longer changes the main text color.
changesets.body:
Other readings:

- **Excepts said first:** "except cards, …", "other than …" and "apart from …" before the ask are read as excepts.
- **Lists with articles:** "the blue, the green and the red ones" names each item.
- **Removals:** "remove X from A and Y from B" removes both.
- **Kept states:** a kept state keeps what Core draws there ("tabs blue except the selected one").
- **States on part anatomy:** a state goes to a part of the part's own anatomy only, never to sample content.
- **Examples:** a "for one, add --when" example stays in the answer's words. It is never listed as a step.
- **One-word removals:** "borderless", "un-outlined" and "shadowless" are removals.
- **"Ones" in a list:** "primary buttons and the ghost ones" names both.
- **Mode pairs:** "the accent darker in dark mode and lighter in light mode" answers both halves.
- **Keeps said as unchanged:** "…, buttons unchanged" is a keep.

`set` reads an option written after `--` with the reason and the line without `--`. `undo` reads an unquoted list of settings ("undo t accent, corners and spacing") the same as a quoted one.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` keeps excepts apart truly:
changesets.body:
- **Excepts on another axis:** an except on another axis ("buttons blue except the small ones") says it cannot be kept apart. Before, it said there was nothing to keep, and the excepted buttons changed anyway.
- **Comma-led excepts:** an except set off by commas is kept, as one with no part named is.
- **Excepts after a list:** a part-less except after a list reaches every part of the list.
- **Kept parts of a group:** a part of a group kept from a one-mode or status step is pinned in each status and mode of that step.

Other readings:

- **Mode pairs:** a mode pair is one subject wherever its part is said ("the text darker in dark mode and lighter in light mode on cards").
- **Text already at its limit:** text that is already as light or as dark as it goes says so, instead of answering "no match".
- **Heading levels:** "keep h1" is a keep.
- **Neither/nor:** "neither a border nor a shadow" reads its articles.
- **Removals:** "from menus and from tooltips" takes the thing of the item before it.
- **Lists of parts:** every ask after a list of parts reaches each part.
- **A second ask with only its value:** "rounder and red" and "bold and red" are two asks on the same part.
- **Neither/nor with parts as the subject:** "neither cards nor dialogs should have shadows" removes the shadow from each part, and "… should be rounded" squares each one.
- **Excepting an item of a list:** an except naming one item of a list leaves that item out of the change.
- **Modes said first:** "in dark mode …, in light mode darker" answers both halves.
- **Indicators:** "indicators" are the check and radio indicators.
- **"Every" in removals:** "remove every shadow" reads as "all shadows".

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` guards its answers, so a phrasing it was never taught gives a named refusal instead of a wrong write.
changesets.body:
**Guards:**

- **Direction:** an ask that makes something fainter, less visible or more see-through, or removes it, never adds or strengthens a border, outline, ring or shadow anywhere. A way asked of a line never adds one to a look Core draws without one. Each such step is left out and named.
- **Keeps:** every kept scope is held after the whole in-order sequence, and that sequence runs the except with its keeps.
  - A compound except keeps that variant in that state only.
  - An except's mode or state stays with its own clause.
  - Several excepts, each with its own mode, are each kept in that mode.
- **Questions:** a question with no clause that asks for a change never writes.
- **Unknown parts:** an unknown part is said, never read as the whole theme or given the part said before it.

**Readers the guards point to:**

- **Fainter borders:** a fainter border is its color at a lower alpha. A part that draws no border says so.
- **See-through text:** see-through text is the text colors at a lower alpha, never the page.
- **Focus rings:** a see-through focus ring is its color at a lower alpha.
- **Table row dividers:** thicker row dividers are the width token the cells read, set on the row.
- **Blur:** "blurrier" shadows have more blur, not more strength.
- **Removal lists:** the items in the middle of a removal list keep its thing.
- **Links in a place:** links in a place take the link token set on that place.
- **Outline buttons in a color:** outline buttons in a color get no fill, with that color as their border and text.
- **A held theme color:** a bound holds a theme color's dial and keeps a tint's alpha.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
changesets.body:
- "the buttons the color of the links" fills the buttons with the link color, instead of turning their text the accent color.
- A part's fainter or muted text, said with an owner ("the card's muted text") or a place, is that part's secondary text. "the card's fainter text lighter" changes how light that text is, not its transparency.
- "the row hovered and selected" means the row in both states at once; neither state is dropped.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads every shadow color through the one shared color reader, so themes that write 8-digit hex shadow colors (butter, chocolate, gothic, matcha, stone, y2k) get an answer to "make shadows darker", "make shadows lighter" and "the shadows are too strong", each color's alpha scaled in the form it was written.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more of each ask the way it is said:
changesets.body:
- **Unknown part names:** a word that names no part, in the part's place ("the zorp padding", "from the blorp"), is named in the answer, never changed for the whole theme.
- **Status excepts:** an except by status ("except error inputs") keeps that status's border on each input that draws one. An input that draws no border of its own is left without one.
- **Fainter text on a part:** a part's text made more transparent, less visible or fainter is its text color at a lower alpha, never the part's opacity. A toast's text uses the on-dark and on-light colors its surface gives it.
- **Danger badges:** "danger badge" is the badge's error variant.
- **Separators:** "separator" is the divider.
- **Keeping the focus ring:** "and keep the focus ring" is a keep.
- **Outline buttons on hover:** "outline buttons blue on hover" colors the main button's outline in that state.
- **Tokens:** "tokens square" changes the tokens.
- **Text on a part:** in "the text on primary buttons 4.5:1", the buttons hold the text; they are not the background it is measured against.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads "like" and "as" as a comparison only in comparison forms ("as round as buttons", "the same padding as cards", "rounded like buttons", "like the dialogs are"): "make components like dialogs and drawers rounder" changes those parts, and "use red as the button background" sets that value. A lighter or darker color role steps its dark half the same way from its own value, and the answer check holds colors (text and borders for contrast in dark mode) and sizes to the asked way in both modes. "A light tint of the accent" is the accent mixed with transparent, never the full accent.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more of each ask:
changesets.body:
- **Links in a container:** "links on cards", in a mode pair too, sets the token a link reads on the card, never app-wide. Before, one half of the pair changed card text instead of links.
- **Lookups:** every lookup is a command that runs.

Other readings:

- **Removals:** in "the shadow from dialogs and popovers", the items after the last "from" join it.
- **"Give neither … a thing":** "give neither the cards nor the popovers a border" removes the border from both.
- **Compound excepts:** "except the disabled secondary ones" keeps that variant in that state only.
- **An ask after an except:** "taller except the large ones and bolder" answers both asks, for every part of the ask.
- **Lists matched to a reference:** "the header and the sidebar the same color as the page" matches each item to the page.
- **An except said before its ask:** "all text except headings red" reads as one ask with its except.
- **Steps that change nothing:** a step that changes nothing is left out of an in-order sequence and named there. The rest still runs.
- **Step counts:** "2 steps rounder" stays two steps in the sequence.
- **Keeps after a comma:** "…, keep h1 and h2" is a keep.
- **Shadow excepts:** "remove every shadow except on cards" keeps the shadow tokens on the card, so elevated cards keep their shadow.
- **A color in a keep:** "keep disabled ones gray" names the look they keep, not a variant.
- **Excepts in one mode:** "except in dark mode" stays with its own clause, and "except the dialog in dark mode" leaves the dialog out in dark mode only.
- **Prohibitions of a look:** "never use rounded corners on buttons" before an ask keeps the buttons.
- **Tone words for text:** "card text dark in light mode and light in dark mode" reads dark and light as colors.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "<part> match the theme" answers with the lines `show` lists for that part under missed (what the theme's own changes should have reached on it), each checked as set checks it, and says so when nothing was missed. A color named like another part's ("grey like the dialogs", "the same grey as the page") is that part's color, read from it, and the other part is never changed. "Hard", "no blur" and "flat" shadows keep their offsets with no blur, never no shadow.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` measures more of its answer: every variant and state a touched part shows (and only the mode a one-mode theme shows), the base theme's own rules for a variant, a kept variant in every state, and a painted background whichever way it is written; the plain answer of a clause with an exception is held to the exception too. A part whose variants read colors of their own ("button text darker", "buttons lighter") gets one step per variant from its own color, in each mode. It also answers: headings smaller (each level's own size when the type dial would change weights), "the text 2px bigger", "the card border 1px thicker", sizes written "48px by 48px", heading ranges for any property ("headings 1 through 3 bolder") and an excepted level ("all headings red except h1", which keeps h1 as it is), a heading level past 6 (said), "the dialog the same color as the page" (the page's own color; the page is not changed), "no shadow and no border on dialogs" (both on that part), "0 steps more" (nothing), "everywhere except", a backdrop more see-through (a lower alpha), a dialog shadow darker, lighter or with no blur from the shadow it has, "remove the card background" (transparent), "thicker borders" from the width there now, a token pointing at another token, a dark-only theme's accent from its dark value, "rounder cards without shadows", "slightly lighter than black", and value questions about a part's font, shadow, opacity and fill, in the variant and mode they name.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` measures its answer before it gives it: each suggested command is built in memory with the theme (the same build `set` makes; nothing is written), and the values the touched parts show, in light and dark, must change the kind of thing the question asks, the way it asks (a lighter fill is lighter in both modes, while text and borders step for contrast, so in dark mode they go the other way; a removal reaches none), while parts it excepts, compares against or forbids show the same values. A command that does not is left out, and the answer says plainly why. It also reads "besides", "save for", "but keep X as they are", "X excepted" and "without changing X" as except; "as well as" as and; "compared to" and "versus" as comparisons; "don't let X get smaller" and "never round the inputs" as keeping X; "X shouldn't be so small" as an ask; "remove the padding and border" as two removals; "black on secondary buttons" as text; "less sharp" and "less thick" as their opposites; value questions about space, gap, shadow, background and font size, and a question followed by an ask; a setting pasted with a colon as its lookup; "heading text lighter"; "the focus ring lighter" as its color; and a lighter or darker accent in both modes.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` and `set` handle one-mode and scoped asks more exactly.
changesets.body:
- **Shadows per mode:** a part's shadow given for one mode keeps every layer the part shows. Their colors stay in the other mode and go transparent in this one, and the new layers' colors show in this mode only. Each mode paints exactly what it did, or what was asked. `set` still takes `--mode` only for colors.
- **Core's shadow layers:** a part whose shadow Core builds from layers of its own (a card's selection ring and elevation) keeps those layers under a theme's shadow, so a card shadow, or a shadow of none, never drops the ring.
- **One-mode removals:**
  - "remove card borders in dark mode" makes the border color transparent in dark mode.
  - "no shadows in dark mode" makes the shared shadows transparent in dark mode only.
  - A border width in one mode is refused, with the reason and the border-color line that does work.
- **Mode words:**
  - Mode words name a mode, never a direction: "darker in light mode" is darker.
  - A mode word that scopes another ask ("more colorful in dark mode") never changes the theme's modes.
- **See-through colors:** a see-through role color, such as a 10% wash, stays see-through when it gets lighter or darker. A border made lighter or darker in a named mode reads that mode's page.
- **Role words:**
  - "the accent text" is the accent text token, never the main text.
  - "labels on accent buttons" are the accent-filled variant's labels.
- **Corners by a length:** a corner step in px starts from the radius the part shows. It passes `set`, and a pill stays a pill.
- **Gradients:** a gradient of one named color uses that color.
- **Keeps and excepts:**
  - "…but keep the inputs" keeps the inputs.
  - An except list keeps every variant, state and heading level it names ("except primary and ghost buttons", "except hovered or disabled", "except h2 and h3").
- **Headings:** headings made bigger never grow the body text, and headings by a px amount move each level.
- **Comparisons with the page:**
  - "darker than the page" keeps each card variant apart.
  - "as dark as the page" takes the page's color.
- **No undo of a removal:** a removal the theme already has is never undone.
- **Swaps:** a swap of two role colors swaps each mode, and a named mode swaps only its own colors.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a motion effect apart from a speed:
changesets.body:
- **Effects:** "fade in tooltips" and "slide in dialogs" now say what the part does now, read from Core's own animations and transitions (the tooltip fades in already). Nothing is written: the editor sets how long motion takes, not which effect a part uses.
- **Speed:** "faster" and "slower" step the motion the part has (a tooltip's animation) from the time it takes now.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a negated word as what it says:
changesets.body:
- **Negated words:** "un-rounded", "non-rounded" and "unrounded" buttons are square, and "un-bold" headings are regular. "border-less" and "shadow-less" are removals, with or without the hyphen.

Other readings:

- **Comparisons:** "as round as the accent" names nothing with a shape, so it is refused with that reason.
- **Removals:** a list of any length gives each item its own "from", so every item is removed.
- **Kept sizes:** "bigger except the small ones" keeps the small size only. When a keep would take the whole change back, the answer says so instead of reporting it as done.
- **Mode pairs:** the main text gets both halves of "darker in dark mode and lighter in light mode", as do typed colors per mode.
- **Heading levels:** "every heading except h1 smaller" leaves h1's own size token out.
- **Titles:** "dialog heading text" colors the dialog's own title.
- **Neither/nor:** "neither rounded nor bordered" negates both words.
- **Fully rounded:** "fully rounded" is the roundest rung.
- **Keeps said first:** "keeping cards, …" and "keep the accent, …" said first are keeps.
- **Except answers:** an except answer names the whole ask it belongs to.
- **Mode splits:** the second half of a mode split keeps the part phrase and its state ("selected tabs red in light mode and blue in dark mode").
- **Color words:** "dark gray in light mode" is a color, not a mode.
- **Excepts in one mode:** an except holds in a one-mode answer too.
- **Ghost buttons:** a hovered or pressed ghost button steps its own wash, never the primary's fill.
- **Check marks:** "check mark" is the mark drawn inside the box, colored with its text color.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more phrasings through one shared grammar:
changesets.body:
- **Keeping a part as it is:** "keep cards as they are", "leave inputs alone" and "don't touch the dialogs" all use one keep grammar, whether they come beside an ask or alone.
- **Density words:** cramped, airy, dense and the other density words come from one table that every density reading uses.
- **A fill's color after "with":** "selected table rows tinted with the accent at low strength" gives the selected state's accent wash.

`set vibrancy` now counts a color by whether its shades change. A warm or cool gray (neutral #78716c) takes vibrancy steps. A pure gray is refused, and the message names the color and says why.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads each ask through its shared readers and holds every answer to what the theme shows.
changesets.body:
- **Fills:** a fill of one color is written as `background-color`, so Core's hover and press tint stays.
- **Keeps and excepts:** one reader takes every way of keeping something as it is, in any position, and joins them into the ask's one except list. That covers "…, but keep cards as they are", "keep the dialogs as they are and …", "…, not the primary ones" and a second keep.
  - A button group cannot be kept apart from the buttons in it, and the answer says so.
  - A removed border kept when focused keeps its whole border.
  - The shared border width is kept as the token on the part.
- **Amounts and bounds:**
  - A decimal comma is a decimal ("1,5 times").
  - An amount with a bound is held to the bound ("8px more but at most 20px").
  - "Don't make X rounder than 8px" is that bound.
- **Removals:** "the X and Y of cards" stays on the cards, and "cards, buttons or inputs" names each part.
- **Asks with no change:** a swap is done exactly or not at all. A part and an aspect alone ("card corners") write nothing.
- **Modes:** "at night" and "night mode" are dark mode. A one-mode shadow on a part moves only that mode. A part that shows no shadow at rest takes a one-mode shadow. The `--mode` refusal for a shadow now says that its color can still differ by mode, through light-dark().
- **Colors and constraints:**
  - "Never use pure white" moves only what is pure white.
  - "With readable text" pairs a label that reads on the fill in each mode.
  - Vibrancy is measured on the accent wash too.
  - A typed color wins over a color word: a typed shadow color, and a typed color for text on the accent.
  - "A lighter purple" is that hue's light shade.
- **Named dial rungs:** "make corners small", "spacing compact" and "text size large" are those rungs.
- **Comparisons and measured values:**
  - "4px less round than buttons" is answered.
  - A value Core writes from several tokens (a card's padding) is measured whole.
  - A px amount on a part starts from the radius the part is built with.
  - Variant pairs need two real variants.
- **No editor theme yet:** `how` starts from, and measures against, the theme the app shows now.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads every list through one list grammar:
changesets.body:
- **Variants and states:** a list of any part's variants or states names each item, whether it comes before the part ("blue, teal and red cards"), before "ones", with an Oxford comma, or after "when" ("orange when hovered or pressed"). A variant name in a list is never read as a color to paint.
- **Parts:** a list of parts ("buttons, cards and inputs rounder") gives each part the ask.
- **Excepts and keeps said first:** an except before the ask ("make everything except buttons rounder") and a keep said first ("without changing buttons, make everything rounder") are read as excepts of the ask. The change alone is no longer offered next to an except answer.

Other readings:

- **Parts:** A corners step on a group leaves out the members already at that end (checkboxes rounder leaves out the radios, which are fully round already). "Card titles" and "dialog titles" color their heading. A state that only a part's items take ("side nav selected items") goes to the items. "Outlined in <color>" is a border color. "Padded" is a spacing word, and "less padded" or "less roomy" is tighter. "Drop-down" reads as "dropdown".
- **Corners:** on a pill base, a kept variant keeps the base's pill.
- **Modes:** "in dark mode only" scopes the ask to dark mode, and never makes the theme dark-only.
- **Shadows:** asks how cannot measure get a true reason. A softer shadow on a part the editor has not seen drawn is refused. A one-mode card shadow change says the card draws no shadow of its own at rest.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a see-through color's alpha with the one shared color reader, so an `rgba()`, `hsla()` or `#rgba` overlay gets more transparent or more opaque as asked, and the check measures it the same way. After a removal, a noun with an adjective ("rounded corners") is an ask of its own: "no shadow and rounded corners on cards" removes the card's shadow and gives it round corners.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` answers from what the theme shows on bases with rules of their own. An except keeps what the part shows: a whole-theme corner change pins the corner token on the part (a button group keeps its square joins), each heading level or variant with its own value keeps it, and a kept hover keeps its fill under Core's tint. A one-mode theme answers only for the mode it shows and never adds a mode. A gradient takes the colors named, in order. A text-size step starts from the base's body size, a variant's own literal fill is stepped from, and "more colorful" keeps each mode's accent hue. "Darker than the page" holds the page as a bound in each mode. "Remove the card border and shadow" removes both, "no bigger than 4px" is a target, a part's own tokens and its base rules count in the measured check, lighter or darker text with a mode named is read the same way by the answer and the check, a shadow typed for one mode goes into light-dark(), a length typed with no way is never a spacing step, and a color clause after an ask ("focus outline on text inputs, pink #db2777") is that ask's color.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more questions through its shared readers:
changesets.body:
- **Lists:** a two-item list of variants or states before a single ask names each one for that ask: "primary and ghost buttons rounder", "hovered and pressed buttons orange", in an except list too. "except disabled buttons" keeps that state. An except covers the whole ask before it. A prohibition said before the ask ("never round the inputs; make everything rounder", "don't make cards rounder, make everything rounder") is read the same as one said after it.
- **One-mode shadows:**
  - A one-mode shadow on a part reads the shared shadows to their layers.
  - It refuses with the true reason when the other mode is unknown, or when nothing of the part's own is there to remove.
- **Ringed parts:** a resting shadow, or its removal, is not offered on a part that draws its hover and focus rings in its box-shadow, in either mode.
- **One-mode lines:** a line the part already draws (a border, one side of it, an outline) takes its color by mode. When `set --mode` refuses such a line, it now names working steps instead of ones that repaint the other mode.
- **Accent colors:** on a theme whose modes show a color in different hues, or that shows only dark mode, a lighter, darker, warmer or cooler accent moves each mode's colors from their own values.
- **Swaps:** swapping two role colors also swaps their text, icon, wash and label colors in every mode.
- **Corners:** comparisons read the radius each part is built with (stone's pill buttons). A button group's corners step by a px amount.
- **Gradients:** gradients named by theme colors ("from the accent to the danger color") use those colors.
- **Hyphens:** a part or phrase written with hyphens or underscores ("focus-ring", "table_row") reads the same as with spaces.
- **Other readings:**
  - A text-only part's color is its text color ("the top nav heading white").
  - "What color is the header" answers its fill.
  - "Bigger but no more than 20px" takes one step of the theme's scale, held to the bound.
  - "Everything serif except headings" keeps the headings' font.
  - "The hover tint stronger" changes the shared hover wash, not the page.
  - "The body text 1px bigger" steps the text size.

`box-shadow none` on a card now also removes Core's elevation shadow. The selection ring stays.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a second item after a removal as a removal only when it carries its own removal word or is a plain removable noun ("no shadows and borders"); a noun with a comparative or an adjective is an ask of its own: "no shadow and rounder corners on cards" removes the card's shadow and makes its corners rounder, and "no border and bigger padding on cards" gives more padding, never none; the removal stays on the part named.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part's value "equal to" (or "identical to") another part's takes that part's value, as "the same as" does, and says so when that part has none to read. "Make the text 4.5:1 against the page" moves the text until it measures that ratio against the page, which is never changed (links too); text that measures it already is kept. "Never taller than 40px" is a ceiling, like "no taller than". A color bound ("darker but not darker than #1e3a8a") holds every color the answer writes, mode by mode, or says the part is past it already; it is never read as the color asked for. A table's lines and padding are read on its cells: a border ratio sets the token they read on the table, and "how dense is the table" answers with their padding. "What is the shadow" lists the shared shadow steps.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: after a contrast ratio, the part named after "on" is what it is measured against and is never changed ("the input border 3:1 contrast on the card"). A status banner's text steps its own status's text color, as its background does. A part that reads a value from several tokens (a heading's weight, one per level) answers each value. The page is the whole theme for a dial ("the page density compact"), and its colors are its body colors, so "equal to the page background" and "as light as the page" read them. "As dark as dialogs" takes the dialog's fill. Striped table rows step the color Core paints the stripes with. "Outline buttons thicker" keeps the width change beside the outline look. A length bound on the corners dial ("never more than 8px") holds every radius the dial writes.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads every removal lead ("no", "without", "remove the", "drop", "get rid of" …) from one shared list: "without shadows and rounder corners on cards" removes the card's shadow and makes its corners rounder, never every shadow in the theme, and "remove the border and bigger padding on cards" gives the cards more padding. A typed mode word such as "constructor" is never read as a mode.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a removal in a clause from the same shared list of removal leads as its rewrites ("strip", "nix", "scrap", "without the" included): "strip shadows from cards" removes the card's shadow, "nix the shadow and rounder corners on cards" removes only the card's shadow and makes its corners rounder, and "no shadows and borders on cards" removes both, as the "without" form does.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more asks the way they are meant:
changesets.body:
- A bound limits the asks of its own kind said with it. "never rounder than 8px; make the buttons and cards rounder" holds the buttons and cards and leaves the rest of the theme alone. "the cards bolder, but never rounder than 8px" still makes the cards bold. A size bound holds each heading size it would pass, and a part already past a bound is left as it is.
- A color bound said by its color alone ("darker in dark mode, at most #000000") keeps the ask's mode. A held color keeps its own hue. A color setting past the bound in one mode is written only for the other mode.
- A contrast ratio "on muted cards" or "on the muted background" is measured against that background.
- Amounts are read as typed: "20% fainter" (80% of the border's strength), "the card background more transparent" (its fill, not the whole card), and "the text 80% opaque".
- Questions answered from what the theme reads: a status banner's background, the focus ring's width or color, and how thick dividers are.
- Typed tokens with a direction ("--color-accent and --color-error darker") move each token from its own value.
- "the page rounder" and "the page font Georgia" change the whole theme, not the page background.
- "the emphasized border", "the muted text" and similar names change that border or text token.
- "dividers thicker and red" does both.
- "radio circles red" colors the radio's circle.
- "transitions faster" and "animations 1,500 ms" change motion.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more asks as meant:
changesets.body:
- "the card text 30% fainter" lowers it by 30%.
- "twice as short", "half as tall" and "twice as tall" change each height the part reads by that amount, instead of one spacing step.
- "expanded" means the part's expanded state, and "pressed" a toggle button's pressed state (a button's press is still its active state).
- "what is the height of buttons?" and "how tall are the buttons?" are answered.
- "the button corners twice as tight" changes only the corners.
- An exact border width ("half as thick") leaves the borderless styles borderless, as "thinner" does.
- A mode with a typo that keeps its letters is read wherever a mode is named: "in drak mode", "ligth theme", "(drak)", "[dark only]".
- Typed tokens each with their own direction ("--color-accent darker and --color-error darker") work.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
changesets.body:
- "the cards rounder and the gizmo red" says there is no "gizmo" instead of painting the cards.
- "the buttons the same color as the links" uses the links' text color.
- "the dividers the card border color" uses the card's border color and leaves alone the divider color that already matches.
- "the muted text in cards fainter" fades only the cards' secondary text.
- "the table row dividers thicker and blue" changes the color and explains why the width stays.
- "never redder than #ff0000" is said to be unenforceable (only darker and lighter limits are held) instead of removing the cards' fill.
- "how round are the cards now?" reports a radius set on the cards themselves.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
changesets.body:
- A color named after another part uses that part's color in the status or variant you name: "the color of the error banner", "the same color as the success banner", "the color of the danger buttons". The other part is no longer changed, and the reference doesn't decide what changes: "cards the button color" fills the cards.
- "the buttons as round as the inputs" says they already match instead of offering a line that set refuses.
- Value questions read a base theme's own colors and any of a part's own options: "what color are error toasts?".
- "the card text 25% of its opacity", "a third fainter" and "transparent by 40%" are read as amounts on the text or border color.
- "the secondary text on cards lighter" changes the cards' secondary text.
- "them" refers to the parts named just before it.
- "remove the shadow from everything" no longer reads "remove" as a part name.
- A mode with a typo is read wherever a mode is named, including before a comma and in "(drak)".
- "the open select" uses its open state.
- "the active toggle button darker" changes the toggle in that state.
- Keeping a status or a focus ring as it is works per input type and in one mode.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
changesets.body:
- A fraction is read the way it's said, before or after the direction and in words or figures: "two thirds fainter", "fainter by a third", "1/3 fainter", "a fifth fainter", "a third more transparent". A fill made "20% more transparent" keeps 80% of its color.
- A color named after another part with its status or variant ("the error banner color", "the success badge color", "the color of the muted card", "the color of the destructive button") uses that version's color and changes the subject in full.
- A base theme's own style for a variant counts first: butter's transparent secondary button shows as transparent. A transparent fill used as a color gives the color it draws next (its outline).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
changesets.body:
- A text part colored like a filled part uses the fill it shows: "the headings the color of the danger buttons", "the links the same color as the danger buttons". A named paint like "the error inputs' border" uses that paint.
- "the transparent buttons" means the button variant drawn with no fill, not a fill to remove.
- A role the part doesn't have ("the success toasts", "the selector's primary variant") gets a "no such type/variant" answer instead of changing every one.
- "transparent by a quarter" and "a quarter more transparent" on a part keep three quarters, and "the text fainter" works theme-wide.
- The focus ring of one variant stays on that variant.
- Two exceptions joined by "and" ("except the disabled ones and the error ones") keep each one.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "make the table row dividers thicker" writes nothing and explains why. The cells draw the row line at a width Core sets per render, so any width the editor could write would also thicken the borders of the controls inside the row (checkboxes, buttons).

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a mode phrase as no way for the shadows: "make shadows darker in light mode" makes the light-mode shadows stronger. A light-only theme asked about dark mode (or a dark-only theme about light mode) is told it has only one mode, whatever form the shadow answer takes.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` scales a named mode of a shadow written as one value by giving it a light-dark() pair, so "make shadows darker in dark mode" on themes such as chocolate or gothic changes the dark shadows and keeps the light ones. A shadow answer that would look the same as now (a color already at full strength) is not offered.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads each ask through one shared reader and holds every answer to what the theme shows. A kept variant or state is pinned from the base theme's own rule (a kept hover keeps Core's tint, as a variant's fill is its background color). A color word before a part names that variant ("make blue cards rounder") or is refused when the part has none ("red buttons"). One removal-list reader takes "take away the card's border and shadow", "remove the card border, shadow and background" and "remove the dialog's shadow and the card border". "dark-mode" is "dark mode". "at most", "no more than" and "a maximum of" are limits, and a limit already met changes nothing. A button's radius is written as its corner token, so button groups keep their square joins. A one-mode shadow on a part that draws a shadow in the other mode (a card's selection ring) is refused. A part given a role color keeps a readable label in every variant. Vibrancy is measured on the accent colors the theme shows. State excepts ("except disabled", "keep disabled ones as they are") go through one state reader; an except set cannot keep, or a text size that differs by screen, is said, and the plain answer is not offered. A step aimed only at an excepted variant is left out. "Darker than the page" steps past the page in each mode; a page reference is never written. A link that reads a shared text color keeps it. "letter-spaced" is letter spacing, and "side nav section headings" is the side nav heading. A refusal's own command is offered when it does what was asked, and `--at` without a picture names a command that runs.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads mode phrases, bounds, shadow strength and prohibitions each through one shared reader, and holds every answer to the measured check: "darker … in light mode" gets darker; "weaker" shadows get softer; "at least 2px", "under 40px" and "no bigger than 12px" hold the bound from the value now; "…, in dark mode" and "light mode #eee, dark mode #222" scope each value; "but leave inputs alone", "don't touch inputs" and "keep their hover the same" keep that part or state; kept parts are checked in every variant and level; a token typed with a part stays on that part; "blue card background" is the color, not the blue variant; page gradients keep the colors named; thinner borders step down from the width now; and value questions that name a mode read that mode.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: padding side words are read with the part's name taken out, so "code block padding" and "top nav padding" set every side of that part. "Card padding bigger (or smaller) than button padding" gives a step past (or under) the button's padding, never a copy of it. A dimension pair such as "16 x 16" is a size, never an amount.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part kept from a spacing change keeps its gap, padding and height ("more compact except buttons"; its own padding shorthand is not yet held, so "bigger padding except cards" says it cannot), and one kept from a border change keeps its border width ("all borders thicker except on inputs"); whole-theme shadows move from each shared shadow's own layers, in both modes or only the one named ("make shadows darker in dark mode"); a part's own gradient and its own two-mode fill step each color; a shadow by a percent scales its colors; an example value has the kind the property takes; and the answer check holds a shadow's strength and a color's see-through to the way asked.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "the current page in pagination" (and "… of the pagination") changes pagination's current button, no longer the page background. The words before "in" or "of" name a part of what follows and its state, and "current" is the state Core paints for the page you are on.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` steps a part's text in a state, such as "make the disabled button text lighter", from each variant's own color. Each step is scoped to its variant and that state, so every variant moves the way asked. Before, one variant's color was written on all of them, and the secondary and ghost buttons moved the opposite way.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a warning, error or success banner made darker or lighter steps its own status's colors, never the info blue. "Less visible" and "half as visible" borders are fainter, by the share named. "Less blurry" shadows are sharper (blur halved), never fainter. Questions about the shadows, the text weight, the background or how strong the borders are read the theme's value and change nothing. "Make the color of the text darker" is about the text. "The danger color brighter" makes it lighter. "The text 50% more transparent" scales the theme's text colors. "The page less dense" is the spacing dial. "The h3 size 20px" sets that heading level's size.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a value question answered from a part's inner parts ("how dense is the table", read on its cells) names the change on the part that holds the value ("table-cell padding 12px") and looks that part up.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads "twice as thin", "twice as small", "twice as narrow", "twice as short" and "twice as tight" as half of now in that direction, and keeps what the words change. "Make dividers twice as thin" halves the divider's line and "the padding twice as tight" gives less room; before, the first had no answer and the second gave more room.

`astryx experimental theme`: a change no longer deletes a copy of a picture (such as `preview-before.png`): only pictures the editor recorded taking, unchanged since, are removed. Every browser the editor starts for a picture, Playwright included, runs as its own process with a temp folder of its own (removed however the run ends), one 60-second bound and the same stop; a browser that does not start keeps its real cause in the message, and Chrome is named only when there is one. A theme folder that cannot be written is a write failure naming the folder; pictures asked for but not taken are said; `preview add` finds a preview renamed by hand instead of starting a second one, through the one list of previews `see`, a change's refresh and the preview commands share; a theme the route imports from outside the project folder (a workspace app run from its own folder) is never dropped from the preview; the no-template refusal offers only pages the app can show; a page remove over a theme that does not load names the whole-preview remove; the `add --template <default page>` note says what was added; from a subfolder, the wiring's paths work from there; and the `preview remove` help says what happens to a path outside the folder.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the check of a theme's own token values judges what a build made now writes, through one path for `show`, `set`, `undo` and `compile`. A value from an import, an expression, a spread or a computed key is judged by its built value; only the value a later key keeps counts; a pair is judged as the `light-dark()` it builds. The source is read only to name the file and line that hold each value (an imported file is named, not the theme file) and for what a build erases: a second `tokens` key, and a pair with other than two values. Typography is judged by the values the build was given: a scale base with a unit (which builds `NaNrem`) is refused with the number of pixels it means, a scale with a ratio and no base is named, a family written in quotes or holding `; { } < >` is refused with the working form, and `fallbacks` is checked as part of the family list it builds. A family set through typography no longer gets the phone note.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a repair's offered value reads the whole typed value, never a subset of its words. A line may carry part of the value only when the refusal's other lines carry the rest (`Inter 600` gives the family and the weight, `italic bold` on a part gives the style and the weight); a part alone (`all` for `all 200`, `bold` for `extra bold`, `5` for `0,5`) is not offered.
changesets.body:
- A comma between digits is a decimal point (`1,5rem` is 1.5rem, `0,5` is 0.5), or before three digits after a whole number a thousands mark (`1,000` on a weight is 1000), never a split into layers.
- Several values of one kind for a property that takes one offer the first as typed, with px only when the property takes no bare number (`line-height 1.5 2` is 1.5), and never one value of a shorthand of several kinds (`transition all 200` gets `how`).
- `headings extra bold` offers heavy (800), and `text-size x-large` offers 24, the size CSS gives it.
- `more` or `less` authorizes a computed value only on a dial with a scale: a token, a part property or a dial's other name given a step gets `how`, never a stock color, weight or size.
- A saved value authorizes only a keep line for its own setting, never the setting being typed, so `base buter` no longer offers the base the theme already has.
- A light and dark pair on a part's color in a one-mode theme gives the half that theme shows, as a token does.
- The note about a second pasted declaration names its line only when `set` takes it, or the line `set` offers for it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: pictures taken with a Chrome or Chromium (no Playwright) are whole-page pictures, the same as Playwright's, through the browser's DevTools protocol, never the top 2400 pixels only. Every browser the editor starts runs under one runner: a temp folder of its own (a run with none is refused, never started on the person's own browser profile), one time bound per browser with the next browser tried when one hangs or fails (and not tried again for the next picture of the run), and a stop (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, or the terminal closing) that closes the browser's whole process group and removes its temp folder and the unfinished picture. When a later browser took the picture, the result says why an earlier one did not, with its real error. A picture file of your own (`preview.png` of any size) is never taken over: only pictures the editor recorded or stamped are. `preview add` from a workspace app's folder keeps a theme the route imports from outside it, as `preview remove` does; two starter apps from `preview app` never share a package name; refusals name commands that work when followed (each app's own folder from a workspace root, a free folder for a starter app, a page this app can show); and the note that the app does not import Core's stylesheet reads the layouts' real import statements.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: one built-value check for a theme's own token values runs before every build (`set`, `undo`, `show`, the preview) and in `compile`, so a value one refuses the other never writes. A `[light, dark]` pair on a token that is not a color is refused however the file gives it (an import, a const, a spread), naming the file and line that hold it. Typography weights are judged as the tokens they build. A private variable (`--_*`) and a key that is no token name (`color`) are refused with their line. A pair in the theme file is shown by its light and dark values in notes. `undo` of a token the theme's own source sets names that file and line.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the check of a theme's own token values judges the input its source gives `defineTheme()`, evaluated as a build evaluates the module, so a value the build would drop or Core would refuse is named before anything is written. `null` and booleans are refused as no text; a value under a computed key is judged before the build drops it; a typography weight given as a number names its field and the quoted form; and the tokens a part's blocks in `components`, `onDark`, `onLight` and adaptation rules set are judged like page-wide tokens, each named by its scope and line.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: the input reader reads numbers, labels and font lists one way on every path.
changesets.body:
- A comma between digits is a decimal point (`1,125rem` is 1.125rem, `1,250s` is 1.25s); only on a weight, whose numbers are whole hundreds, is a comma before three digits a thousands mark (`1,000`).
- Two numbers are never joined into one (`12 16px` is no 1216px); only a unit split off by a space (`16 px`) is read with its number.
- A minus sign is never read away: `-8px` for a size, a padding or a duration gets `how`, never `8px`, and `-700` on a weight is no weight 1.
- Another CSS property's declaration is no setting's value on any setting (`corners 'margin: 24px'`, `text-size 'width: 20px'`); a pasted property is read only when the setting is what it sets (`border-radius` for corners, a color property for a color dial, a property that reads the token).
- One reader for a family list on the font dial, a family token and a part's `font-family`: a weight or a size in the list, alone or after a family (`Inter, 600`, `Inter 600, sans-serif`, `Inter extra-bold`), is refused with the families and the headings weight (a weight word that is part of a family's name, as in `Arial Black, sans-serif`, stays part of it), and a quoted generic (`'sans-serif'`) is offered unquoted; a part's `font-family` reads a missing comma before a generic as the dial does.
- Values a property's grammar pairs with a slash (`aspect-ratio 16 9`, `grid-row 2 4`) are offered as the pair (`16 / 9`), never the first number.
- A mode label in any spelling (`dark mode: red`, `darkmode: red`, `mode dark: red`) is that mode's label: the offer is `--mode dark`.
- A base or mode in the settings file one slip off (`neutrl`, `light`, `lightonly`) is read as meant, as `set` reads it; one that reads as nothing is refused with the line that sets it, never dropped by an unrelated change.
- A pasted object whose entries all fail points to `how` for each entry, never `how settings`.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: a theme with both modes gets a sheet and preview that render each part as the app renders it in each mode (a Toast in dark is the app's dark Toast, no longer a blank bar), the page showing the render of the mode it is in. From a workspace root, a folder in a workspace app gets that app's own checks (its routes folder, public/, build folder, themes/, Pages Router, unrouted folders); the pointers to an app below keep every argument (`--theme`, `--template`, `--top`) and use `--path` from a project root; a theme that a workspace app holds is named there, with the command run from that app. Every pointer is one its command takes: `preview add` only where add takes the folder, a starter folder free of any file, dangling link or case twin, a `cd` that a folder starting with `-` does not break, and `editor show <theme> --png` after a stop during the pictures. Starter apps get package names that never collide. A preview moved into a folder with a space or another character no plain URL takes is updated where it is. A second Ctrl-C while the pictures stop kills the browser at once and removes its temp folder.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a mistyped part (`nmber-input`) is read as the whole part name it is a typo of, never a group one word of it names, and a did-you-mean follows the one typo limit (a name that only holds the typed word inside it is none). A boolean option written with a value (`--only=true`, `--png=false`, `--only false`) gets the same reading in set, undo, new, how and show: the option takes no value, with the command that works. A toast's text on Core's media surface reads the on-dark or on-light color, so a low one is a problem with a fix that sets it; a color given as a theme token (`var(--token)`) is measured as that token's value in each mode; and text on different parts is a problem for each part, so following one fix line no longer turns up the others as new.
`astryx experimental theme …`: starter apps, pages and pictures say and write what is true.
changesets.body:

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: repairs follow the readers `set` already uses.
changesets.body:
- A saved property name with a space or capitals (`"background color"`) is repaired by `set` in place: the line replaces the broken entry, and the theme loads again.
- A unit typed after a space joins its number for every CSS unit (`50 %`, `50 vw`, `200 ms`, `1,5 rem`), not only px, rem and em.
- A typo in `--when` (`variant:primray`, `siez:lg`) offers the same command with `--when` corrected. A saved one gets the undo, then that line, so the setting is kept.
- `undo <thing> <value>` with no `--mode` is refused when the setting is saved for one mode with another value, and names the saved value and its mode.
- `new --font 'Inter 600'` offers `--font Inter --headings semibold`, as `set` reads the same value.
- A saved entry that names its thing under `setting`, a saved entry with the setting and value the other way round, and a saved mode of `"both"` or `""` are read as `set` reads them typed, with a note, so the theme loads.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> --color-background-body <color>` no longer moves the neutral color's other surfaces. A mid-tone page such as teal used to turn cards, popovers, menus and dialogs near-black in light mode (with dark text on them), because the neutral shades followed the written page color instead of the page the base theme's surfaces were made for. The written page color is now that one color, in light-only and two-mode themes alike.
`astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- A pseudo-class after a pseudo-element that takes one is accepted: any after `::file-selector-button` and `::details-content`, `:window-inactive` after a highlight such as `::selection`, `:target-current` after `::scroll-marker`. One that does not take it is refused with what it takes.
- Only `:hover` and `:active` written in capitals are refused, the two names Core reads; `::BEFORE` or `:FOCUS` build as written.
- A part property that builds dash-first without a vendor prefix (`Color`, `BACKGROUND`, `-webkit-`) is refused, with the name in lower case.
- A tokens map spread from a defined theme's tokens no longer trips over Core's own private copies in it; another private variable it carries is named as coming with the spread, with the way out.
- A value read from another file is blamed on that file through an array element (`cs[1]`), a template (`` `${c}` ``), a choice (`B.x ? B.x : '#fff'`), a call of a global or a function of the theme file's own (`String(B.x)`), and `await import()`.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme …`: settings reach the build, and fonts load as the theme shows them.
changesets.body:
- A theme source that spreads the `defineTheme` result and replaces its `components` (`{...defineTheme(…), components: {}}`) is refused by name, as one that replaces its tokens is: a part setting would be saved and never built. Give your own components inside `defineTheme({…, components: {…}})` instead.
- Italic text (`font-style: italic`, or `italic` in a `font` shorthand) loads the installed package's italic stylesheets beside the upright ones (`400-italic.css`, a variable package's `wght-italic.css`), so the browser no longer draws a slanted copy.
- Noto Sans, Noto Serif and Noto Sans Mono are named system fonts of Android, ChromeOS and Linux, and Cantarell, Ubuntu and Ubuntu Mono system fonts of Linux, so a system font stack that names them is not told it needs a package.
- A heading weight given with no type scale is offered `editor set <theme> headings <weight>`, which changes only the heading weight. The hint no longer says to add a type scale, which would also resize all text. A weight number outside 1 to 1000 is no longer echoed as the example.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`'s pictures and its `missed` list show what the theme draws:
changesets.body:

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor show`'s line for an inverted surface lost in the page works with every Core: it gives the surface as the color it is, and turns the text of each part drawn on it that reads a token (a tooltip's) to the theme's text color.
`astryx experimental theme preview` and the starter offer lines that work and name what is in the way:

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: lines the editor offers run as offered. `undo` with a value one mode holds removes that mode's entry, and an undo of one of two settings says what each mode shows now; a theme typed second gets no line for a theme that does not exist; a dial or property name a letter off (`cornres`, `paddng`) gets its set line, with the value and scope kept; saved entries with their field names in other letters (`Thing`, `Value`) are read; a design token with a fallback (`var(--color-error, red)`) is offered as typed; and a setting typed where the theme goes (`undo accent`) gets that theme's undo, never a new theme of the setting's name.

`astryx experimental theme …`: a pasted form is read as the typed one. A var() naming a design token in other letters (`var(--Spacing-4)`) gets the line with that token, though others of its family are one letter away. A pasted entry with its setting and value in the other order (`'pill: corners'`, `'{"red":"background-color","on":"card"}'`) gets the same swapped line as the typed pair.
