`astryx experimental theme editor how` value questions read the status or state they name: "what is the border of error inputs in dark mode" gives the error border, "…of focused inputs" the focused one and "…of selected cards" the selected one, instead of the plain rule's value; "how thick is the input focus ring" gives the ring's width with how it is drawn.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a `--when` or `--state` typo, or another case, on a group (`--on inputs --when status:eror`, `--on checks --state chekced`) gets the corrected command, read against what the group's members have between them, as the same typo on one part does. A setting's name typed where the theme goes gets a command on the theme here (`show accent` offers `show t`, `set corners pill` offers `set t corners pill`, `undo corners` that no theme holds offers `show t`), never a theme of the setting's name; `undo t accent corners spacing` reads the bare words as a list; and an unknown subcommand followed by an option (`experimental theme preview path --theme t`) is named as the unknown subcommand, with the near ones.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a list value with one item misspelled, for a dial that takes each word alone (`set t headings 'blod tight'`), gets a line for each word, as each word alone does; and `undo` reads three or more bare words as a list of settings only when every word names a setting, so `undo t font Inter Tight` is a setting and its value again.
`astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- Custom properties that read each other are refused at their line: a token and a local token reading one another, and a part's own custom property reading itself.
- A pseudo-class after `::search-text` (`:current`) or `::scroll-marker-group` is accepted. A pseudo-element inside `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` or `:has()`, a pseudo-class after `::highlight()`, and `:window-inactive` after any highlight but `::selection` are refused. A pseudo-element near a known one (`::befor`) is refused as that one misspelled; one missing from the CLI's selector data and near none (`::column`, `::scroll-button()`) is noted as possibly newer than the CLI, and built.
- A misspelled vendor property (`-webkit-line-clmap`, `WebkitApperance`) is refused, with the vendor property it is near.
- A value read from another file through array or nested destructuring (`const [first] = arr`, `const {a: {b}} = cs`) is blamed on that file and line.
- A null value is warned at its line and the theme keeps working, while a boolean, NaN, an object or an array, which mean nothing in CSS, are refused. The warning says what it builds: a null property leaves the base theme's value; a null token is kept by the browser as the token's value, so most properties that read it act as if they were not set (text keeps the surrounding color, a background goes transparent) and a font family reading it falls back to the browser's default font.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: fonts Apple ships on iPhone and iPad as well as the Mac (Apple Color Emoji, Helvetica Neue, PingFang, Hiragino Sans, Avenir Next, Futura and others), and `-apple-system`, are noted as shipping only on Apple platforms (macOS, iOS and iPadOS), not only on macOS. Mac-only fonts (Monaco, Lucida Grande, Geneva, `BlinkMacSystemFont` and others) are still noted as macOS only.
changesets.body: A comma before three digits on a millisecond time (`transition-duration '1,000ms'`) is a thousands mark, as on a pixel length, so the repair is `1000ms`, not `1.000ms`. On rem, em and seconds it stays a decimal point (`1,125rem` is `1.125rem`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme …`: the settings file and pasted forms are read as typed input. A saved setting whose `on`, `when` or `state` is not text (`"when": 5`, `"on": {}`), or whose part is empty, no longer makes every command fail: it is refused as a damaged setting with an undo line that removes it. A set of headings replaces a saved headings entry whose axis names no half, so later commands work. A saved base written `None` (in any letters) is no base, and the file's own field names in other letters (`Like`, `Settings`, `Mode`) are those fields. A pasted entry's field spelled as its flag (`"--on": "card"`) is that field, and a pasted change line with the `→` arrow, a label before its colon, or a label and colon with no old value keeps the label as the mode. An empty pasted object points to the dials and the help. `undo t 'accent red'` reads the setting and its value as set does. A swapped setting and value whose setting is misspelled (`set t pill cornres`) gets the swap line.

`astryx experimental theme …`: a pasted change line whose label names a part (`background-color (card) -> red`) sets that part instead of reading the label as a mode; a label that is no part name is still read as a mode, its typo included (`(drak)` is dark).
`astryx experimental theme editor` contrast checks judge what the page draws, and every fix line fixes its problem without making another:
changesets.body:
- A fix line keeps the scope of the change it answers: after a setting with `--only`, its line carries `--only`, so following it changes the part named alone.
- The text typed in an input (its value, or its placeholder) is measured on the input's fill like any other text, with a fix line.
- Text that sits on a part whose variants draw different grounds (a heading on the app's header) is measured on each variant's ground, and its fix line names that variant, so a fix for one leaves the others readable. A new problem on another ground is named as new.
- A base theme's own text color on a part (butter's nav item) is what is measured, before a text token set on the part around it; a line that would change nothing on the page is not offered, and a problem no single line can fix (the same text on grounds that need opposite colors) shows with no line.
- `show`'s `missed` list offers only lines set takes: a part whose filled variants set cannot name is left out, never given a question.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme` starters and pictures say and write what is true:
changesets.body:
- A starter's note for a font the CLI does not know names the stylesheet of each weight the theme uses, not the package's index sheet, which loads weight 400 alone.
- `show --png --section overlays` makes, photographs and lists the open states page once.
- A starter leaves out every version-control folder (Sapling, Bazaar, Pijul, CVS, Fossil and darcs beside Git, Mercurial, Subversion and Jujutsu).
- A pipe or a folder at the pictures record is left as it is and named, and no picture is taken; the editor's writer never replaces a pipe, a device or a socket.
- A write of the same bytes a file already holds leaves the file as it is, so a refused command that puts back what it built changes nothing.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a token family follows the token it is made from. A surface the theme sets (`--color-background-surface`) now carries the fills made from it, cards, popovers and menus, the muted fill (table stripes), code blocks and skeletons, at the base theme's lightness step from it; an opaque `--color-border` carries `--color-border-emphasized`, so inputs and selectors frame like cards; and the neutral color now reaches the page (`--color-background-body`, the app shell's header and side nav) at the official theme's step, as it reaches the cards. A token the theme pins, by a setting or its own source, always keeps its value.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a line offered when the theme is left out keeps every option typed (`--on`, `--state`, `--mode`, `--only`, `--like`, `--section`), so following it changes what was asked, never the whole theme. `undo` reads the words after the thing as one value, typed unquoted as `set` takes it (`undo t padding 4px 8px --on card`). With the theme left out, `undo` reads the scope in every spelling it takes with the theme typed (`--state focusVisible`, `--on Card`, `--mode Dark`) and offers the undo on the theme that holds it. A token typed where the theme goes (`show --color-accent`) is never a theme to make. A settings file whose list is written `"Settings"` is a theme that exists to `new`, never made again; written beside `"settings"`, the two are read as one list, the editor's entry winning where both set one thing, and the change says so.

`astryx experimental theme`: an option typed before a group's real subcommand (`preview --theme t list`, `editor --mode light set t …`) is read as that: the refusal names the option and the subcommand, offers the command with the options the subcommand takes moved after it, and says which options it takes none of. An option's value is never reported as an unknown subcommand, and the line offered is the subcommand typed, never another one.
`astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- `editor show`'s `missed` list frames only what draws a box: a part with no filled box at rest in any variant (a ghost toggle button, a menu row) is borderless on purpose, and with the border width at zero nothing is missed for want of a border.
- `preview app`'s font note names only weight sheets a Fontsource package can have: a weight between two hundreds (650) is drawn from the two around it.
- `preview app` refuses a theme that imports a Sass, Less or Stylus file, which the new app does not build, naming the import, before writing anything.
- `preview app` names an entry called node_modules or a version-control folder as left out whether it is a folder, a file or a link, and the note on a link says to copy what it leads to.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: tokens of the theme's own that read each other (`--a1: var(--a2)`, `--a2: var(--a1)`) are refused at their line, as a token that reads itself is. A token in `onDark` or `onLight` is judged against what that surface sets, so a surface token that reads a token the page sets from it is accepted.

`astryx experimental theme …`: undo and pasted forms are read as typed. `undo t 'cornres pill'` names the setting the typo means, and a setting the theme does not hold gets `show`, never a step back that would remove another change. Bare words for undo that are a held setting's value (`corners pill accent`) are read as that value. A setting's name where the theme goes, in other letters or as a token (`undo Corners`, `undo --color-accent`, `show Corners`), offers the themes to look at, never a new theme of that name. Several lines pasted as one argument give one line each. An empty pasted object with a separator (`{,}`) points to the dials. A pasted label that is a part typo (`(crad)`) is read as that part and a state (`(hover)`) as the state; a label that is no mode is never dropped for a line that changes both modes. A damaged saved entry beside a clean one of the same scope gets only its undo, never a set over the clean entry.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's own state written as the part names it (`--state isPressed` on toggle-button) is saved and read back as that state. Before, the next command read the saved `isPressed` as `is-pressed`, a state the part does not have, and refused every change to the theme. A theme already holding such a state is refused with its undo and a `set` line that writes the setting in its place, so the theme loads again.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A toast's text takes its own `color` on the toast: it goes into the two colors Core's media surface gives the toast's text, on the toast alone, so the lightbox and the scrim keep theirs. A text color token on the toast is refused with that line.
- Text on a one-layer linear or radial gradient is measured on the color under the text (the gradient's middle or center), so a glossy highlight at an edge is not taken for the ground.
- `show`'s `missed` list names shape and ring too: corners the theme left at the base's size beside one it changed (a popover at the container size beside square elements), with one line that sets the size it left, and a focus ring still drawn outside each part beside square corners or a theme border, with a line that draws it inside. A line is offered only where it changes the built theme.
- The inverted-surface line in `missed` gives the inverted surface to the part alone, with its text readable on it, and a variant with a fill of its own (an error toast) keeps readable text.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> accent <color>` keeps the color you gave as the link and accent text color wherever it reads at 4.5:1 on what that text sits on, in each mode its fill is your exact color; only where it does not do links move, to the nearest shade that reads, and the result says so with the ratio. Text on the fill stays white or near-black by contrast (button and badge labels are normal-size text, which needs 4.5:1, so white on iOS blue #007aff, at 4.02:1, is not picked), and the note now names how to keep the other one exactly.
`astryx experimental theme` pictures show what a person sees once the page runs:
changesets.body:
- A calendar on the sheet shows its days: a part whose server render keeps content inert until the browser runs is drawn as the browser mounts it.
- The open states page draws a context menu (right-clicked), a submenu's flyout, a popover that holds a form, a date and time field's time list, a command palette's items and a narrow screen's navigation drawer. Its drawing asks about the pointer as a desktop's mouse does, presses the controls an opened overlay holds, and closes an open popover when it presses outside it, as a browser does.
- A states section draws each control of the sample page at rest, hovered, focused from the keyboard and pressed: the page marks each one with its state, and the render's stylesheet applies that state's rules to it.
- A nav icon gets the icon its doc suggests, and an icon-only button gets an icon, so neither draws empty or spills its name.
- A border set on the inputs lands on a date and time field's two boxes, not the row around them, so it draws once on each box.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a mode word typed with a typo that keeps its letters (`drak`, `darkk`, `ligth`) is that mode wherever a person types one, by one reader: a pasted label in a `how` question (`drak: cards #1c1c1e` changes the dark cards only) or in a `set` value (`'drak: #eeeeee'` offers the `--mode dark` line) and the `--mode` flag. A word of its own (right, tight, bark) is never read as a mode.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's own state saved in a spelling `set` reads typed (toggle-button's `is-pressed` or `ispressed` for isPressed) is read as that state, with a note, instead of being refused as damage. The next change saves the part's spelling.

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: for a setting the settings file lists twice by hand, undo accepts either value it holds (`undo t accent red` or `blue`), removes every entry, and its result names each value removed (`alsoRemoved` in `--json`); a value it does not hold is refused naming the one the build reads. `show` notes a field the settings file writes twice (`like` and `Like`), as a change does. A token name whose word is a part the editor knows (`--color-text-link`) is no longer repaired by spelling to another token (`--color-text-pink`).

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `set` with the theme left out and a value of several words (`set padding '4px 8px' --on card`, `set shadow '0 1px 2px red' --on card`) offers the set on the one theme here when set's check passes it, every option kept, never a theme named after the setting. `undo` never offers to make a theme from the word: a typo of a setting the theme holds (`undo acent`), a value it holds (`undo red`, `undo t red`), or a setting with its value in one word (`undo 'corners pill'`) gets that setting's undo, and a step back says which change it takes back; `show 'corners pill'` looks at the theme. A value with commas typed unquoted, as `set` takes it (`undo t font Inter, Arial`), is that setting's value, never a list. `new` reads a setting typed after the name (`new t2 accent red`, `corners=pill`, `corners: pill; accent: red`, a pasted JSON object) as its option, never part of the name, and a token typed for the name (`new --color-accent`) is never the name offered. An option typed before a nested group (`theme --mode dark editor set …`) goes after the command it names; an option whose value is a subcommand's name keeps it; and options with no subcommand at all (`preview --theme t`) name the subcommands that take them, never their value as a subcommand.

`astryx experimental theme editor undo <theme> <word>` with no setting named never leads with a plain step back, which can take back another change than the one typed: a value one setting holds gets that setting's undo, a value several hold gets each one's, a word nothing holds gets a look at the theme (`show`), and only `all` or `last` offers the step back.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` is written around a file of yours at another name (a note, a swap file); only a file of yours at one of the copy's names, or a link on the way to it, stops it, and then every change's result and `wiring` say the copy was not updated and why. The copy's `<theme>.fonts.css` is always there (a comment only when the theme loads no font stylesheet), so the app theme module's import of it holds when fonts or the base change; `compile` writes the whole copy, that file included. `new` refuses a name the theme commands skip (`a--b`, `b-`) and suggests the cleaned one. The package commands give true answers for an editor theme: `eject` says its source is yours already, and a path (`themes/<theme>`) is answered with the command by name.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a padding or gap amount ("50% bigger", "20% smaller", "double", "150%") is an exact value from the one the part has now (its own setting, else its rule or the token it reads, each side of an unequal padding scaled), never a CSS percent padding; and with no amount, a part with an exact padding gets a step of that padding (said to be a step), since the spacing dial does not move an exact padding.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the input cleanup follows through. Quotes are mapped only where they delimit a value (curly quotes of one kind in any shape, such as „Inter“ or ‚Inter‘, «», ‹›, full-width quotes and backticks around a font name become straight ones, and a curly quote left unpaired is the straight one it stands for), and a quoted CSS string keeps what it holds, curly quotes, no-break spaces and a `;` included; a saved value is checked the same way, and quotes around a value are named as such. An entry pasted from JSON (`"accent": "#e11d48"`, `{"accent": "#e11d48"}`) or with copy debris (a trailing comma, a stray quote or bracket, a leading `=` or `:`, a second declaration after a `;` outside quotes) is read as the value; a quoted dial value suggests that value; a dash-like character inside a token name is its hyphen; `textSize` and `text_size` are text-size. A font stack is read as families: a trailing comma is dropped, a stack wrapped in one more pair of quotes is unwrapped, and an empty family is refused. `--mode` is cleaned like a value, and a near typo keeps `--mode` in the suggestion. A saved dial value with stray spaces, quotes, other letters or a pasted `corners: pill` is offered cleaned, read by the same input cleanup as typed values; a theme folder holding only empty folders counts as empty for `new`; a mistyped theme name in set or undo (`T`, `themes/t`, `./t`) suggests the same command with the theme's name.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: an exact amount ("half", "double", "a quarter", "a third", "3 times", "25% bigger") of a part's font size, line height, letter spacing, opacity, width or border width is that factor of what the part has now, never a fixed step; "3 times bigger" is an amount, never a 3px value; "double the border width" doubles it (no double-line style, no width cap); "half as round" scales the radius there now; a quarter of a padding or gap with nothing to read is a step down, said to be a step; a group's own name ("checks") is read as that group; an amount with a state ("on hover") scales that state's value and keeps the state; a dialog's header is the dialog header, not the app's top bar (likewise a card's or a dialog's footer); and the part "everything except cards" leaves out keeps the value it has now.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: two parts joined by "and" share the ask around them, so "half the corner radius on buttons and cards on hover" gives both parts their own command with the amount and `--state hover` (before, the first lost the state and the second was dropped). "context menu" is Core's context-menu part, not the dropdown menu.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "focus ring color like the links" (or "the same as", "match") sets the focus ring's color from that part's own color token, theme-wide unless a part is named before it, instead of a ring width on that part. An amount of padding on a part with no padding to take it of says the answer is one step, not an exact amount.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "lighter" or "darker" on a part's fill starts from the fill it shows at rest (its own setting first; never a pressed overlay), uses the amount asked and keeps a see-through color see-through. `astryx experimental theme editor how` checks its answer against what the question means: a part the question only compares against ("rounder than buttons", "darker than the page") is never changed, and the answer says so; a prohibition ("don't make the cards bigger", "buttons should not be rounder") changes nothing and says what stays; a question about a value ("how much padding do buttons have", "what color is the button") answers with the value now. Comparisons write onto the first part only, with a typed offset ("4px rounder than buttons"), its variant and state, and the property the words name ("button text the same color as the card text", "input border the same color as the button background"); two parts that should match copy one value, or say they already match. "Except" keeps an exact radius change, a text size change, a variant beside a part, small and muted ones, and a state. A side border ("remove the top border"), close icons and header titles, "inputs with errors", a heading level ("red h1"), a part's own radius, text colors for two button variants, an elided second clause ("… and darker when pressed", "… and half on ghost ones") and "buttons inside cards" (the container is kept, and the answer says the part changes everywhere) are read as asked. A theme name typed in another case keeps the question.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: amounts read the way they are said. Zero, none and no set that property to 0 or none in any position ("card corners zero", "zero border", "opacity zero", "no letter spacing", "remove the top padding"), and a padding side reads its own value now. One amount reader takes "up 20%", "increase by 50%", "2/3", "two thirds", "three quarters", "twice as small", "a third again" and a lone "½" as a share of now; a bare percent radius is refused with the command that scales the radius instead. "Two steps bigger" gives two dial steps, "2 spacing units" is twice the spacing unit token, a size such as "24x16px" on padding is that exact padding, and "+4px", "-2px" or "4px more" on padding, gap, radius or text size is the value now plus or minus that length. `astryx experimental theme editor`: a setting listed twice by hand now changes the last entry, the one the build reads, so "keep pill" saves and builds pill. A damaged mode or base written in other letters or as a package name (`Dark-Only`, `Neutral`, `@astryxdesign/theme-neutral`) is fixed first by the suggestions, and a change to another setting cleans it to the value meant instead of resetting it. Names copied from the app (`tTheme`, `tTheme.ts`, `brand.theme.ts`, `themes//t`, `BrandDark`, `Brand Dark`) reach the theme they name, and `new` says when it is here already. The note after Ctrl-C says what `undo` or `new` saved, with the project's own CLI command. An undo of padding in the other form (a side or the shorthand) suggests the undo that matches what is saved.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: what is pasted is read as meant, and a repair carries the value given.
changesets.body:
- A repair never offers a stock value the input did not hold (a gray, a violet, `inter`, `system`, `1px`): a line that sets the same setting again carries the value typed or saved, cleaned, else `how` for the setting.
- A value labeled with a word that is not the setting's own name is refused with what the word means, never set with it dropped: a mode (`accent 'dark: #2563eb'` offers `--color-accent '#2563eb' --mode dark`), a state (set on a part with `--state`), a kind of screen (not set per screen), a part (`--on <part>`), a heading level (`headings 'h1: bold'` offers `font-weight 700 --on heading --when level:1`), or a word it does not read. `astryx experimental theme editor`: the input reader covers more pasted shapes, and a repair still offers only the value typed (cleaned) or a documented reading of it, never a stock value.
changesets.body:
- A label on a part's property or a type token is read like a label on a dial: `padding 'hover: 4px' --on button` offers `--state hover`, `'dark: red'` offers `--mode dark`, `'card: 4px'` offers `--on card`, and the property's own label (`background-color: red`) is the value. - An object of several settings written with single quotes or without braces gets one line per setting.
- A saved `red / blue` color offers its `light-dark()` pair; a saved vibrancy with no color to saturate offers only its undo.
- A whole font stack in one pair of quotes (`"Inter, serif"`), families split by `|`, `;` or `/`, and a comma missing before any generic family (`Inter, Georgia serif`, `georgia serif`) are offered as the list meant. `font: Inter, serif` and `fontFamily:` labels are read. `\u0020` in a family and `\x2022` in content are read as CSS reads its escapes.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: repairs work when followed. `astryx experimental theme editor`: one check for the token values a theme's own source gives, run by `show`, `set`, `undo` and `compile`, each refusing with the same message and writing nothing. `astryx experimental theme editor`: an `--on` naming several parts (`'button, text-input'`, `button/text-input`, `'button and text-input'`, or spaces) is refused with one command per part named, never a group that one word of the list names. changesets.body:
No repair on a part property offers a reset the input did not hold (`0`, `none`, `1`, `auto`, `normal`). A background with one layer too many or an empty one offers the layers typed (`url(a.png), red`), and a bare number on `background` is no longer offered as a px position. `border-radius round` offers `9999px`, `opacity half` offers `0.5`, `content Hi` offers the text quoted, `font-weight heavy` its number and `text-transform caps` uppercase; other words (`padding large`, `box-shadow soft`) point to `how`, and `2 spacing units` is no longer read as `2px`. changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: with Playwright in the project, pictures try Playwright's own browser before the system Chrome, and the advice names only a fix that can help (Playwright's browser only when it is missing); the Chrome lookup passes over a folder or a file that does not run and keeps looking on PATH; a change keeps every in-app preview of the theme in step, including one renamed by hand or whose record was lost, the same previews `see` names; `preview add --path app/<x>` in a src/app project says that a root app/ would stop the whole app in src/app/ from being served; the `preview app` error table names the project folder as the bound; and a stop that lands after a preview command printed its result no longer turns that ok into exit 130.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: every value a refusal or a saved-settings repair offers now passes one gate, and each offered line is checked as `set` checks it before it is shown. A value may come only from these sources:
changesets.body:
- What was typed, under exact readings: quotes, labels and copy debris (a trailing `;`, `!important`, a comment) taken off; the same number written another way (full-width digits, a comma decimal, an exponent, rem or pt as px, a percent); CSS color names written as words (`dark red` is `darkred`).
- A documented table: Tailwind's radius classes (`rounded-lg` is 8px), a dial's own words, a weight word, a number read as a dial's nearest rung.
- The theme's own saved values, for a keep or unlock line.
- The setting's documented fallback or other-direction step.
- The correction of a typo of what was typed: one letter off for a word of five letters or fewer, two for a longer one.

Anything else, such as a stock color, a stock shadow or easing, a reset, a default token or a nearest guess, gives `how <thing>`. A scale step (`red-500`) is no bare color.

Also:

- `font 'Inter 600'` offers the family and the weight separately.
- A Google Fonts spec (`Inter:wght@400;600`) offers its family.
- Another property's label on a part property (`padding 'margin: 8px'`) offers that property.
- `--color-danger` offers the error token, and `--color-primary` or `--color-brand` the accent token.
- A CSS property typed for the whole theme leads with its dial or token (`border-radius 8px` → `corners 8px`), never a part that was not named.
- A pasted object's nested values are read, and each of its lines is checked.
- A bare fraction on a size token gets no px guessed.
- A very long input is near nothing.
- `--state 'hover,focus-visible'` gives one line per state.
- A saved light-dark pair for one mode is refused with the half for that mode.
- A CSS-wide keyword on a token offers the undo only when the theme sets the token.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: a process that runs several editor commands (an API caller) reads the app as it is now: a font package removed since an earlier command is no longer counted as installed, and an app copy folder that was not writable and is now no longer blocks `compile --check` with the old reason. `astryx experimental theme editor`: the pictures to open are named where they are read. A change with `--png` says in its `see` line to open preview.png (the sample page) and sheet-overlays.png (every menu, tooltip, popover and list, drawn open); without `--png` it still names the pages. `show --png` says it on its first line and its last (`look`, also in the JSON), so a head or a tail of the output keeps it.

- A soft shadow beside square corners or a theme border (a popover's, a menu's, a dialog's) is listed, with a line that takes its blur away.
- A status fill (a banner's, a badge's status variants) is listed only where its dial builds a color of its own (the theme's vibrancy moved); at the base's vibrancy the dial gives the base's own color back.
- `how`'s answer for a part on that list (`how "make the tooltips match the theme"`) leads with the same line.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a color for one mode on a part is written in the part's block for that mode.
changesets.body:
- In the other mode the theme writes nothing there, so what Core and the base theme give the part in context stays as it was: the current page in Pagination, a text field's error, warning and success borders.
- A one-mode color in a state is accepted on a part that has no color of its own in that state; the other mode keeps Core's.
- A one-mode gradient goes into the part's block for that mode as its image layers (and a color layer as that mode's color), so the other mode keeps Core's own images, such as a button's hover tint.
- A one-mode background on an app shell region leaves the page background painting it in the other mode.
- A one-mode color in a state is accepted on every member of a group, and an exception kept in a state (inputs darker except when focused) keeps that state's own fill in each mode.
- The part data records a background a part inherits (`inherit`) as no paint of its own.
- The result lists each property a change writes inside a mode block, under its path (`@dark :hover`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor set`: defineTheme's motion knobs typed as a setting (`motion`, `tempo`, `character`) say the editor sets motion through the duration and ease tokens, and point to `how "faster motion"` and `how "slower motion"`, the slower first for a tempo above 1.

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: a saved twin of a setting in other letters (`accent` and `Accent`, `--color-accent` and `--Color-Accent`, `background-color` and `Background-Color` on a part) is that setting listed twice, which a set or undo of it fixes, instead of a refusal saying `Accent` is no dial. A field a saved setting writes several ways, none of them the editor's (`On` and `--on`, `thing` and `setting`), is read once from the first, with a note, and the next change writes it once. A saved field the editor does not read (`modes`) is named, with the field it is a typo of. An entry pasted in the saved form without a value (`undo t '{"thing":"padding","on":"card"}'`) is read by its thing.

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: a set of a property typed in other letters (`set t Background-Color green --on card`) is that property, so it fixes that property listed twice in the settings file, instead of a refusal that offers a swapped line back and forth. A top-level `base` in the settings file (the editor's word for it) is read as the base, with a note, instead of the theme building on no base.

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: a saved setting that writes one field two ways (`value` and `Value`, `on` and `--on`) is read the editor's way with a note naming both, and the next change writes the field once. A pasted declaration whose unquoted value went on past a space (`set t font=Inter, Arial`) is read whole, so the line offered with the theme left out works too.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a color dial made lighter or darker steps from the color it grows its shades from, its saved color, else its token where that is a color of its own. "make the neutral color darker" no longer offers `neutral '#000000'` (a gray seed grows the same shades, so it changed nothing) nor an exact `--color-neutral` that turned every see-through neutral fill opaque; it says why and what to name instead. An exact-token alternative keeps the token's own strength.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a settings entry's `only` written as text (`"false"`, `"true"`) is read as what it says, with a note, and any other value that is not true is refused with the undo that removes that entry, so `show` and the build never disagree. A theme typed after the setting (`set --color-accent '#123457' t`) is refused with the same `set` or `undo` with the theme first, never a `new` of the setting's name. `undo <theme> vibrancy` says the default vibrancy applies now. `new` with several bad dial flags suggests one command that fixes or drops each of them; `new --base` points to `--like`; `show` names a show that works and its help for an option it does not take. The name rule lists every reserved name it refuses (com0-com9, lpt0-lpt9, and com¹-com³, lpt¹-lpt³). corners takes a rem (saved in px), and a bare number gets the px line. Dial words are read in any case (ROOMY, MORE, BOTH). `set t 'corners pill'` is read as the thing and its value. With no theme named in an app with one theme, show and undo name that theme. The compile line in the result works from the folder the command ran in.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a typo of a CSS keyword that starts with no- or not- (`cursor not-alowed`, `background-repeat no-repat`) is offered the keyword, as any typo is; a real negation (`cursor 'not pointer'`) is still never offered the word it negates.

`astryx experimental theme`: a file, folder or link of yours at the open states page's name (sheet-overlays.html) is never written over by `--png`; the picture is not taken, and `set --png` and `show --png` alike say why. The open states picture shows each overlay at the height of what it holds, up to a window's height, and a dropdown menu's submenu opens with rows. `preview app --theme` refuses a theme image reached through a link that leads out of the theme folder, notes images of this app's public/ folder the new app lacks, adds each package the theme's own source imports at this project's version (refusing one this project does not have), and adds no font package for a fallback face or a family the base's fonts stylesheet already loads. A preview page file that is not a regular file is named so, with what fixes it, and its page stays so the same remove runs again. Beside `--template`, a description is offered only when it relates to a page.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `--png` takes sheet-overlays.png beside preview.png, on `show` and on every change: every menu, tooltip, popover and list drawn open, in each mode the theme has. The sample page shows none open and the full sheet is too tall to read whole, so the result of `new` names it in its look-at-it line. A change without `--png` removes it with the other pictures, and names `show --png`, which takes it again. A typeahead, whose doc requires a search source, is rendered with a sample one in the catalog the part data is read from, so its list (`typeahead-dropdown`) is recorded and `how` reads it.

`astryx experimental theme editor` sets a list's highlighted option through `--state highlighted` on its row (`selector-option-row`, `multi-selector-option`, `typeahead-option`), and reads a value labeled with that state.

`astryx experimental theme`: an editor theme whose icon registry is a module in its own folder (as compile advises) now loads in the editor's checks, and its app copy carries that module, so `show` and `set` check it and `compile --check` passes. A theme source whose tokens replace the settings' (a spread of `defineTheme`'s result with a `tokens` field of its own) is refused by name instead of every change being saved and never built. A source name cut short (`themes/t/t`, `themes/t/t.theme.`) or a theme folder in other letters is offered the theme source. An empty `--out` is refused like a blank one. A weight given in a part's `font` shorthand is loaded, and weights are judged per family, so no font gets a gap note for a weight only another family uses. The stable `theme build` of an editor theme says it does not write (or check) the theme's app copy, and names the compile that does. A copy's compile with `--out` in the theme's own folder offers only a line compile takes, once.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: the refusal of a theme's own token values no longer ends a reason with two periods.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a page background on `app-shell` also paints the shell's header and side nav, so they stay opaque when content scrolls under a sticky header; a page gradient is fixed to the viewport on the shell and those regions so they line up. `how` gives the page background one example value per mode, so text stays readable in dark mode.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode colors, kept sizes and own padding sides.
changesets.body:
- In a `light-only` or `dark-only` theme, a color you set (a token or a part's color) fills only that mode's half; the other half keeps the base theme's, so a lightbox, an overlay or a toast Core draws in the other mode stays readable. A setting saved for the theme's mode keeps its half when the theme turns one-mode.
- `mode both` after a one-mode theme says to take out a `mode` given to the app's `<Theme>` for it.
- The spacing dial keeps control sizes in order around an exact size the theme keeps (`--size-element-md 34px` with `spacing tight` gives a larger size above 34px).
- A padding your own `<theme>.theme.ts` sets on some sides of a part wins on those sides; the editor's padding still applies on the other sides, on every part, and the result says so. A physical side stays physical and a logical side logical, in each text direction: with your own `paddingLeft`, the editor's left is never written; with your own `paddingInlineStart`, the editor's `padding-left` shows only right to left (where the start is the right). A variant your own source pads wins over an editor padding on the part's plain rule, whatever sides that sets.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: per-variant colors in one mode, hover on every variant, later longhands, nested cards and kept sizes.
changesets.body:
- A one-mode color (`--mode`, or any color in a `light-only` or `dark-only` theme) on a part whose variants each have their own (a button or card background, a badge's text) goes to each variant's own rule, with the other mode's half exactly what that variant showed there (the base theme's value, else Core's; transparent stays transparent), so the other mode is unchanged for every variant; a variant's own hover still shows.
- A whole-part hover background (`--state hover`) reaches every variant, including ones the base theme gives their own hover or resting color.
- A longhand set after a shorthand wins even where the base theme holds that longhand (`padding-inline` after `padding`, `border-color` after `border`).
- A plain card inside a variant card keeps the card padding the editor gives it, in each text direction, and a variant's own padding (from the settings or your own source) no longer leaks into it; a variant your own source pads keeps its padding after an unequal editor padding on the plain card.
- The spacing dial keeps every exact control size the theme keeps (in px, rem or calc, from your own source, or set on the part) in order, on a part too; a size with no room between two kept ones takes the smaller one's size, and the result says so.
- `--mode` refused on a border names the variant in the per-mode color step; a gradient is offered as written for both modes.
- With your own source setting one corner, the corners note says the dial shows on the other corners after the undo.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode colors per variant, the spacing dial around kept steps, and padding amounts from the base theme.
changesets.body:
- A one-mode color on a part whose variants each have their own is written to each variant as the property it names (a card's `border-color` stays a border color), with each variant's own other half: an earlier setting for the other mode or for both modes, else what the variant shows unset. `--mode` on a color longhand such as `background-color` or `border-color` is accepted this way.
- A hover set as `background-color` stays on every variant after a later one-mode `background`, and a one-mode background after a plain one applies to every variant in both modes.
- A whole-part state setting that your own `<theme>.theme.ts` sets on the same state is not repeated on the variants, so it does not show anywhere, as the result says.
- The spacing dial keeps spacing steps in order around an exact step the theme keeps, reads a kept control size written as a token, `clamp()`, `min()` or `max()`, and keeps a part's own exact control size in order under a whole-theme dial.
- `how` padding amounts read the base theme's own block and inline padding on a part ("double the button padding" on butter gives `1rem 2rem`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: state settings keep the base theme's other state styles, one-mode halves across the background family and states, and one-mode tokens that are no color.
changesets.body:
- A state setting (a hover text color, say) keeps the base theme's other styles in that state, such as a variant's own hover background, in both modes.
- A one-mode color in a state keeps, in the other mode, what that state shows there: its own value, else the resting color a setting gives the variant or the part, else the base theme's.
- `background` and `background-color` count as one property for one-mode settings: a variant's earlier color is kept as the other half and replaced, and a later both-mode color replaces a one-mode one of the other name.
- A one-mode color in a state is accepted where the base theme gives the part that color.
- In a `light-only` or `dark-only` theme, a token that is no color (a shadow) is written as one value, never as a light and dark pair.
- When `--mode` is refused in a one-mode theme, the offered command keeps `--when` and `--state`, and offers `mode both` first for the mode the theme does not show.
- The spacing dial reads kept sizes in pt, pc, in, cm, mm, Q and em, in any letter case, and keeps a variant's own exact size in order on that variant.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: heading colors, the page background, gradients per mode, and background values with many variables.
changesets.body:
- `color … --on heading` (also per level with `--when level:N`) is written as the text color tokens the heading's color prop reads, on headings only, so it shows; `how` answers "headings in the accent color" with it.
- The page behind your parts is painted by `app-shell`: `--on page` (or `body`) is refused with the `app-shell` command, and `how "page background"` offers `--color-background-body` for a color and `background … --on app-shell` for a color or a gradient. Setting `--color-background-body` no longer says it changes nothing where Core's own page styles read it.
- A gradient background can differ between light and dark: `background '<gradient>' --mode dark` paints each of its colors in that mode only, beside the other mode's layers.
- A background value with more than three variables (`color-mix()` with `var()` and a stop position, layered dots) is read as CSS, as the same value with plain colors is.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode gradients and tokens keep the other mode, the page background in every AppShell, and heading colors and types.
changesets.body:
- A gradient for one mode is written as background images (typed as `background` too), so the other mode keeps its own background color; each mode's layers are kept by mode as they are written, so a fade to `transparent` is never lost. A gradient holding a `light-dark()` stop takes no `--mode`.
- A token set on a part for one mode (a heading color included, and any color in a one-mode theme) keeps the token's own value in the other mode.
- A one-mode `background` no longer removes the other mode's one-mode `background-color`.
- A background on `app-shell` shows in every AppShell variant: the shell's header and side nav take the same background (they stay opaque when content scrolls under them), its main content area is see-through, and the result says so.
- A heading color that names a text color token (`var(--color-text-secondary)`) is accepted; heading `--when type:` takes Heading's own types (display-1 to display-3).
- `how` offers a gradient for one mode as `background-image … --mode`, and a one-mode color under a part's own gradient says it does not show.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode colors in a variant or a state, gradient layers with a color, keywords with a mode, and the corners dial on parts with their own radius.
changesets.body:
- A one-mode color in a variant or a state (a heading level, a hover) keeps the theme's own value around it in the other mode: the variant's resting color, then the part's, then the whole theme's, as the theme finally has it. A later brand color reaches the other mode.
- In a one-mode background, a color written beside a gradient (`#f00 linear-gradient(…)`) is that mode's background color, and the gradient its image.
- A CSS-wide keyword (`unset`, `inherit`) takes no `--mode`; the offered command sets it for both modes.
- The corners dial reaches parts whose base theme gives them a radius of their own, and a corners step on a part starts from the radius the part shows.
- A one-mode color on a part says that, in the other mode, it overrides what Core or the base theme gives the part in context.
- `how` lists the margins a part reads among its spacing, as `set` reads them.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: part facts read from more of Core, colors that reach a part's inner text, corners that reach the parts drawing them, and results and refusals that say what is true.
changesets.body:
- The part data renders each component with each look flag turned on too (a table's `isStriped`, `hasHover`), so a table row reads its hover fill, and `how` steps that token for a lighter or darker hover instead of a brightness filter.
- `how` and a refusal of a state a part lacks list the same states.
- The focus outline tokens can be set on checkbox and radio indicators, where Core draws the focus ring at focus time.
- Changing one member of a group kept alike (inputs) alone in height says it now differs from the rest, and names `--on <group>`.
- A color on a part whose text is drawn by elements that read a text color token themselves (a top nav heading, a top nav) also goes into those tokens on the part, so the text shows it.
- Corners on a part whose corners are drawn by parts of its own inside it (a date-time input's date and time boxes) round those parts, for the part and its group.
- A whole-theme corners dial moves a part a base pins to a length or to a token the dial never moves (such as `--radius-full` on buttons), keeps a part Core rounds with a fixed token (a pill badge), and never overwrites corners set on a part.
- The result lists every state rule a change writes, including one the base theme already has a state block for.
- A color given beside its own image in one background is never reported as covered by it.
- A keyword with `--mode` on a token offers only the color; on a one-mode theme, a thing that takes no mode is refused with the command that drops `--mode`, never with a change of the theme's mode.
- A one-mode state color on a group names the members that cannot keep the other mode and offers `--only` for the part named.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: more part facts read from Core, color asks answered with colors, and refusals that point to the setting that shows.
changesets.body:
- The part data reads a background a part inherits from the region it sits in (a side nav in an app shell), and the declarations of every target an element carries (an app shell's side nav region, which is a layout panel too).
- `how` answers a lighter or darker background with a color, never a brightness filter, which dims the text and icons too: from the page's color for "darker than the page", from each variant's own fill in a state, and from the part's resting fill otherwise.
- `how` answers striped or no striped rows with the token Core paints every other row with, on the row.
- The focus ring Core draws on a checkbox or radio indicator is read as tokens the indicator reads always: an outline property or a focus state there is refused, pointing to the focus outline token with no state.
- A font size, weight, line height or letter spacing on a part whose text is drawn by elements that set their own from a token (a top nav heading, a side nav heading, a banner) is refused, pointing to that token on the part; `how` answers with it and its current value.
- A border on a part that draws none of its own, whose edges its inner parts draw (a date-time input), is refused, pointing to those parts; `how` reads "date and time input" as that part and answers for its date and time boxes.
- A checkbox's indeterminate look is reachable with `--when checked:indeterminate`, and `how` adds it beside `--state checked`.
- A text property CSS inherits, set on a part, says which parts inside it also take it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a part that another component places somewhere (the current page's button in a pagination, a pressed toggle) records that place as a condition, so what that component paints it with there is never read as the part's look at rest. A ghost button reads no fill at rest, as Core paints it.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: `how` names the same states for a state a part lacks (a selected table row) as `set` and `how <part>` do: the states `set` takes there.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: padding and corners reach the elements Core draws them on.
changesets.body:
- Padding on a table row, which CSS draws no padding on, is refused for its cells, and `how` answers a typed table row padding on the cells.
- Corners on a button group are written as the corner token its first and last buttons read, so the group's outer corners follow.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: the contrast check reads gradients, and `how` reads side nav section headings as the sections.
changesets.body:
- Text on a gradient background is measured against each of its color stops, the worst one counting; a background with an image, or a stop with no fixed color, is listed as not checked.
- `how` reads "sidebar section headings" as the side nav's sections, whose title is drawn inside them, and says which inner parts an inherited text property also reaches.
- `how <part>` says what the part is, from its component's doc.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a one-mode write changes only its mode.
changesets.body:
- A token set for one mode keeps its other half as what that mode shows: Core's own reference when the base theme's value follows it (a focus ring that follows the accent), so it keeps following the theme's tokens.
- A one-mode page background on the app shell makes the main content area see-through, and a gradient fixed, in its mode only.
- A one-mode background shorthand replaces longhands set for its mode only; a longhand set for both modes stays.
- A light-only or dark-only theme keeps the other mode's settings for the regions Core draws in that mode (a toast, a lightbox), says so, and takes `--mode` for that mode; its own mode needs no `--mode`.
- A color on a link is refused for the token its color prop reads (`--color-text-accent` for a default link), set on the link.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's conditions come from what its theming target declares. The part data records every visual prop and runtime state the part's target declares, and the readers keep a runtime state the target declares (or one written as its own name) as a condition, so a state Core adds needs no change to the editor.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: a shorthand set for one mode points to commands that change that mode only.
changesets.body:
- A shorthand with a color longhand (`border`, `border-top`, `outline`, `text-decoration`, `background`) set with `--mode` points to its color longhand for that mode and its other words (width, style) for both modes, so following it never repaints the other mode; a named color counts as a color.
- A shadow's color for one mode is offered in the value as `light-dark()`: on a part with no shadow of its own, the other half `transparent`; on a shadow token, each layer's other half kept from what that mode shows, or a true reason when the layers differ.
- `set --help` and `undo --help` say a light-only or dark-only theme takes `--mode` for the other mode, which applies where Core draws that mode.
- A light-only or dark-only theme lists the other mode's token changes it writes.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a state setting on a part (`font-weight 500 --on tab --state selected`) wins over the build's copy of the plain part's value, which the build no longer writes after it; and `how` keeps a state at the value the part shows in that state (a selected tab's semibold).
changesets.body: A shadow on the resting rule of a part that draws its rings in its box-shadow (a text input's hover and focus rings) is refused with that reason, in both modes or one, since it would replace the rings in every state.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- The part data reads overlays drawn open: a tooltip, a popover, a hover card, and the lists a menu's button or a selector's field opens, which render on the server as markers alone, so `how tooltip` names what it paints and the menus group is checked.
- A fill set on a part says which fills Core gives its variants and states it now covers (a checked box's accent, a primary button's), with the line that changes only the fill at rest and the lines that fill one variant or state; a later color change says where the part's own fill keeps it from reaching.
- `corners more` from round steps to half as round again before pill, and `corners less` from pill back.
- A border color the theme sets is held to 3:1 against what it sits on in each mode.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `how`: a dialog's or drawer's title is colored, made bold or bigger through the text tokens on its title block, never on every heading; a title Core has no part for (a card's) is said so. A weight, size or color set on a part whose text is all in parts inside it that set their own is refused with those tokens.
- `how`: an alpha said of a shadow ("card shadows with 30% alpha", "50% transparent") sets its colors' alpha in every layer the part shows; a part's shadow in a state is read from that state at its default status (an input's own hover ring, never the error ring), never from a hidden layer; a ring with no blur softens through its alpha.
- `how`: "on-accent text" is the on-accent color; "heavy borders" are thicker borders; "pill buttons less round" steps the corners; a fully round part steps from half its height; "checkbox" is the box itself, not the checks group.
- The part data records a file input (a required prop that may be null is sampled as null), so a resting shadow on it keeps its hover ring.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a resting shadow on a part that draws rings in its box-shadow (an input's hover and focus rings, a status's ring) is written, and in each state Core rings it the theme's shadow comes with that ring after it, so the rings keep working; a shadow the theme sets for a state keeps its own. `how "sunken bevel on inputs"` answers with an inset bevel lit from the bottom right.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `how` reads "<part> title" (and header) after any part the census knows, of one word or more ("the empty state title"), as that part's own title part, never as every heading; "bigger" on a part that is only text is its text size, so "the empty state title red and bigger" colors and sizes the title text.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A text color on a part whose text sits on Core's media surface inside it (a toast's inverted surface) is refused with the lines that reach it, `--color-on-dark` and `--color-on-light` on the part, and `how` answers with them; the part data records such a surface.
- A resting shadow on a part that rings itself in its box-shadow keeps each of its renders' own rings: a status that draws none while focused gets the shadow alone, a shadow of none leaves the rings in their states, and a state's own shadow for the part wins on every render.
- An input's focus ring is its box-shadow ring: `how` answers a focus ring color there with that ring while focused, and an outline color, width or offset on a part that draws no outline is refused.
- "toggle thumb", "switch knob" and the like are the switch's thumb, never its track.
- A one-mode fill's covers notes keep its mode, in their words and their lines.
- The corners help names the step `more` and `less` take between round and pill.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `how` keeps a state where another of the part's own states was changed only where both hold: a checked, disabled checkbox keeps Core's fill, and an unchecked one is left alone.
- A long answer is cut only between whole asks; the rest follows as the next runnable sequences.
- "remove the underline from tabs" makes the tab's indicator transparent where it paints.
- An input's focus ring is its box-shadow ring for a color, a width or a removal; in one mode only that mode changes, and status fields, which draw no ring while focused, keep none.
- A resting shadow on ringed parts keeps each render's own focus look, for every variant (selectors included) and for a write scoped to one status.
- A piece of a part Core has no part for ("the popover arrow", "the empty state icon", "sheet titles") is named and nothing is written for the whole part; a sheet is the bottom sheet, and an alert's title is the banner's own text.
- A toast's text color refused in one mode keeps that mode on the lines it offers.
- The corners help lists the step between round and pill among its rungs.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `how` colors a table's row lines ("table row dividers red", "table borders red") through the color its cells draw them with, set on the row; never the Divider part, a row fill or a border over the cells.
- "outline buttons" is the buttons dial's outline; one variant outlined ("the danger buttons outline only") clears its fill and takes its own color as its border and text.
- A keep that needs two states at once ("the switch red when on except when disabled") says so.
- An input's focus ring asked per mode is one ring for both halves of a mode pair, and a layer per mode for a width in one mode, so the other mode is unchanged; a status named with the inputs ("error inputs") is that status's ring; "50% more transparent" is the ring color's alpha; a question about the ring writes nothing.
- A hover or press shadow on inputs keeps the focus ring while the field is focused.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- The part data draws every prop that changes a part's look (a toast's type, an avatar's shape), and reads a prop as a condition where it changes a color the part paints, so "the error toast background darker" steps from the error toast's own red.
- A part kept from a corner change pins every corner token its shapes read.
- A select's chevron or caret is its indicator icon, and a piece a part does not have (a date picker's segments) is named; neither writes the whole part.
- "indeterminate checkboxes red" reaches indeterminate boxes only, and "selected" is a toggle button's pressed state.
- A part that draws a line on some sides only (a grouped button's join) is still listed as drawing no border of its own.
- A one-mode hover shadow on inputs keeps their hover ring; "half as visible" is the input ring's alpha; "all focus rings" colors the inputs' rings too; a one-mode border on a part with no line draws one, see-through in the other mode; a radio's dot is its own part; "the progress indicator" is the progress bar's, and a state it does not draw apart (indeterminate) is named.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: the part data records what a divider's line paints (its color per variant and its thickness) as the divider's own, so `how` makes a divider fainter, thinner or darker through the color and width its line reads, and thinner or thicker steps from the thickness it shows now.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A border in one mode on a part that draws none is a ring at its edge (an inset box-shadow) that takes no room, so the other mode keeps its size; where the part draws a shadow of its own, the answer says why it cannot.
- Outlined buttons in one mode keep the outline dial beside the one-mode colors, and say the dial is the same in both modes.
- A divider's line is reached per variant: its color (the strong divider's own token), its thickness by the amount said, and its removal. A fill on the divider's own element, or a token its variant does not read, is refused with the line that reaches it.
- A token family follows a source written as one `light-dark()` value or a token reference.
- A variant's low-contrast text is listed once, with a fix scoped to that variant.
- A part's border is no longer colored through parts inside it that draw no line (a toast's ghost buttons); a part with no border made thicker takes its own height.
- A state shadow that keeps Core's ring keeps each status's own ring there.
- Pieces named after a part's catalog name ("the checkbox check", "the select arrow") are those parts.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- States Core paints from an ARIA attribute are states `set` names: `current` (a pagination's current page), `pressed` and `expanded` (an open menu button), built as that attribute.
- Several states at once (`--state checked+disabled`) are taken where Core paints them together, and `how` names them that way.
- A group styled alike (checks, inputs) spreads a setting only to members Core draws alike: a checkbox's corners stay off the round radios.
- The part data reads what a checkbox list and a menu holds (its rows, a row's icon), so scoped tokens on them are taken.
- A fill drawn by an element inside a part (a slider's filled range) is reached through the token it is painted with.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: an element named before "in" or "of" a part ("the selected option row in the selector", "the hovered option in the selector", "the checked item in the dropdown menu") is that part's own element, by the rest of its catalog name and the state said, never another component the words seem to name (a table's rows) or the part itself; the last place said is the place ("the text in the hovered menu item of the dropdown" is in the dropdown), which is never written as a part of its own.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A part's text made transparent by an amount ("the button text 50% transparent", "the fainter text in cards 50% transparent") is its text colors at that alpha, never the whole part's opacity.
- A state typed by its prop name or its ARIA attribute (`--state isPressed` or `aria-pressed` on a button, `isSelected` on a tab) is the state of that name.
- Several states at once are taken where the element takes them (a hovered selected tab), saved in one order so either spelling is one setting, and undone in either; `how` carries both states said ("hovered selected tabs").
- A one-mode border on a part that draws a border in that state (a focused input) is that border's color alone; a line drawn as a ring keeps the shadow the part draws in that state.
- A divider's line: "fainter" fades every variant's line, "hide" takes them away, and a thickness for one variant ("subtle dividers thicker") stays on it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor` pictures (`--png`) never wait on a network: the picture's browser loads the page's own files only, so a remote stylesheet, font or image a page names (a base theme's Google Fonts import, a template's photo) fails at once instead of holding the picture until the time limit when the machine is offline or has no direct internet.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a Chrome or Chromium that stops at once (no display, a missing library) is named with its own error when `--png` reports the picture was not taken, never with the closed pipe it leaves behind. A typo of a keyword with a dash (`cursor not-alowed`) is offered the keyword again.

`astryx experimental theme`: a refused `preview app --theme` or `preview add` writes nothing: a stale theme it builds first is put back when the build fails (a theme source that does not load), so the same command is refused again rather than copying an old build. `preview app --theme` refuses a theme stylesheet url that leads out of the theme folder (the new app would not build), a theme file too large for one read, and one that cannot be read, each by name (a read, never called a write). A named pipe or a device at a file the editor reads (the preview record, a page, a picture, the pictures record) is never opened, so no command hangs on one. Theme image names are URL text (`a%20b.png` is "a b.png"), and a quoted url may hold parentheses; an image that cannot be read is left out of the previews with a note. A section sheet's pictures go with the others when the look changes, and the command that takes them again is named. A starter app names the weights of a font it adds that it does not load. `preview add` reads a typed dash form of its options, and beside a description offers only a `--template` page this app can add; `--top` beside a default page, or alone, offers the command without it; an empty `--theme` offers the preview command with each theme.

`astryx experimental theme`: a preview picture's browser makes no network request of its own (no update, time, sync or metrics checks, no proxy, no host name resolved), on the Chrome and Playwright paths alike. A theme file that is not a regular file (a named pipe, a link to a device) is never read, so `show` cannot hang on it. `show` names the theme images the previews cannot show (loaded from the network, not found, not a regular file, or over the size a preview page carries), and an image too large for a preview is refused with its name and size instead of as a React failure. Extra words to `preview app`, `preview list` and `preview remove` get a command that works and the command's help. `preview app --theme` from a workspace root gives the `cd` to the app. A description longer than the words read is quoted as typed, and a refusal says it was cut. A `--template` typo names only pages this app can add now.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a change's new problems are the ones the theme did not have before it, compared by what each problem is (the text, what draws it, what it sits on, its variant and mode), not by its printed ratio, so moving a color that leaves the same text low makes no new problem.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `openProblems` and `newProblems` list every contrast problem in JSON, and a change's new problems are compared against all of them, so following one fix line no longer reports old problems as new. The text shows the first eight and counts the rest.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: on an installed Core that draws a radio's circle with the pill token (`--radius-full`), squaring the pills ("no rounding anywhere", the square-corners note) keeps the radio marks round with that token at Core's value on them. On a Core that draws the circle at 50%, no pin is written. The "thick borders on everything" answer also frames the label boxes (badges, tokens).

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a typo of a font preset reads as that preset when the preset and the system family it names both match (`Verdena`, `Segoe IU`); a family near a system font only (`Times New Romna`, `Arail` in a list) is kept as typed, with a note whose line sets that font. `show` and `compile` give set's repair for a damaged saved value beside its undo, as every change does, and an entry saved in a typed form (`corners: pill`, `red --on card`) gets the reading set gives it. The editor's own printed setting line pasted back (`corners = pill (whole theme)`, `opacity = 0.5 on card`) carries its scope. A dial saved for one mode is refused as `set` refuses `--mode` on it, never built for both modes or for none. `set mode night` reads as dark only; `undo` compares colors as colors (`#F00` is the saved `#ff0000`); two headings words (`bold wide`, `bold and wide`) are one `new` line, and set's second line is the next step; a token in another style (`--color_accent`) or with a typo is offered as the token.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a reset value typed with a typo on a part property (`display nnone`, `font-weight normall`) offers that value again (`none`, `normal`), since it is what was typed, corrected.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: several values of one kind on a property that takes one (`margin-top '-4px -8px'`, `padding-top '1pt 2pt'`) are offered the first again, with its sign and any unit: the repair and the repair gate read "several values of one kind" through one shared reading.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: names saved in a spelling `--state` or `set` reads typed are read the same way, with a note naming the spelling saved. Before, every command refused the theme. This covers:

The agent block and the theme docs say a change to one kind of part (the sidebar, its selected item, the gaps in a form) is a theme change too, not props or styles on one page, and that `astryx experimental theme editor how "<ask>"` names the `set … --on <part>` line for it.

`astryx experimental theme`: the settings a theme's source extends are the settings module's own export, by identity anywhere up its `extends` chain, so a theme merely named like the settings is refused and one that reaches them through another theme is accepted. A source that stops loading is refused by `show` and never recorded as built. `compile` builds a family in a `font` shorthand like any font, leaves a family the app copy loads out of the full font help family by family, names a theme folder it cannot write with its fix, says in its JSON result the `--out` warnings text prints, and says that an editor theme's next set or show builds it without `--icons-specifier`. `set` and `show` give the install line for every built family nothing loads, a font token's included. A theme or an `extends` written as a helper's call or a conditional is named as what the build cannot follow, not as an inline icon registry.

With no app yet, the agent block, the theme docs and `astryx experimental theme --help` point to `astryx experimental theme preview app <dir>`, which makes a starter app that shows the theme, instead of building an app by hand.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: several states saved joined by `+` with spaces around it (`"selected + hover"`) are read as those states, as `--state` reads them typed, with a note. Before, every command refused the theme.
changesets.body: A part's own state saved by hand in a spelling the editor reads (`is-pressed` on button) no longer leaves `compile` refusing after `show`: the build reads the state, and the settings stay as saved until a change writes the part's spelling.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: a font macOS or Windows ships (such as Avenir Next, Optima, Futura, Candara, Corbel, Bahnschrift or Segoe UI Variable) gets no install line, and a Fontsource package the editor cannot vouch for gets its own install line in compile's font help, so one that does not exist never stops the others installing. Typography `fallbacks` with no `family` in that role are refused, as Core builds nothing from them. A weight the theme uses that the base theme's font stylesheet does not load is named, with the weight it shows as, by `show` and `compile`.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: a selected table row's fill is the token Core paints it with.
changesets.body:
- The part data reads the paint Core writes inline when it sets a state at run time, so a table row in `selected` reads `--color-accent-muted`.
- `how "selected table row light blue"` answers `--color-accent-muted <color> --on table-row --state selected`, and a background on a selected table row, which Core's inline wash would hide, is refused with that command.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a setting on toggle-button's own pressed state (`--state isPressed`) is built on the attribute value ToggleButton writes, `[data-is-pressed="true"]`, so it now applies; before, it was built on `[data-is-pressed="isPressed"]`, which never matches. A part's state that names a boolean prop of its component is built as that prop's "true" value; any other state is built as its own name, as before.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the sheet and its pictures show a typeahead's list open. The render loads React DOM's client with a document in place before the page (a part that loads it with the page, such as a toast, loaded it with none, so typing never reached a field's change handler), types as a person types, and opens a typeahead's open look without waiting for its search delay.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: every repair reads a typo of a typed value, setting, part, state or theme or token name the same way: within one letter for a word of five letters or fewer and two for a longer one, two letters swapped counting as one. So `border-style line` is no longer offered `none`, and `display flxe` is offered `flex`, never `flow`; `nnone` and `normall` are still corrected. The words of a `how` question keep their own spelling reading.

`astryx experimental theme editor undo`: the headline names what the undo took back (`[ok] v: undid neutral = #78716c (whole theme)`, or `undid 2 changes: …`), in the text and in the JSON (`undid`), so a tail of the output keeps it. When the last change command was refused, the undo says that command changed nothing, so it took back the change before it (`refusedBefore`).

`astryx experimental theme editor set … font`: a family the editor does not know is kept as typed (Corben, Gabriela, Candal are real families, no typos of Corbel, Gabriola, Candara), with a note giving the line that sets the font a system ships spelled near it. A typo of a font preset is refused with the preset, a name listed both as a preset and a system font counted once (`Gerogia` reads as georgia), and the presets are read before the system fonts near it (`Corier` is courier, `Monlo` mono). Arial Narrow and Andale Mono are noted as fonts only macOS ships.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a `var()` is read as CSS reads it. Glued after a letter or a digit (`padding '2var(--spacing-4)'`), CSS reads no reference there, so the value is refused instead of written as a value the browser drops. Text glued after it (`'var(--spacing-4)px'`, `'8pxvar(--spacing-4)'`) is refused for the value's grammar, not as the token being the wrong kind, and the refusal no longer offers the same input again.

A run that prints its answer and then exits 1 records the code that answer carries in its debug event, as an error that `cliError` prints does. A component batch with a selector that does not resolve records the first unresolved row's code (such as `ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT`); `theme build --check` that finds stale outputs records `ERR_THEME_STALE`; `upgrade` records the code of an error it reports in text mode, and the `errorCode` of a run that stops incomplete (such as `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED`), in text and in `--json`; `init` that refuses its agent-docs path records `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`. Each code is recorded once the answer is printed, so an error that stops the answer first (a recorded theme that does not load) keeps its own code. A `debug` handler saw these runs as `ERR_UNCLASSIFIED_EXIT`. Output and exit codes are unchanged.

A machine's first `search` or `build` run, and its first `component`, `template`, `theme`, `discover` or `docs` run in a project where an integration can load, now keeps what it gathers, and Node's compile cache is written from the first run. With the CLI installed in the project, the second command on a new machine (most often the same session's next one) reads them instead of gathering again: about 1.7 s faster for `search` and 0.8 s for `component` in a project with an integration.
