A global copy with no Core beside it starts installing its Core after its first run, which changes what the next run reads, so it reads from its third run, as before. Answers do not change; `doctor`'s "Kept catalog cache" row counts the entries the first run now keeps.

Malformed component icon slot values no longer throw while formatting diagnostics. Invalid fields keep the component fallback without dropping valid sibling fields, and production skips diagnostic formatting.
MultiSelector's caller-rendered trigger exposes its disabled state and blocks caller activation handlers, including when read-only or disabled by InputGroup, while remaining focusable.

An `Item` with its own `onClick` or `href` no longer rings the whole row when a control in its `startContent` or `endContent` takes focus, and a `Token`'s remove button no longer rings the whole token: each of those tab stops shows one focus ring. Rows that delegate to a nested control, and reorderable rows with a handle, keep their ring as before.

Tab moves through a `Popover` or a `DropdownMenu` that opens inside a native `<dialog>` that the page displays closed. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap at the layer's edges, and a `DropdownMenu`'s header and footer are Tab stops again. The focus trap counted every control in a closed dialog as hidden, so it found no Tab stops and held focus in place.
changesets.body: A closed dialog that the page displays has a box, so its controls are Tab stops. A closed dialog with `display: none` has no box, and its controls stay out of the Tab cycle.

changesets.headline: Buttons in form page templates that did nothing now show a demo message that says what would happen: Cancel in the workspace and audiobook wizards, Create workspace and Submit for review on a finished last step, Place Order on a complete payment form, and Save on the payment form's cart line.

In a fresh clone (a project that lists `@astryxdesign/core` and a theme package, with nothing installed yet), `astryx doctor` now says to install the project's dependencies, such as `npm install`, for a missing Core and a missing theme package. Before, its fixes added Core with no version and the theme package at the latest release, so following them replaced the project's versions with others.

In a fresh clone whose `package.json` lists `@astryxdesign/cli`, the once-a-day hint, `doctor`, and the setup reminder now say to install the project's dependencies (such as `npm install`), not to add the CLI again. Adding it again replaced the exact version the project lists with a range, such as `^0.7.10`.

File protection now decodes consecutive octal escapes in quoted `.gitattributes` paths as UTF-8 bytes. Before, a rule such as `"caf\303\251.js" linguist-generated` was treated as separate code points and failed to protect the matching `café.js` file; quoted and literal UTF-8 spellings now classify consistently.

In a Yarn Plug'n'Play project, the `astryx` command installed for the computer hands each run to the project's own CLI: it starts again with the project's runtime, as Yarn starts a command, instead of answering with its own release and telling you to install a CLI the project already has. Commands the CLI prints there start with `yarn astryx`, not with a `yarn dlx` download of the CLI.

Two page templates no longer leave an empty column on wide screens. The product gallery's header (a heading and its intro) now fills two columns instead of three, and the two-column form's contact strip fills three columns instead of four, so it sits centered. Narrower widths are unchanged.

The hero and gallery page templates' call-to-action buttons (Get started, Learn more, Explore in `centered-hero`, `gallery-hero`, `product-gallery` and `side-gallery`) are now links to `#`, so they behave as the links they stand in for instead of doing nothing. The Get started arrows in `centered-hero` and `product-gallery` now point toward the end of the line in right-to-left, as in `gallery-hero`; nothing else changes in layout or styling.

Hook docs for `useChatDictation`, so `astryx hook useChatDictation` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useChatDictation — Voice input` example block: a start and stop control that stays off when the browser has no speech recognition.

Hook docs for `useChatPasteAsToken`, so `astryx hook useChatPasteAsToken` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useChatPasteAsToken — Long paste` example block: a composer that uses a threshold of 40 and a Pasted note label.

Hook docs for `useSpeechRecognition`, so `astryx hook useSpeechRecognition` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useSpeechRecognition — Transcript` example block: a headless control that shows whether the browser can listen and the interim transcript.

Hook docs for `useSyntaxTheme`, so `astryx hook useSyntaxTheme` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useSyntaxTheme — Keyword color` example block: the word const painted with the keyword color of the GitHub Light syntax theme.

A run through `@astryxdesign/cli/host` now keeps what it gathers, as a run of the `astryx` bin does, so a tool that carries the CLI answers its second `search` from the kept catalog: about 0.47 s instead of 1.4 s. A kept entry names the package sets, integrations and command name the host passed, so a hosted run and a bin run in the same folder never read each other's answers. Answers do not change.
The IDE page template's description now says what its middle pane is: a single read-only code pane, not tabbed documents.

In the Tool: IDE page template, the editor's and terminal's scrollbars no longer sit under the properties panel's resize handle. On desktop the editor and terminal keep a small gap before the handle, so the whole scrollbar scrolls; before, a press on the half of the scrollbar nearest the handle resized the panel. Mobile, where the panel is hidden, is unchanged.

In `RichTextEditor`, a Markdown block marker typed at the start of a list item now re-marks it and keeps its text: `- `, `1. `, or `[ ] ` switches the item's list between bullets, numbers, and tasks, and `# ` or `> ` takes a top-level item out of its list as a heading or a quote, the rest of the list continuing after it. Each change is one undo step, back to the marker as typed.

The incident console page template works on a phone and its buttons act. On a narrow screen its header controls wrap onto their own rows, and choosing an incident opens its details in a bottom sheet instead of doing nothing. The inspector's next-step button ("Mark mitigated", "Resolve", "Reopen") moves the incident to its next status, and "Escalate" and "Declare incident" confirm with a demo toast that marks where to connect the real action. Rows show each incident's start date and time instead of a relative time that grew stale. The template stays unready for now.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor` name a theme module that `theme build` wrote (`.js`, `.mjs` or `.cjs`) and that imports TypeScript source, as built themes from a CLI before this one do (`built_module_imports_typescript`, a `next` note with the weight of `relative_import_not_shipped`), with the file, the line, and the fix.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` in a package's own folder keep npm's list of the files the package packs. They read it back while the package's folders list the same entries (names, types and where each link points), and package.json, the ignore files npm applies in the package and in each folder above it, any package.json above it, and the npmrc files npm reads are all unchanged. Which files npm packs never depends on what they hold, so a run after an edit inside a file, saved in place or by renaming a new copy over it, skips npm. That took seconds for a large package: each check there finished about 2.6 seconds sooner. A package that bundles dependencies, or has a link in its folders, is asked every time. Output does not change.

`integration check` and `doctor integration validate` ask npm once what a package's own folder packs, instead of once for each check that asks, and the authoring checks inside `integration check` no longer run the shipped-import check, whose notes they never read. In a large package with a `files` field, `integration check` finishes in about 10 seconds instead of 27, and `doctor integration validate` in about 9 instead of 12.5. Output does not change.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` now resolve every relative import of the modules a package ships the way an app's bundler does, against the files npm packs (for an installed package, its files on disk). Run in the package's own folder, they used to pass an import such as `./icons` that the tarball leaves out, because the file was on disk there. Each import no shipped file answers is a `relative_import_not_shipped` note marked `next`, naming the importing file, the import, and that the file is not in the package. It fails `integration check --strict --next` now; the next minor release makes it a warning, which fails `--strict`. When npm cannot be asked, an import whose file no `files` entry can reach is still a note, and any other is listed as not checked. `astryx doctor`'s theme owners check now also reads a package theme's stylesheets, whose `@import` and `url()` references it never followed, and warns that the built module loads but names a file the package does not ship. Type-only imports are skipped; `./icons` resolving to `icons/index.js` is fine.

`astryx theme add`, on the first add, when an installed package names the provider that wires its themes, says so: "This app may already get its theme from <Provider> (from <module>, declared by <package>)", with the props it takes the theme and mode through. When that one provider takes the theme (its manifest's `themeProvider` names `themeProp`), every receipt that shows wiring shows that provider in place of a Theme wrap: the first add passes the generated module's theme to it (`<Provider theme={themes[defaultThemeSlug]}>`, plus `<modeProp>={themeModes[defaultThemeSlug]}` for a theme with one color mode when it names `modeProp`), a later add that first lists `themeModes` passes the mode to it when the manifest names `modeProp`, and `theme remove` of the last theme undoes those props and keeps the provider. With no `themeProp`, or two such providers, the first add names each provider and its trade-off ("Replacing <Provider> applies this theme everywhere but also drops anything else it sets up; a Theme inside it themes only what it wraps.") above the Theme wiring. No receipt reads app source. The JSON carries it as `appProvider`: each provider as `{export, from}` (with `themeProp` and `modeProp`), `wire`, and `themeProp` and `line` when the provider form applies. An integration manifest's `themeProvider` takes an optional `themeProp` and, beside it, an optional `modeProp`. `themeProvider` is a hint and never stops a manifest loading: a part this CLI cannot use (an export that is no component name, a prop that names no prop, a `modeProp` with no `themeProp`) is dropped with an `ignored_manifest_field` warning.

For an app whose theme its integration's provider wires, `astryx doctor` names the theme a stylesheet of the package belongs to: one in that theme's own folder, or one its stylesheet imports. `astryx theme list` says on each such theme's `wiredBy` line that the provider applies when the app renders it, and that `astryx doctor` checks where.

An integration that wires its themes with its own provider component can name it once in its manifest: `themeProvider: {export, from}`. `astryx doctor` then counts the package's theme as wired when the app renders that component (the theme whose stylesheet the app imports, or the package's only theme), instead of warning that no theme is wired, and its CLI-managed-themes check names the theme and its provider instead of offering `theme add`. An import of the provider that is never rendered still does not count. A stylesheet the app imports from the package counts as the theme it is, wherever the package keeps it; doctor names it, and never calls it missing when it cannot match it to one theme. `astryx theme list` shows `wiredBy` beside each of the package's themes, in text and JSON; its added and default marks stay as they are. A CLI that does not know the key, or a key inside it, ignores it with a warning and keeps the rest of the manifest.

An open swipe-action row on `Item` and `ListItem` closes on a touch tap on its own content, as a UIKit list row does, and that tap no longer activates the row or paints its press. It also closes when the list or the page scrolls, including a scroll that starts on the row itself, unless focus is inside its open panel (the browser may be scrolling a focused entry into view), and it counts as open from the release that opens it, before its spring comes to rest.

Under a finger, a full swipe on an `Item` or `ListItem` swipe-action row works like a UIKit list row's, the same on every touch device. Past the open width the entries ride the row and the outermost action stretches out to the edge. Dragged on past the confirm point, judged on the finger as UIKit does, the row runs ahead and the outermost action covers its place. Letting go there fires it at any speed; backing out undoes that and closes the row. On a side with two or more actions, a full swipe confirms only from the open row. A disabled outermost action never confirms.

Swipe actions on `Item` and `ListItem` run on the gesture system. A row claims a sideways touch at 8 px, before a browser commits to scrolling it. From the claim the row follows the finger one for one, so the part under the finger stays under it. A pen now swipes the row as a finger does. A second finger that lands before the claim leaves the touch to the browser's pinch; once the row has claimed its finger, a second finger no longer cancels the swipe. The click a browser synthesizes after a swipe is cancelled at its source instead of being swallowed by a 400 ms timer.

A trackpad's two-finger swipe moves an `Item` or `ListItem` swipe-action row with the fingers from its first event past 8 px and, when they lift, settles it on the nearest stop at their speed, without stopping first. Within one swipe an open row only closes, and a long fast swipe fires the outermost action where a full swipe may. A mouse wheel's notches never swipe a row.

Under a finger, swipe actions on `Item` and `ListItem` move like a UIKit list row, the same on every touch device. The row stays under the finger, one for one, until the release, and settles on UIKit's own spring from where it is and as fast as it was moving, so a release no longer stops dead and restarts. The settle plays on the compositor, so a busy page cannot hold it back. A flick opens the row or closes it, by its direction. Under Reduce Motion nothing a release starts travels or springs: the row cross-fades to where it lands, as `design:reduced-motion` asks. A finger that lands on a moving row catches it instead of being ignored until the row stops.

`component --list` keeps its list between runs in a project where an integration can load, like template discovery's records, so a repeat list answers sooner there (about 220 ms with a large TypeScript integration). A new, removed or edited component, doc or integration lists again on the very next run.

Which integration component answers to a Core component's name is kept between runs with the component list, so `component` in a project whose integration replaces Core components no longer loads every one of that integration's component docs on each run: about 40 to 60 ms faster per call in a project with a large integration. It is decided again whenever a doc's `replaces`, the package's CLI range, the integration's components folder, its configuration or its manifest changes. Output does not change.

A kept catalog entry now names the kept entries it builds on and stores only the file states they do not hold. A run checks each kept entry once, however many entries build on it, so an entry checks no file that the entries it builds on already checked. A warm `component`, `search` or `template` in a project with a large integration checks about 3,800 fewer files; output does not change.

In a project with an integration, `astryx` commands that read back what they kept (`component`, `search`, `template`, `docs`, `build` and others) finish about 10 ms sooner. A kept gather no longer checks the CLI's own files one by one: as the per-user cache record already says, the CLI's build id stands for them, and now so does the folder the CLI runs from, so a copy installed in another folder, such as a patched one, keeps its own entries. In-place edits to an installed CLI stay unsupported; deleting the per-user `astryx/catalogs` folder clears what was kept. A package in the node_modules folder inside the CLI's is still checked, as before. Output does not change, except `astryx doctor`'s cache row, which now names the folder beside the build id.

A released input hold no longer changes its layer. A closing BottomSheet's hold reads focus a moment after focus leaves the sheet; if the hold was released in between, that late read could leave the sheet inert and hidden from assistive technology. No browser flow is known to hit this today.

`doctor` keeps its scan of how the app wires its themes between runs, like its docs checks, so a repeat `doctor` answers about 20 to 35 ms sooner. An edit to the app's source, a theme or a theme package scans again on the very next run.

`Popover`, `Tooltip`, `HoverCard` and the other anchored layers open again when their trigger sits in a native `<dialog>` that the page displays closed. Such a dialog never enters the top layer, so its trigger is a valid anchor. The layer waited for the dialog to open, and it never opened.
changesets.body:
A layer still waits for a `Dialog` that displays its element before it calls `showModal()`. `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `Lightbox` and `MobileNav` open their dialog in the Effects of the commit that displays it. A trigger with a box in a closed dialog now waits for one more commit. React runs those Effects before it renders that commit, so a dialog that is still closed then stays closed, and the layer opens at once. For a press, that commit runs before the press's task ends, so the layer and its initial focus land within the press. A closed dialog with `display: none` gives its trigger no box, and the layer still waits for it with no time limit.

A second `show()` while a layer waits for the same trigger keeps that wait. It no longer restarts it.

changesets.headline: The theme build loads jiti, which transpiles TypeScript theme sources, through the module loader's lazy CommonJS loader, instead of importing jiti's ES module entry whenever any command loads the theme API. `component` in text and `doctor` no longer load jiti and start about 15 to 30 ms sooner. `theme build` still loads it, but no longer through the ES module entry, which made Node scan jiti's whole CommonJS bundle for export names; it starts about 15 to 30 ms sooner too. Output does not change.

Lightbox: an open caption that ends in a block image wider than the room beside "less" keeps its text lines when the window widens, instead of growing by a line every frame. "less" takes the line below the image. (#11740)

In block and inline layout, a Link whose label has no break opportunity, such as a bare URL from `useLinkify`, now wraps inside its line instead of running past it and making the page scroll sideways. The Link stops at its container and its label may shrink, so its text wraps. In a flex row, a Link whose label is wider than the row is now capped at the row's width and wraps. A Link in a line wide enough for its label looks the same. A content-sized grid or table column still grows to the label's longest word.

Markdown's anatomy now says when its Image part shows alternative text: for an empty image URL, while an unsafe URL renders as source text. Its guidance adds two don'ts: plugins cannot cross a Server Component boundary, and Markdown does not sanitize renderer output. Prop docs now describe `density`, `isStreaming`, `onLinkClick`, and `components`; `inlinePlugins` keeps its own description instead of lending it to `plugins`; `contentWidth` names its 680 default; and the `contentAlign="start"` description now says inline start instead of left. The `onLinkClick` docs say that a custom `link` renderer does not receive the handler.

The messaging shell page template, still marked not ready, now works as an app. AppShell owns its side navigation of channels and direct messages, so on a phone the channels open from the navigation toggle. Picking a direct message shows that conversation, sending a message or a thread reply adds it to the page, a message's replies open its thread (in a drawer on narrow screens), and selecting a conversation clears its unread count. The page no longer uses raw elements or a local style object, and the actions without a real destination show a demo toast.

The messaging shell template notes what must hold before it is marked ready: build keeps the default app shell for parts and edits whose words the template does not use, and the page-pick model is retrained to include it.

MetadataListItem's prop docs now list `xstyle`, `className`, `style`, `ref`, and `data-testid`, and say which element each one reaches: the label `dt` when the item is side by side, or the wrapper when it is stacked. The `data-testid` docs say that a side-by-side item puts `-label` and `-value` on its two cells.

MobileNavToggle's docs now say every case where it renders nothing: above the mobile breakpoint, without an AppShell mobile context (AppShell's, or an `AppShellMobileContext` you provide), and when AppShell has no mobile navigation (no side or top nav, `mobileNav={false}`, or a `mobileNav` node).

MobileNav with `side="auto"` opens from the opener's inline edge in right-to-left layouts. When the opener holds focus, that is used. When nothing is focused (such as the first open after a page load), the opener is found through its `aria-controls`, which AppShell's `MobileNavToggle` sets. A custom opener without `aria-controls` that never takes focus still opens from `end`.

MoreMenu's prop docs now list `isMenuOpen` and say that without `size` the trigger takes the surrounding size (from a SizeProvider, ButtonGroup, or Toolbar), else `md`. The Chinese docs gain `isMenuOpen` and `onOpenChange` and the note on where host `data-*` attributes land.

Icons, `useIcon`, and component icon slots use the nearest Theme's object, so registering or nesting another theme with the same name does not replace their artwork. Icons outside a provider keep the registered root-theme fallback.

When `astryx component` or `astryx template` finds no entry, the not-found error also points to a hook the name nearly spells or names by meaning. A `use…` name one or two slips from a hook's name, or one whose every word that hook's name carries (`useTableExpansion` for `useTableRowExpansion`), suggests that hook (`astryx hook <name>`). For `astryx component`, a name of two or more words that are exactly a keyword one hook's doc declares (`CopyButton` for a hook whose doc lists `copy button`) suggests that hook. The hint goes first only when no own suggestion matches as well: a suggestion whose name nearly spells the typed name or carries every typed word, or a component whose doc keywords or search-card synonyms hold the same phrase, stays ahead of it. The list never grows, the lookup still fails, and a name that already matches another command's entry by name keeps that hint.
The npm descriptions of `@astryxdesign/core` and `@astryxdesign/cli` name Astryx, so a search for "astryx" on npm lists them with the other Astryx packages.

`OverflowList`s that mount or change in one render now measure together after it, before the frame paints. When other components write to the page in the same render, each list used to read its size after those writes and force its own layout; now all lists read their sizes first and the page lays out once for them. The first painted frame is the same. `useOverflow` results and `onOverflowChange` arrive one microtask after the render instead of inside it. A test that checks them right after a synchronous render awaits that microtask first, for example with `await act(async () => {})`. With fake timers that also fake `queueMicrotask`, as Jest's modern fake timers do by default, flush the faked microtasks too, for example with `jest.runAllTicks()` or `vi.runAllTicks()`.

Pagination: page links. Pass `getPageHref` and the page number, previous, next, first and last controls render as real links to each page's URL, so a page opens in a new tab, its address can be copied, and it works before scripts load. `getPageHref(page, pageSize)` returns the URL in the shape your app uses: a query parameter, a path segment, an offset or a cursor. `as` sets the link component, as on Button, and `LinkProvider` applies too. `onChange` still runs when a link is activated: use it for state or analytics, and do not navigate in it, because the link navigates. The dots, the page box and the page-size selector are not links and work as before. A control that stops being a link while it holds focus, at the first or last page or while the pagination is disabled, keeps that focus. A Pagination without `getPageHref` is unchanged.
`usePopover` keeps its focus-return target when `show()` runs again after initial focus has moved inside the popover, so a close returns focus to the element that opened it instead of losing it.

Add a Welcome portal page template (`welcome-portal`) for an employee intranet home: a greeting with a search box that narrows the destination cards, a "Start here" onboarding checklist with progress, and a rail of favorites, recent pages, announcements and help. It is not ready yet, so `astryx build` does not start it.

`astryx doctor` starts about 6 to 10 ms sooner, and a first lookup in a project whose integration imports the CLI's API about 15 ms sooner. Doctor's theme checks and the codemods' parser loaded postcss as they loaded, so every importer of the CLI's API loaded it too; they now load it only when they read a stylesheet. Output does not change.

`astryx component` and the `astryx theme` commands start about 5–10 ms sooner again. The theme build module they load loaded postcss at once, through the module that reads a built theme's imports; postcss now loads only when a stylesheet's imports are read. The font stylesheet reader uses the same first-use postcss. Output does not change.

A press no longer scales a trigger whose own layer is open: a Button that opens a menu or a Popover, and a ghost or secondary Selector, MultiSelector or ComplexSelector. Under a mouse or a finger, the open layer stays where an unpressed open puts it. A disclosure button without a popup keeps its press.

What the CLI keeps between runs is checked against what each check it made returned, and no more. A check whether a file is there is checked by whether it is still there, and a real-path lookup by the path it answered. An edit to a file the CLI only checked for, or only resolved, no longer makes the next run work its kept data out again. A file whose content any kept step read is checked by its stamp, as before, and so is an ignore file a check looks for before it asks npm what a package packs. Output does not change.

`astryx component <Name>` (and its `--props` view) lists props one per line, ``- `name`: `type` = `default` - description``, with the required and experimental markers after the type, instead of a four-column table. Union types keep their pipes as written, and no field is dropped; `--json` is unchanged.

`astryx component <Name>` prints the first sentence of each prop's description, under one line naming the command that prints them whole: the read's own selector and `--package` scope with `--props`, so it resolves to the same component. A read prints its descriptions whole when that line would cost more than the cut saves. The `--props` view, `--json` and `astryx discover` keep every description whole.
Selector and MultiSelector keep their selection surfaces closed when mounted disabled with `isDefaultOpen`, including when read-only or disabled by an InputGroup.

The install page now says that registry calls use Astryx's own short retry and timeout, not npm's fetch-retry or fetch-timeout settings: one retry after a 2-second wait, and at most 30 seconds per request.

`astryx experimental render` carries the page's own modules and JSON data whose names only look like configuration: `config.ts`, `lib/arc.ts`, `data/chart-config.json`, `data/config.json`. They were left out as tool configuration, so the page came back from `--reverse` with `exact: false` and without them. These names stay refused: `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.*.json`, `jsconfig.json`, any `*.config.json` or `*.config.{js,ts,…}` module, manifests and lockfiles, and dotfiles such as `.eslintrc.js`. A file that carries one says render format 2, so a CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it; 0.7.16 and earlier refuse it as damaged.

`astryx experimental render` carries the `.mts`, `.cts` and `.cjs` modules a page imports, and `--reverse` gives them back and follows their imports. The render loaded them but left them out of the file, so the page came back with `exact: false` and those modules missing. A file that carries one says render format 2, so an earlier CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it instead of calling the file damaged; every other file stays format 1.

`astryx experimental render` carries every image, font and media file a carried module's strings or a carried stylesheet name by a relative path inside the folder that holds the carried files, also when the page did not show it in this render: a branch the page did not take, or a stylesheet rule no element uses. Such files now ship in the rendered file, up to 8 MB each, as a shown image does; a larger one, one whose bytes are not an image, font or media file, or one it cannot read, is left out with a `not-embedded` warning that names the file that names it. A name that climbs above that folder is not the page's file and is not carried, as `--reverse` reads it too. `--reverse` reads the same names with the same scan, so such a page used to come back with `exact: false` and those files missing.

`astryx experimental render` draws a recharts chart sized by its `ResponsiveContainer` at a set of widths, from a narrow table cell to a wide screen, and the file's CSS shows the drawing nearest the width the reader's browser gives the chart, with no script. Before, such a chart was drawn once at a guessed size and stretched to the page's width: its text was about one and a half times its size on a desktop and half its size on a phone, and a chart that filled a box of fixed height ran out of the box. The widths run from 60 to 1920 pixels, each the square root of two times the one before, so the drawing shown scales by at most the fourth root of two either way. The chart now keeps the height the page gives it (a number, the width over `aspect`, or its share of the height that the box it fills states in its own style) and fits that box whole, so its text stays within a fifth of its own size. A box whose height comes from a stylesheet gives no height to read: the chart is drawn 300 pixels high and fits inside the box, scaled down in a shorter box and with empty space above and below in a taller one. Its legend sits inside its picture, where recharts places it, and keeps the rest of its style. Each such chart carries eleven drawings, whose coordinates keep two decimal places, so it takes several times the room in the file that one drawing takes. A chart of fixed size is drawn as before.

When a page does not compile, `astryx experimental render` names the file and the line the error points at, also for a module the page imports. When StyleX cannot read a value a style imports, the message names the value and the import, and says what StyleX needs: the value written in the style, or a `.stylex.ts` or `.stylex.js` file that defines it; for a `.stylex` file it cannot find, it says to check that the file or its package is there.

`astryx experimental render`: a rendered file now explains itself to whoever opens it next. A note at its top names the CLI version and render format that made it, the page's path, the files it carries and the packages it rendered with, and gives the exact commands that get the source back and render it again; a short note after the embedded source repeats the way back. `--reverse` reports the render format, the CLI version (`renderedBy`), the packages and an explicit `--title` (`title`), and, for files this version renders, whether someone changed the markup after the render (`edited`, read as a browser reads the file, so a copy whose line ends changed on the way is not edited) with each text change (`edits`: what it was, what it is now, and the restored file and line that hold the old text, in a module or the JSON data it imports, also where it wraps across lines). A file in a newer render format than the CLI reads is refused with the new `ERR_RENDER_NEWER_FORMAT`, which names the CLI version that wrote it; a file that names a CLI version that is not a semantic version is refused as damaged, so no printed command carries it, and every path a printed command takes from a received file is quoted. The render format stays 1, so earlier CLIs keep reading the files this version writes, except for a file that carries an `.mts`, `.cts` or `.cjs` module, which says format 2 so that a CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it; 0.7.16 and earlier refuse it as damaged.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` finds a rendered file's title, styles and body as a browser does, outside comments and outside the text of the style element, so an untouched file whose stylesheet text looks like HTML, or whose page path looks like a tag, no longer reads as edited.

`astryx experimental render` says why when no answer from the page's process reaches the CLI: the answer was sent but not received, the process ended while it sent it, or the stage it ended in, after how many seconds and with how much memory free. When the page's process cannot send its answer, the error now says so.

A page render that draws overlays open waits for React's queued work before it reads them, and no longer compares the page's markup turn after turn: a page whose overlays have settled is read at once, so the theme editor's sample page and sheet render as fast as before while each render stays the same every time. The theme editor's contrast checks reuse each part's token reads within a command.

A page render that draws overlays open (the theme editor's sample page and sheet) reads each overlay once its update has finished. Before, on a busy machine it could read an overlay between two renders, so the same theme could render to different pages: `undo` then left the sample page different from before the change.

`astryx experimental render` outside a project carries the modules a page imports from above its own folder, and the files those modules import, as long as they are inside the current folder. A page restored with its neighbours (`report-restored/app/report/page.tsx` beside `report-restored/components/`) and rendered again by the command its file prints used to leave those modules out, so the new file came back with `exact: false`. Where the render reads the page's `tsconfig.json` and `public/` images does not change.

`astryx experimental render` renders a page outside a project whose StyleX reads Astryx theme variables (`@astryxdesign/core/theme/tokens.stylex`), as many templates do. Such a page stopped with "The page does not compile: Could not resolve the path to the imported file", because the StyleX compiler looked for Core beside the page, where outside a project there is none. The compiler now gets the theme file the page loads from the CLI's own Core, and the page renders the same as it does inside a project.

`astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` read a folder or file whose name begins with two dots (`..x`) as one inside the folder that holds it, where they took it for the folder above. A page in such a folder keeps its own folder as the root of the files it carries, so the file it writes reverses; a file above it stays out, named in a `not-embedded` warning. The note at the top of a page rendered outside a project names the page by its path among the files it lists (`app/x/page.tsx`), where it named only the file (`page.tsx`) and pointed at it as the file to edit.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the overlays a page opens are drawn one part at a time, so a part's document listeners (a typeahead's or a menu's outside press) hear only presses on its own controls. Every editor command that reads the part data, and every sheet picture, no longer pays for each press on every other part. The part data is the same as before.

`astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` say that a file they cannot read cannot be read, with the reason (`EACCES: no permission`, a folder or a pipe given as the file), and the new error code `ERR_READ_FAILED`. They used to say the file does not exist, with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, which a file that is not there keeps.

`astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` read path aliases from the config TypeScript reads for the page: the nearest `tsconfig.json` (else `jsconfig.json`) at or above it, through its `extends` (a path with or without `.json`, a package's config, or a list, the later one winning, with `${configDir}`), and, behind a solution-style `tsconfig.json` (`"files": []` with `references`, as Vite sets up), the referenced project that includes the page. A page whose aliases live in `tsconfig.app.json` or in an extended config used to fail, with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, or with `ERR_RENDER_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` when the alias looks like a package name (`@data/rows`), although `tsc` and the app's build found its imports.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` gives back a page that imports files through a path alias (`@/components/Header`) in a folder whose project has no alias for those imports, such as an empty folder holding only the HTML file. A render records which carried file each alias import named; where no alias of the receiving project names the import, the file comes back in the page's own layout inside the new folder, byte for byte. The result's `aliased` names each such import with its file, the whole `paths` the page needs to build (the entries the config has now, own or inherited, with every target the imports need), and the tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json it belongs in (the one TypeScript reads for the page, else a new one), and the text prints them. Only an import that cannot be a package name or a package's own subpath import is followed this way (`@/…`, `~/…`), so a received file can never remap a package or the reader's own imports. Such a page used to be refused as carrying "files the page does not import". Where the project's alias points outside the new folder, the restore is still refused; an import that looks like a package name (`@components/Header`), or a file from an older CLI, which records no alias imports, is still refused unless the receiving project has the alias, and the refusal now says so.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` finds the embedded source in a file whose script tag a minifier or another tool rewrote: an unquoted `type` (`<script type=application/x-astryx-source>`), or an attribute before `type`. Such a file used to come back as a page rebuilt from its markup (text and layout only) instead of the exact source.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` refuses two kinds of damaged Astryx page with `ERR_RENDER_SOURCE_DAMAGED` and writes nothing, instead of answering with a page that looks fine. A rendered file cut short before its embedded source used to come back rebuilt from the part of the markup that was left; it is now refused as cut short. An Astryx page a merge left with conflict markers used to give back one side's source without a word; it is now refused, naming the conflict, so you keep the whole file from one side or render the merged page again. A file that is not an Astryx page is still refused with `ERR_RENDER_NOT_ASTRYX`, markers or not.

`astryx experimental render` gives a relative or aliased import with `?raw` the file's text, and a `.css` file imported with `?inline` its text (not added to the page), as Vite does by itself, however the import names it. It used to give a JSON file's object for `?raw`, fail on a text file such as `notes.txt?raw`, and refuse a `.css` file with `?inline` as CSS Modules. A package import with `?raw`, and a Sass, Less or package stylesheet with `?inline`, stay as before. Any other query loads the file as it loads without one, as before: an image, font or media file as its address (`?url`, `?inline`, `?w=400`), a module as itself. `--reverse` gives back the files the render carries; a `?raw` file of a kind a render never carries, such as `notes.md`, is named in a `not-embedded` warning.

`astryx experimental render` warns when the page asks a media query in JavaScript, with Core's `useMediaQuery` (from `@astryxdesign/core` or `@astryxdesign/core/hooks`) or with `matchMedia`. The rendered file runs no script, so readers on every screen got the layout of the answer the page had on the server, with no word why. The new `screen-query` warning names each query and says to fold the layout with CSS: `Grid` with `columns={{minWidth}}`, or a StyleX `@media` or `@container` style.

On Windows, `astryx experimental render` and the experimental theme editor now transform the page's own files. The renderer read every file as outside the project, because the module loader named files with forward slashes while the project path used backslashes, so no file was transformed. A page or theme that imported a stylesheet then failed with `Unknown file extension ".css"`, and StyleX, image and JSON imports were not handled either.

`astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` write in one step. A render writes the HTML file under a temporary name beside it, then gives it its name, so a reader or another run never finds half a file: two renders of one page to one file both succeed, where one could be refused because the file "already exists and was not written by a render". A restore writes its new folder the same way, so restores run at the same time each get a folder of their own, also when they restore with `--out` into folders under one new folder, where some were refused, and a restore stopped part-way leaves no folder behind, so the same command works again. A run stopped between its write and its rename leaves a hidden temporary file or folder, which the next run to the same place, on the same computer and in the same container or sandbox, removes once that run's process is gone. A render still never replaces an HTML file this user cannot write, and the file it replaces keeps its permission bits; it now needs to make a file in the HTML file's folder, so a folder this user cannot write is refused, and the refusal names it. Every copy a restore writes, except the page at its target, lands in the one new folder, including a copy of the page that a path alias places; such a copy outside it is refused with nothing written.

reset.css gives the page the `--font-family-body` font, so text in the page body outside the Theme wrapper, such as a tooltip or a hidden span a chart uses to measure labels, no longer falls back to the browser's serif font. A page where no stylesheet defines the token keeps its current font.

A command that reuses kept data hands each kept list of what it read to the run's records once, instead of once for every step that reuses it, and works out the CLI-file states a derived value keys on only when one is asked for. In a project with a large integration, `component`, `docs`, `doctor`, `search`, `template` and `theme list` finish 4 to 14 ms sooner. Output does not change.

Adds a Review Workspace page template for grading a batch of items one at a time: score, decision, issue checklist and note per item, with a summary at the end. It is marked WIP (`isReady: false`) and stays out of the docsite template gallery until it is ready.

Apps that install the rich text package no longer see "Warning: @astryxdesign/richtext has N integration issue(s)" on `astryx search`, `component`, `template`, `theme`, `discover` and `upgrade`. The editor's internal plugins now live in a folder the CLI does not read as components, so the integration check reports no issues. The public components and imports are unchanged.
Internal: the toolbar's link popover, its URL form, the link address rule, and the toolbar's inline-format helpers move into modules RichText shares internally. Apps see no change.

A line break typed with Shift+Enter at the end of a paragraph, list item or quote no longer saves as a backslash that comes back as a literal `\` the next time the Markdown loads. Markdown has no line break at the end of a block, so the editor leaves it out of the Markdown; a line break inside a block still saves and loads as a line break.

A new `Run Console` page template, not yet listed as ready: a table of pipeline and test runs with status tabs that opens a run page with progress, numbered steps, each step's log, and test results with failed tests first. New run, Re-run and Cancel update the run list. It adds the `Tools - Run Console` template category. Copy it with `astryx template run-console <path>`.

`astryx search` prints the first sentence of each result's description instead of the whole description, so a list of 20 results stays short. Component, hook and doc results' commands print the full doc; `--verbose` and `--json` keep descriptions whole.

Every `--json` result that lists or returns a template gives it `isReady`: false for a template whose doc sets `isReady: false`, else true. `discover`, which names a package's templates only by id, carries neither. That covers `search` results, `build`'s start, alternatives, pages and blocks, `template <id>` (shown, `--skeleton`, and copied), and `component <Name> --blocks`; `template --list` already had it. In text, those commands mark an unready template `(not ready)`, and `template --list` says `(not ready)` instead of `(WIP)`. Search still lists an unready template in the same place.

`astryx search` reads a one-identifier query written as a component's, type's or icon's name (PascalCase, such as `ThemeProvider`) as its words also when all it matches is text that mentions it, including a code term or table cell a doc's keywords gather. The entry that mentions it stays in the answer, beside the entries its words find. In the lexical ranking, the entry that mentions it, and an entry one of its words names outright, come before every entry its words only match; search's learned order inside a score band still applies, so `astryx search` can list a words-only match above them. A prop's name (camelCase, such as `autoFocus`) keeps only the entries that mention it, as before, and other queries rank exactly as before.

`search` lowercases each candidate's names, keywords and prose once per run instead of on every term and synonym, and scores a one-word query once instead of twice, so a warm search answers up to about 20 ms sooner, most for one-word and typo queries. Results are unchanged.

Controls that did nothing in two settings page templates now respond with a demo message that says what would happen: the three Save buttons on the settings page, and Professional hosting tools on the sidebar settings page. The sidebar settings page's back arrow and drill-in chevrons now point the right way in right-to-left languages.

A new experimental guide, `astryx docs cli/experimental/share-a-page`, walks through making a shareable page: write it with Astryx components, render it to one HTML file, share or upload that file, and turn the file back into source to change it.

The shareable-page guide (`astryx docs cli/experimental/share-a-page`) names the layouts that go wrong on a phone in a file with no script, and how to write each one: a Badge beside text in an HStack (StackItem `static` and `fill`, as its example now does), a Badge on its own line in a VStack (`<StackItem crossAlignSelf="start">`), a long string ListItem label (pass an element), and a table wider than the screen (the file cannot scroll it sideways: keep it within about 310 px with shares that match the floors or `pixel()` columns, each floor fitting its column's longest word and header, padding included). It also suggests `isWrapped`, which shows long CodeBlock lines whole. `astryx experimental render --help` and its doc now point to the guide.

Some controls in the app shell page templates did nothing when clicked. Now `shell-nav`'s Run project and Share, `shell-top-nav`'s Search products, Sign in and Checkout, and in `theme-showcase` the chat's Export, Close, Attach and Voice input buttons, Add item, the list and grid view buttons, and the inventory row menu's Edit, Duplicate and Move to each show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"). No layout or styling changes.

A horizontal `Slider` with labelled `marks` now keeps room for the labels: before, the labels hung below the slider's box and the content after it overlapped them; now that content starts below the labels. The labels take the supporting text's line height, so the room no longer depends on the surrounding text. Sliders without mark labels, and vertical sliders, keep their size.

Three page templates, not yet marked ready, for the screens every app needs when a page can't be shown: a not-found page with a search over the app's main destinations, an access-denied page that names the resource and the signed-in account with a request note, and an error page whose Try again reloads the page and whose connection check shows whether the browser is online. Actions an app must wire up (opening a destination, sending an access request, switching accounts, contacting support) show a demo message that says so.

In a Stepper's compact horizontal layout, a disabled Step now tells screen-reader users it is unavailable, with a hidden word after its label, as the expanded layout's disabled button already does. The new translated string is `@astryx.step.status.unavailable`; locales without it fall back to English.

The published CLI stores Core's component list and imports at publish, and uses them while the installed Core's files are unchanged, so `component --list` answers about 30 to 60 ms sooner in a project with no integrations. Another Core version, or a change to any Core file or folder the list reads, reads Core live, as before.

The published CLI reads its own shipped docs as already checked against their schema at publish, instead of checking each one on every read, so `docs` answers about 25 ms sooner. A doc that was edited or is not shipped is checked as before. Output is unchanged.

The published CLI stores search's catalog at publish, and uses it in a project that adds nothing to a catalog while the CLI's and Core's files are unchanged, so a machine's first `search` answers about 350 ms sooner and its first `build` about 290 ms sooner. The catalog is gathered live, as before, in a project with an integration, a package that adds docs or blocks, or a local theme; with another Core version; and after a change to any file or folder the catalog reads. Output is the same.

`astryx upgrade` rewrites the deprecated `swipeActions` and `swipeBehavior` props of `Item` and `ListItem` to `swipe={createSwipe(…)}` where each entry is an object literal. Each entry with no `id` takes one from its side and place, such as `'trailing-0'`, so the result compiles. It adds the `createSwipe` import. It reports, and leaves unchanged, a value whose entries it cannot see and a JSX spread it cannot rewrite.

Swipe actions on `Item` and `ListItem` come from one prop, `swipe`, whose value `createSwipe` makes, from `@astryxdesign/core/Swipe` or the package root: `swipe={createSwipe({leading, trailing, swipeBehavior})}`. Each action has an `id`, and its `onActivate` receives `{id, itemKey}`: the action's `id` and the `ListItem`'s `itemKey`. So one definition at module scope serves every row; one whose handlers need component state goes in `useMemo`. The swipe's type carries the ids, so an id it does not have fails to compile. A new value with the same ids keeps an open row open, and one with other ids closes it. The swipe's code comes with `createSwipe`, so a row given `swipe` is swipeable at its first paint, and an app that never imports it ships none of it. The `swipeActions` and `swipeBehavior` props and the `ItemSwipeAction` and `ItemSwipeActions` types are deprecated (DEP-0017) and are removed in the next minor release. `ItemSwipeActionVariant` and `ItemSwipeBehavior` stay, and the new API uses them. Until then the deprecated ones keep working, with the swipe behavior this release gives every row, and when `swipe` is set too, `swipe` wins. `astryx upgrade` rewrites static uses and gives each action an `id`.

Internal: the swipe hook's and the swipe layer's file headers keep only their tags and the SYNC reminder. The prose that explains each moves, unchanged, into the JSDoc of `useSwipeAction` and `SwipeActionsLayer`. No behavior or type changes, and neither is exported from the package entry point.

`astryx swizzle` without Core says what to do. Outside a project, it says the folder is outside a project and that swizzle copies source into an app project that installs `@astryxdesign/core`; in a project that has not installed Core, it says to install it. It no longer tells you to work inside the design system's own repository. The error code stays `ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND`.

With `useTableColumnsVirtualization`, a horizontal scroll that changes which columns are mounted now renders only the cells of the columns that enter. Before, every mounted cell of every mounted row ran its plugin transforms and rendered again. Each body cell is now its own memoized element, so cells whose inputs stay the same skip both. `useTableStickyColumns` now returns a new plugin object when its pinned keys change, so changing `startKeys` or `endKeys` at runtime pins and unpins body cells together with their header; before, body rows kept their old pinning until they rendered for another reason.

In a Table with sortable and resizable columns, a sortable column's resize line now sits on the column divider, like every other column's, in left-to-right and right-to-left layouts. Before, it sat one cell padding inside the column. A sortable header's right-click menu still opens at the pointer.

A table row that `useTableSelection` selects carries the `table-row` target's `selected` theme state, so a theme can style selected rows (`components: {'table-row': {selected: {…}}}`). The selection wash stays as it was; a theme recolors it by setting `--color-accent-muted` in that state.

The markdown tables in `astryx component <Name>`, `astryx hook <name>` and an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` use a three-dash rule under each header cell (`|---|---|`) instead of a rule as wide as the header text. Tables render the same in markdown.

The `table` page template now builds what its description promises: sortable columns, row selection into a bulk-action toolbar, and a per-row overflow menu, with a confirm step before removing members. It stays unlisted (`isReady: false`) for now.

`astryx template <name> <path>` and `astryx template --cdn <path>` accept an absolute path inside the project root, also through a symlinked project folder. It is written exactly as its relative path. An absolute path outside the project is still refused with `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`. For `astryx template <name> <path>`, the receipt says the path was written as its relative path (`data.givenPath` in `--json`), and the refusal names a command that writes inside the project and the command that prints the source without writing anything. In a Next app whose `pageExtensions` include `tsx` (the default), the named path is one Next builds and serves: a page goes to the App Router folder (`app/<name>`, or `src/app/<name>`, inside the route group with the root layout when that folder has none of its own), or, with only the Pages Router, to the page file `pages/<name>.tsx`; a block goes to `app/components/<name>` with a root `app/` folder, `components/<name>` with only a root `pages/` folder, else `src/components/<name>`. Every other project gets `src/pages/<name>` and `src/components/<name>`. When that path exists or another page already serves its URL, the name becomes `<name>-2`, `<name>-3` and so on. The path is quoted in the command when a shell would read it otherwise, as with a route group folder. Next refuses to build when its `app` and `pages` folders are in different folders, and when two pages serve one URL. For `--cdn`, the receipt is unchanged, and the refusal names `astryx template --cdn cdn.template.html`.

A page template's keyword now means one concept. When build chooses the start and its alternatives, a multi-word keyword counts only as the whole phrase (skipping stopwords and one-letter words inside it), so its single words no longer count for other templates. Core templates' keywords are migrated: lists of words are split into single keywords, terms that mean something different as a whole (such as "getting started" or "reading pane") stay phrases, and keywords that weren't true of their template are removed. The template-doc field reference says how to write keywords.

Four Core page templates no longer list keywords for things their page does not render, so `astryx build` and `astryx search` stop offering them for those ideas. AI Chat Conversation drops "citations", "reasoning" and "playground"; Kanban Board drops "swimlane" and "backlog"; Page Editor drops "drag and drop"; Theme Showcase drops "tokens", "palette" and "typography". The Page Editor and Theme Showcase descriptions now say what the page renders: blocks reorder with move up and move down, and the showcase shows sample product screens in the active theme.

`astryx template --list` prints the first sentence of each template's description, so the catalog is about a quarter shorter. `--json` keeps descriptions whole, and `astryx template <id> --skeleton` prints a template's whole description above its layout. The first-sentence rule that `astryx build` shares no longer ends a sentence at a period inside quotes, so a description quoting a date such as "2. Nov. 2026" reads whole there too.

`astryx template <name> <path>` writes a scratch copy to an absolute path in the system temp folder (`os.tmpdir()`, or `/tmp` on a POSIX system), such as `/tmp/dashboard`, instead of refusing it. The receipt names the folder by its whole path (`data.outputDir` in `--json`), and the checks of a write in the project apply: no link carries the copy out of the temp folder, and an existing file is replaced only with `--overwrite`. A temp folder that is a disk's root or holds the home folder is not used. Any other path outside the project is still refused with `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` gather the parts of each source file the template walks judge once per check, instead of walking the file's whole syntax tree again for every template that reaches it. For a package with many templates that share helpers, each check finished about 0.4 seconds sooner. Output does not change.

Action buttons that did nothing in four page templates now respond with a confirmation toast: Restock, Fulfill item, Create label, Refund and Send Invoice on the order detail page, the next-step action in the service-jobs detail panel, Dispute this line on the invoice line items page, and Format Document in the IDE workspace.

Action buttons and menu items that did nothing in eleven more page templates now respond with a toast that names the demo action: Add to Cart and Buy it now on the product detail page, Publish in the page editor, the sign-in, plan, export and connected-app actions in the settings dialog, Sign In, Google Pay, PayPal and the promo code's Apply on the payment form, Save & exit, Crop image and Preview on device in the vertical form wizard, the social sign-in buttons on both login pages, Share in the file explorer, the AI chat landing page's settings menu and composer, and Pin, Rename and Archive in the side-nav shell's conversation menu. On the work item page, Add subtask and each attachment's Edit name their demo action, Cancel clears the comment, and Comment confirms it and clears the field. The settings dialog's search-result chevron mirrors in right-to-left layouts.

The technical documentation page template now teaches the real setup. Its AI setup prompt no longer asks for a style compiler, which contradicted the article's own precompiled-CSS step, and its theming example uses the real `Theme` component from `@astryxdesign/core/theme` with a theme package instead of a `ThemeProvider` that Astryx does not export. Its prerequisites now name React 19 or later, which Core requires.

Three menu items in two page templates now respond instead of doing nothing. In the grouped issues table, "Edit issue" and "Duplicate" confirm with a demo toast. On the kanban board, "Assign to me" confirms with a demo toast. Each toast handler carries a comment that marks where to connect the real action.

Page templates now have no horizontal overflow on a 390 px phone, with touch or a mouse. In the service-health, data, funnel-and-cohort and program-status dashboards and the kanban board, the header controls now wrap onto a second row instead of widening the page past the screen edge, and on the data dashboard a section heading's hint is no longer squeezed into a narrow column beside the heading. Desktop layouts are unchanged. A check builds every ready page template into an app and runs it in a 390 px phone emulation, with touch and with a mouse, so a template that widens the page past a phone's screen fails before release.

A page whose components bring no tooltip code, such as one that renders only `Text` and `Heading`, loads about 9.6 KB less JavaScript before first paint (about 3.4 KB gzip). The truncation tooltip's tap handling no longer shares a file with the touch trigger code that its lazily loaded tooltip uses, so that code stays with the tooltip. Tapping a truncated text opens its tooltip as before.

`theme add` and `theme use` wire a theme with one color mode in that mode. When a theme's built module exports `colorModes` (`["light"]` or `["dark"]`; `theme build` writes it when the theme source exports it), the `theme.app` receipt gives that theme a `mode` field and the generated theme module lists it in a `themeModes` export. The first import's wiring passes `mode={themeModes[defaultThemeSlug] ?? 'system'}` to `Theme`, so the selected theme shows its own mode and a theme with both modes follows the system. When a later `theme add` or `theme use` first adds `themeModes` to an app that is already wired, the receipt marks `change.wireModes` and prints the wiring line to use. Once the module has exported `themeModes`, it keeps the export (empty when no theme has one mode), so the wiring keeps compiling after `theme remove`. The mode is read from the file that declares the theme, so a theme module that re-exports the built module (whole or by name) carries it. A project whose themes all have both modes gets the same receipt, module and wiring as before.

`astryx theme build`: a theme module that throws from a microtask it queues while it loads is a refused load (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`), not a crash; a listener a theme module adds to `process` (`process.on('exit', …)`, `beforeExit`) goes with its load, so it no longer sets the command's exit code, prints after the `--json` envelope, or keeps the command from ending. `--out` naming a stylesheet's source map (`p.css.map`) is refused, and a slip after `.css` (`p.css.bak`) is told the stylesheet name meant (`p.css`, not `p.css.css`).
changesets.body: `astryx experimental theme compile` refuses a theme whose own values throw when read (a `tokens` getter or Proxy) as the build does, with no stack trace or `ERR_UNKNOWN`.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build`:
changesets.body:
- A plain-object theme (`export default {name, tokens}`) goes through `defineTheme` as a `defineTheme(…)` call does: a `[light, dark]` pair is written as `light-dark()`, and Core's media-surface rules are written. One with `extends` and no tokens builds as the empty theme over its base.
- A spread of a package theme (`{...neutralTheme, name}`) is refused naming the spread and the form that builds (`extends: neutralTheme`), not an `icons` field the file does not set.
- A stylesheet the theme source imports (`import './brand.css'`) is named in a warning: the built outputs do not carry it, so the app imports it.
- What a theme module changes while it loads in `console`, a global (`Buffer`) or the file mode mask is put back when the load ends, so the command prints its result and writes readable files.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` names an import through a path alias (`@/lib/c`, `~/lib/c`) as one the theme loader does not map, never as a package to install; expands a quoted glob to the theme sources it matches in its suggestion; and counts the fonts macOS and Windows ship, from one table by platform, as system fonts in its note on fonts named but not loaded.

`astryx theme build` refuses a blank or whitespace-only `--out` (it wrote files named by the spaces alone), and its note on fonts named but not loaded leaves out the families a local theme's own font stylesheet loads (`<slug>.fonts.css` beside the source, the stylesheet `theme add` imports). `astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` also treat Segoe UI Light, Semilight, Semibold and Black as system fonts, the faces Windows installs as families of their own, so neither reports them as not loaded.

`astryx theme build` counts the fonts macOS and Windows ship for Chinese, Japanese and Korean (such as PingFang SC, Hiragino Sans, Microsoft YaHei and 微软雅黑) as system fonts, so it no longer names them as fonts the theme does not load.

`astryx theme build` of a theme with a local TypeScript or JSX module, such as an icon registry, finishes about 200 ms sooner when the module has not changed since the last build. The JavaScript it compiles from the module is kept beside the kept gathers and read back while the source, the compile options, the imports it rewrites and every file of the Babel that compiled it are unchanged, so such a build loads neither `@babel/core` nor its TypeScript and JSX plugins. A first build, and a build after an edit to the module, compile as before. The written files do not change.

`astryx theme build` of a theme whose part styles hold pseudo-class keys (`':hover'`, `'::before'`) or whose tokens hold names without two dashes finishes about 20 to 30 ms sooner on a repeat build. What its css-tree checks of those keys and names find is kept beside the kept gathers and read back while the keys and every file of css-tree's code and data are unchanged, so such a build loads no css-tree. The build's warnings, errors and written files do not change.

`astryx theme build` reads a font family name as CSS reads it (`Gill\ Sans` is Gill Sans), names as not loaded a family the theme holds in its own property and reads with `var()`, and builds a theme bound with `let` or `var` that is never assigned again as it builds a `const` (one assigned again is refused naming that, not as an icon registry it sets).

`astryx theme build`: a doc module given as the theme (`oceanTheme.doc.mjs`, or a file whose default export is a doc such as `{type: 'theme', name, description}`) is refused with `ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming it as a doc and the theme source beside it to build, and nothing is written.

`theme build` reads each Core component doc at most once per run. A theme whose component overrides name prop values (such as `variant:ghost` or `size:sm`) was checked against up to three views of Core's docs (the theming targets, the known prop values, and the components a new value augments), and each view read and checked every doc again. Such a build now finishes about 50 to 110 ms sooner. A theme with no such overrides reads the docs once, as before. Output does not change.

`theme build` of a missing file in a folder whose files another command generates (their first comment says which command writes them) says the file is generated and names that command, instead of offering a blank theme template. `doctor` still compares such a local theme's outputs with its source, and its fix for a stale or missing one runs the exact command that writes it, never a `theme build`. `doctor`'s fix when the themes folder cannot be read names the theme the message names (for a generated one, its command), never `<slug>`. A font stylesheet's local `@import` (a file beside it, `url(faces.css)`, or a package stylesheet such as `@fontsource/inter/index.css`, resolved from where the stylesheet really is) is followed and its fonts proven; a URL import is an external font service, and a local import doctor cannot follow, or one past the files it follows, is a warning, never a failure. The help and docs say `editor show <name> --png` takes pictures of real components.

`astryx theme build`: building a theme the theme editor made now also says that the build does not write (or, with `--check`, does not check) the theme's app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/`, which the app imports, and names the `astryx experimental theme compile` command that builds the theme and writes the copy.

`astryx theme build`: a plain-object theme with no `tokens`, a name alone (`export default {name: 'p'}`) or a name and component styles, builds as an empty theme over the base instead of ending with "Cannot convert undefined or null to object".

In a project where an integration can load, `theme build` keeps what it checks a theme against in Core's component docs between runs, while every doc and folder they were worked out from is unchanged. It works them out before it reads the theme, so they do not depend on the theme: building a theme again, with or without an edit to it, finishes about 120 to 150 ms sooner. A Core-only project keeps nothing and works out only what a build needs, as before. `doctor`'s row for the per-user cache names the new entry; output does not change otherwise.

`themeBuildFamily` (`astryx theme build --family`) builds each member as it is at that build. Before, a second family build in the same process, such as a tool or a test that builds in process, built a member file changed since the first build from the module the first build had loaded.

`astryx theme build`: its font notices name the typography recipe, written with the project's own runner in text output, and it compares real paths in the disk's own case, so a theme reached through a differently cased path is not reported as missing or as another file.
`astryx theme build` (and `astryx experimental theme compile`, which builds the same way):
changesets.body:
- A theme that gives null for a part or a style key's block is refused at the line that gives it, never a crash. A null property or token value keeps its meaning (it is written as it is) and is warned at its line.
- A style key no element carries is warned: a value a closed prop never takes (`size:xxl` on Button, which takes sm, md and lg) and a pseudo-class written as a style key (`':hover'`, which goes inside one: `base: {':hover': …}`).
- A named pipe, a device or a socket where an output or `--out` goes is refused at once, never opened.
- `--out out/.css` is told to give the stylesheet a name. An `--out` that starts with an unexpanded `~` is warned: the build writes in the project's `~` folder, as before, and the warning names that folder and the home folder path to give instead.
- A theme with no name is refused as one, at its line.
- Apple Color Emoji and Noto Color Emoji count as the systems' own fonts.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the form that works, more part keys a browser drops or Core misreads: a vendor property written without its dash, a pseudo name in capitals, something after a pseudo-element, two pseudo-elements, an escaped pseudo name, the custom property `--`, an empty key, and a block under a key that nests none. The output is the same as before. A `--family` build with such a key in a member builds, with each warning naming the member's file, where it stopped on an unknown error before. A default export that is a Promise of a theme is named as one, instead of a theme without a name.
`astryx theme build`: a family build names a file it replaces, and builds that would not load say so.
changesets.body:
- A family build over a file with no build header at the `--family-key` name (an output of a CLI before 0.6.7, or a file of your own) still replaces it, now with a warning naming the file. Another theme's outputs there are replaced with a warning naming that theme.
- A family member whose icon registry is imported without its extension (`import {icons} from './icons'`) builds, as it does on its own.
- An icon registry that imports an asset (`import check from './check.svg'`, a `.png`, a font) builds; the asset loads as its URL, as a bundler gives it.
- With `--out` in another folder, a relative icon registry import that nothing answers to from there is warned, with the `--icons-specifier` that names the registry from there.
- A theme file that exports two named themes and no default warns which theme it builds and which it leaves out.
- An empty or blank `--icons-specifier` is warned (the built module would import from `""`); `astryx experimental theme compile` refuses it, and an empty or blank `--out`, before building. `theme build --out ''` still writes beside the source.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, more values a browser drops: a part property that builds dash-first without a vendor prefix (`Color`), a token or part value that is no text (an object, a boolean, NaN, an array in a part), a [light, dark] pair with a missing half or another count, a token that reads itself, and a token's `var()` that no token sets. A pseudo-class after a pseudo-element that takes one (`::file-selector-button:hover`) is no longer warned, and only `:hover` and `:active` in capitals are. A warning about a value the theme takes from the theme it extends no longer gives a line of the file that extends it, and a `--family` build names it once, at the member that writes it. A tokens map spread from a defined theme's tokens no longer trips over Core's own private copies in it.

`astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, custom properties that read each other (a token with a fallback reading itself, two tokens, a half of a [light, dark] pair, tokens and local tokens, a part's own custom property), a pseudo-element near a known one (as that one misspelled), a pseudo-element missing from the CLI's selector data (as possibly newer than the CLI), a pseudo-element inside `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` or `:has()`, a pseudo-class after `::highlight()`, `:window-inactive` after any highlight but `::selection`, a token name that does not start with exactly two dashes, and an empty token value. A pseudo-class after `::search-text` or `::scroll-marker-group` is no longer warned. A child theme's own build names the file and line of a value the theme it extends writes. A null value's warning says what it builds: a null property leaves the base theme's value, while a null token is kept by the browser as the token's value, so most properties that read it act as if they were not set (text keeps the surrounding color, a background goes transparent) and a font family reading it falls back to the browser's default font.
`astryx theme build`: a theme file is read for its theme, and nothing it does while loading breaks the command.
changesets.body:
- A Sass, Less, Stylus or PostCSS stylesheet a theme module imports loads as an empty module, as a `.css` import does.
- An import that the project's tsconfig `paths` or `baseUrl` maps (`@app/c`, `lib/c`) is named as a path alias, never offered as a package to install.
- With `--out` naming another stylesheet, the built module's usage comment names the stylesheet written.
- When a build of several files stops at a failure, the error says which outputs the files before it wrote, in text and `--json` alike.
- A default export that holds themes (`export default {light, dark}`) is named as such.
- A theme module that calls `process.exit` while loading is refused by name; `--check` never passes without its verdict.
- A value a theme module throws that is not an Error is shown as it is.
- What a theme module prints goes to stderr, so `--json` output stays valid.
- A timer a theme module leaves running no longer keeps `theme build` or `--check` from exiting.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` reads `var()` in any letter case when it warns about a token that reads itself, tokens that read each other, or a `var()` no token sets, and it follows a loop through the token definitions Core sets on the theme's root (`--font-size-2xl: var(--text-heading-1-size)`). A misspelled pseudo-class (`:hovr`) is warned with the one it is near. The output is the same as before.
`astryx theme build`: a theme file is read for its theme, and what its code leaves behind no longer decides the command.
changesets.body:
- A family build over a file at the `--family-key` name lists the replace warning in `--json` too, as the text does.
- A `process.exitCode` a theme module sets is not the command's exit code.
- A theme module importing a `.postcss`, `.stylus` or `.sss` stylesheet loads it as an empty module.
- What a theme module prints after it loaded (a deferred log) goes to stderr, so `--json` stays valid.
- A theme module whose top-level await never settles is refused (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming the file), not ended by Node with exit 13.
- A theme source may import the stylesheet its own build writes, which a first build from a clean checkout now writes; a missing stylesheet it does not write is refused by name.
- Every handle a theme module opens (a timer from `node:timers`, a file watcher, a server, a message port) is let go once it is loaded, so the command exits.
- A promise a theme module leaves rejecting is a warning on stderr, not a crash after the result.
- `astryx experimental theme compile` names a value a theme two `extends` up refuses in the file and line that hold it.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build`: what a theme module leaves running no longer decides the command, and three source layouts build.
changesets.body:
- A callback a theme module leaves running that calls `process.exit` after the module loaded is ignored with a warning; one that sets `process.exitCode` does not set the command's; one that throws is a warning, not a crash after the result.
- A family root may import the family's own stylesheet (`import './k.css'` for `--family-key k`), and a source its own stylesheet with a query (`import './p.css?inline'`): a first build from a clean checkout writes it.
- A project in a folder whose name holds `#`, `?` or `%20` builds a theme that imports a stylesheet.
