- What a theme module changes for the whole process while it loads (the working folder, a built-in object such as `JSON` or `Object.prototype`) is put back when the load ends.
- `--out` naming a TypeScript declaration file (`p.css.d.ts`) is refused with the stylesheet name to give, instead of writing CSS into it.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, a field `defineTheme()` does not take (`component:`, `tokenz:`, `ondark:`, `onDark.localTokens`, `typography.body.fontFamily`), with the field it is near; and a BigInt, a function or a Date value, naming what it writes. A BigInt no longer ends the build with an unknown error. A surface token that loops through a token Core sets on that surface is warned once, at its line, and Core's own surface token is no longer named as one from the theme it extends.

`astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field wherever the theme's sources write its input: an input held in a const, `defineTheme` imported under another name, a theme a file re-exports from another module (named with that module's file and line), and an `onDark`, `onLight` or `typography` block held in a const; a method written as a field (`onLoad() {}`) is warned too, and so is a BigInt typography value. A TypeScript type assertion such as `<any>1` in a `.ts` theme no longer costs every warning its line. A BigInt inside a part's array or nested block no longer ends the build: it is warned by what is written, and a value that holds itself stops the build at its line. A symbol, or a tokens object that holds itself, stops the build at its line instead of with a raw error. A boxed string (`new String('4px')`) is judged by what is written: no warning as a token or a pair half.

`astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field that reaches the theme input through a spread (`{...shared}`, `onDark: {...dark}`, an imported object), or in a theme the file imports and then exports, at the line that writes it; a BigInt typography value held in a const is named too; and a `[light, dark]` pair whose half is empty or a number, which `light-dark()` does not take, so the browser drops the value. A boxed primitive in a part (`padding: new String('4px')`) is written as its text, as a token's is, instead of as JSON text with its quotes.

`astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` no longer warn that a theme's font does not load for Noto Sans, Noto Serif and Noto Sans Mono (system fonts of Android, ChromeOS and Linux) or Cantarell, Ubuntu and Ubuntu Mono (system fonts of Linux). A system font stack that names them needs no font package.

`astryx theme build`: the import hint is given only for a load failure that is an unresolved import, and `@fontsource-variable/<name>` is read as loading `<Name> Variable`, the family that package declares, not `<Name>`.

`astryx theme build` now writes a built theme module that loads in any bundler and in plain Node. A local module the built module imports (an icon registry, a component icon slot value, or the helpers they import) that is TypeScript or JSX is compiled to JavaScript named after its source (`icons.tsx` → `icons.tsx.js`) in a folder beside the built module named for it (`w98.modules` beside `w98.js`, whatever `--out` names the stylesheet), at the place each source has under the folder that holds the theme and its compiled sources, so every compiled module has a path of its own: `import { icons } from './icons'` with `icons.tsx` beside the theme becomes `import { icons } from './w98.modules/icons.tsx.js'`, and a helper it imports becomes `w98.modules/helper.ts.js`. Each local import names its file with its extension. Before, the built module kept the TypeScript import, so an app whose bundler does not compile TypeScript from `node_modules` (a plain Next.js app) failed to build after it added the theme. The compiled modules carry the build header, `--check` compares them, and a file of your own at a compiled module's path is never replaced (that import stays as written, with a warning saying so). A theme with no local module writes the same outputs as before; package imports stay as they are. `--family` builds compile each member's TypeScript registry the same way, in a folder named for the family key.

`astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the form that works, a part key it cannot write as intended: a pseudo key that leaves a parenthesis, bracket, quote or comment open (a browser then drops the rules after it), a pseudo key that is no selector, a selector list such as `':hover, :focus'` (only its first member is scoped to the part), and a custom property with capitals (written in kebab case, so `var()` of the name as written reads nothing). The output is the same as before. A missing input near a theme source in the same folder (a missing extension, a one-letter slip) is offered that source.

An import written as a template literal with nothing put in it (``import(`./icons.ts`)``) is read as the string it holds by these commands: `astryx theme build --watch` follows it, the built theme module carries it, `astryx doctor`'s shipped-import check judges it, and `astryx template` lists a package imported that way in its install line when the project lacks it. Before, such an import was skipped.

`theme build` keeps the transpiled code of the theme sources it loads in the transpile cache the CLI already uses for integration manifests and TypeScript docs, so a build of an unchanged theme no longer transpiles it again: about 150 ms faster per build. An edited theme is transpiled again. On systems with user ids, that cache is the per-user one, which now stays within the same size limit as the kept catalogs: once it has grown, a run removes its least recently used transpiled copies, never one written in the last day or read in the last day where the file system records reads. `doctor`'s "Kept catalog cache" row now names that limit. Other output does not change.

`astryx theme build --json` carries in its `warnings` the `--out` warnings the text run prints (a stylesheet name that is not .css, an output of another theme source it replaces, a folder the theme editor made), names a folder it cannot write with its fix instead of a temporary file's error, and names an `extends` written as a helper's call or a conditional as what it cannot follow instead of an inline icon registry. Its note on fonts named but not loaded also names the families of a component's `font` shorthand (`font: '600 14px Lora, serif'`).
changesets.body: [fix] `astryx theme build`'s full font help leaves out, family by family, each family the theme's own `<slug>.fonts.css` loads; before, it printed the whole list unless every family was loaded.

changesets.headline: A theme's component overrides can hold `@light` and `@dark` blocks: properties, pseudo-class overrides and pseudo-elements that apply only where the element's color mode is that mode, as `Theme` resolves it from its own `mode`, the system preference, or a `MediaTheme` surface. Inside media surfaces the nearest surface decides, for up to five surfaces of alternating modes nested one in another, so a light `MediaTheme` inside a dark one (a toast over a dark surface) takes only the light block. Where no enclosing mode matches, the block writes nothing, so every other rule applies there as it would without it, and it can be any value, not only a color. Themes without these blocks compile to the same CSS.

`astryx experimental theme` reads its cached part data once per change of the cache file instead of parsing it again for every command in a process. The per-user cache of transpiled TypeScript is not read again when it has grown until its oldest copy could be removed, so a large cache no longer slows every theme command's first load.

`astryx experimental theme editor undo` refuses a `themes` that is a file, not a folder, by name on Node 22.13 too ("themes in this app is a file, not a folder …", with `ls -la themes` to see what is there). Before, on the CLI's oldest supported Node, it stopped with a raw "ENOTDIR: not a directory" error instead.

A theme that styles `link` keeps Core's hover tint on a link's color: the rules that hold each link `color` prop's color now hold, on hover, Core's tint of that color, so a link setting of any kind (a color for one mode, or any theme link color) no longer removes the hover tint in that mode. A theme's own hover color for a link color key still wins over the tint.

`astryx theme list` names, for each theme, the owner the app imports it from and whether that owner is installed (`owner`, `installed`). The CLI ships a bundled theme's descriptor and source (for `theme eject`), not the built output the app imports: `theme add` records and the app imports that from the theme's own package (such as `@astryxdesign/theme-neutral`), and refuses to add it until that package is installed; the list now says so instead of naming only the CLI. Existing fields are unchanged.
Skeleton placeholders show on the light page: `--color-skeleton` takes a darker neutral stop, so the placeholder reads at its pulse peak against the page and every surface.

The Theming section of `astryx component <Name>` (and of an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>`) prints its `defineTheme` override example, and its standard-CSS example, on one line each instead of a multi-line code block. The same keys and comments appear; `--json` is unchanged.

`astryx experimental theme preview add <description>` adds a page only when build is sure of its start. When build starts from the app shell, or from a page its page pick gives less than a clear fit (`start.fit` under build's `CLEAR_FIT`), it refuses, says why, and offers the nearest pages this app can show by name (`--template <id>`), then the list of every page. A description that names a page by its id or display name, names an app the preview has pages for, or names a page build's ranking matches by its name or a keyword, still adds it.

`astryx theme remove --help` states its exit codes plainly: removing the only added theme exits 0, removes the generated module and prints the lines the app root must drop; removing the default fails only while other themes are still added, and the line says to choose another default with `theme use` first. Agents read the old line, "is the default while other themes are added", as "the default can never be removed" and added a theme nobody asked for.

`astryx theme remove` can remove the only added theme. Before, it refused and said to add another theme and make it the default first, so removing a theme left the app on a theme nobody chose. Now it deletes the generated theme module when the module is exactly what the CLI wrote, and prints the module import and the `Theme` wrapper the app root must drop. A module with changes the CLI did not write stays, and the command says how to finish by hand. Removing the default while other themes are added still asks for `theme use` first. In `--json`, the `theme.app` result of that removal has no themes, an empty `default`, and `change.moduleRemoved: true` (and `change.themeModes: true` when the deleted module exported `themeModes`).

`theme build` (with or without `--check` or `--family`), `integration verify` and `doctor` load a theme that extends a base theme whose module imports its own stylesheet, such as a package's `./themes/<slug>` entry that loads the theme's CSS. Node stopped on that import with `Unknown file extension ".css"`. On Node 22.15 and later, a stylesheet that any module of the theme imports now loads as an empty module. Node resolves each stylesheet import from the module that writes it, so a missing stylesheet still fails. On Node 22.13 and 22.14 nothing changes: a theme build (`theme build`, `integration verify`, `doctor`'s freshness check) still stops on any stylesheet import, and a read of a built theme module (`doctor`, `component`) still loads only a stylesheet whose import resolves from that module's folder.
`astryx theme template` lists the `'@light'` and `'@dark'` block form among a component's style keys, with a commented example: a block that applies only in that color mode.
Skeleton placeholders show on the light page: `--color-skeleton` takes a darker neutral stop, so the placeholder reads at its pulse peak against the page and every surface.
Tokenizer shows the caret in a focused, empty input when the field has no width

The tool page templates now give their dead buttons and menu items a behavior: in `canvas-editor`, `file-explorer`, `ide`, `kanban-board` and `editor`, the toolbar buttons, menu items and view switch that did nothing now either work or show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), and toasts that claimed an action had happened now say it would happen. Text fields, form inputs and some menus are not part of this change. In right-to-left layouts, canvas-editor's Undo and Redo arrows now mirror. No other layout or styling changes.

Tooltip paints the theme's inverted surface (`--color-background-inverted`), the surface Toast paints, instead of the primary text color, so a theme that sets its inverted surface styles tooltips and toasts alike. Its text stays the page surface color. To keep the previous look, a theme can set the `tooltip` target's `backgroundColor` to `var(--color-text-primary)`.
On a phone, TopNav's compact bar keeps a plain-text heading on one line and ends it in an ellipsis, so a long title no longer wraps and makes the bar taller.
Typeahead and Tokenizer: when a search matches more items than `maxMenuItems` shows, the result count announced to screen readers names every match, not only the rows shown.

Internal: the UIKit values of a swipe-action row (the swipe threshold, the springs a confirmed row runs ahead on and a released row settles with, the touch claim distance the web needs) and the release rule that picks closed, open or fire (a fast release goes the way it moves, a slow one by where it is, and only a confirmed full swipe fires), checked against releases measured on UIKit. Not exported from the package entry point.

`astryx upgrade --list` prints each codemod on one line, its name and title, under its version, with `(optional)` on the codemods that run only on request and the package named once when every codemod shares it, instead of a five-line record per codemod. The list now grows by one line per new codemod, plus a heading when a codemod starts a new version. `--json` is unchanged.

`astryx upgrade` reads a `.ts` file as TypeScript without JSX and a declaration file as declarations, as TypeScript does. A type assertion (`<Item>value`) in a `.ts` file, or a declaration without a value (`export const limit: number;`) in a declaration file (`.d.ts`, `.d.mts`, `.d.cts`, or an arbitrary-extension declaration file such as `styles.d.css.ts`), no longer stops the run with a parse error, and a codemod changes such a file like any other. A `.tsx` file and JavaScript read as before.

The useHotkeys docs no longer recommend `shift+/` for a help overlay. The hook compares the final key against `event.key`, and Shift+/ produces `?` on US layouts, so a `shift+/` registration never fires there. The docs now use `?` and say to register a punctuation key that shift changes as the character it produces. No behavior changes.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` parse each of a package's source files once for the walks that follow each template's imports, instead of once for every template that reaches the file. For a package with many templates that share helpers, each check finishes about a second sooner. Output does not change.
